citations.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, $\mu$, $\chi_k$ and the
spaces $H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ be as in
[[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]] ($m\ge1$).

**(a) Mode sets.** For $N\ge0$ put
$\Lambda_N:=\{k\in\mathbb Z^3:|k|\le N\}$ with $|k|$ the Euclidean norm, and
$$X_N:=\Bigl\{\sum_{k\in\Lambda_N}a_k\chi_k:\ a_k\in\mathbb C^m,\ a_{-k}=\overline{a_k}\Bigr\}\subseteq C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m),$$
the **Galerkin space of modes up to $N$**; it is a finite-dimensional real
vector space of dimension $d_N:=m\,|\Lambda_N|$, and $X_N\subseteq X_{N'}$ for
$N\le N'$. (The reality condition $a_{-k}=\overline{a_k}$ is exactly the
condition that the trigonometric polynomial be real-valued.)

**(b) Projection.** For $u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ define
$$P_Nu:=\sum_{k\in\Lambda_N}\widehat u(k)\chi_k,\qquad (P_Nu)(x)=\sum_{k\in\Lambda_N}\widehat u(k)\chi_k(x),$$
with $\widehat u(k)$ the Fourier coefficients of clause (c) of
[[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]]; the second expression is a finite
sum, so $P_Nu\in X_N$; and $P_N:X_N\to X_N$ is the identity.
$P_N$ is called the **Galerkin (Fourier) projection**.

The definition fixes the projection only. Its self-adjointness,
derivative-commutation and operator-norm properties are proved in
[[lem-gr-galerkin-projection-properties]].

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $m\ge1$, $N\ge0$, and let $P_N$ be the Galerkin
projection and $X_N$ the Galerkin space of [[def-gr-galerkin-fourier-projection]]
on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$. Then:

**(a)** $P_N$ is linear on $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$, self-adjoint
($\langle P_Nu,v\rangle_2=\langle u,P_Nv\rangle_2$ for all $u,v\in L^2$) and
idempotent ($P_N^2=P_N$), with range $X_N$ and kernel the classes with vanishing
coefficients on $\Lambda_N$;

**(b)** for every multi-index $\alpha$ with $|\alpha|\le s$ and every
$u\in H^s$, $P_ND^\alpha u=D^\alpha P_Nu$;

**(c)** for every $0\le r\le s$ and every $u\in H^r$,
$\|P_Nu\|_{H^r}\le\|u\|_{H^r}$;

**(d)** for every $0\le r\le s$ and every $u\in H^r$, $P_Nu\to u$ in $H^r$ as
$N\to\infty$;

**(e)** for every $s\ge1$, every $u\in H^s$ and every $N\ge0$,
$$\|u-P_Nu\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C_s\,(1+N^2)^{-1/2}\,\|u\|_{H^s}$$
with $C_s$ depending only on $s$.

Let $m\ge1$ and let $B\in\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$ be positive definite,
that is $B^{\mathsf T}=B$ and $z^{\mathsf T}Bz>0$ for every nonzero
$z\in\mathbb R^m$ with the standard coordinate inner product.

**(a)** There are real numbers $0<a\le b$ with $a\,|z|^2\le z^{\mathsf T}Bz\le b\,|z|^2$
for every $z\in\mathbb R^m$; equivalently $aI\le B\le bI$ in the Loewner
order. They can be taken to be the least and largest eigenvalues of $B$.

**(b)** $B$ is invertible and $\tfrac1bI\le B^{-1}\le\tfrac1aI$, so in
particular $\|B^{-1}z\|\le a^{-1}\|z\|$.

**(c)** Let $\Lambda$ be a compact topological space and let
$B:\Lambda\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$ be continuous with $B(\lambda)$
positive definite for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$. Then there are constants
$0<a\le b$ with $aI\le B(\lambda)\le bI$ for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$.

**(d)** Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^p$ be open and let $B:D\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$
be smooth with $B(x)\ge aI$ for a constant $a>0$ and all $x\in D$. Then
$x\mapsto B(x)^{-1}$ is smooth on $D$ and $B(x)^{-1}\le a^{-1}I$ there.

Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^n$ be open, let $F:D\to\mathbb R^n$ be continuous and locally Lipschitz in the state variable, and let $(t_0,x_0)\in D$. Then a unique local solution of the IVP exists on some interval around the initial time. More quantitatively, if $h,r>0$ make

$$[t_0-h,t_0+h]\times\overline B(x_0,r)\subseteq D,$$

if $\|F\|_2\le M$ and $F$ has state-Lipschitz constant $L$ on this cylinder, and if $hM\le r$ and $Lh<1$, then there is exactly one solution on $[t_0-h,t_0+h]$ through $(t_0,x_0)$ whose graph lies in the cylinder. Any two solutions through the same initial data agree on every common subinterval containing $t_0$.

In particular, a unique local solution exists on an interval around the initial time.

Let $F(t,x,\lambda)$ be jointly $C^\infty$ in $(t,x,\lambda)$ on an open time-state-parameter
domain. Near any base data $(t_0,x_0,\lambda_0)$ there are a compact time
interval $I$ and a neighbourhood $W$ of $(x_0,\lambda_0)$ such that, for every
$(y,\lambda)\in W$, the solution of

$$x'(t)=F(t,x(t),\lambda),\qquad x(t_0)=y,$$

is defined on $I$, and the resulting solution map is smooth in the pair
$(y,\lambda)$.

Let $k\in\mathbb N$, let $m,q\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, and let $f:U\to\mathbb R^q$. A map $f:U\to\mathbb R^q$ is of class $C^k$ when each component is of class $C^k$. Each scalar component uses the word-derivative convention of [[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]], whose source dimension is positive. The map is **smooth**, or $C^\infty$, when it is $C^k$ for every $k\in\mathbb N$.

Let $n\ge1$ and let $U,V\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open. A bijection $f:U\to V$ is a **$C^k$ diffeomorphism** when both $f$ and $f^{-1}$ are $C^k$. For $k\ge1$, a **local $C^k$ diffeomorphism at $a\in U$** is a restriction $f|_P:P\to Q$ between open neighbourhoods of $a$ and $f(a)$ that is a $C^k$ diffeomorphism. At $k=1$ this agrees with [[def-c-one-map-and-local-inverse]]: continuous first partial derivatives give the required total derivative by [[thm-continuous-partial-derivatives-imply-total-differentiability]], while continuity of the total derivative gives continuity of its matrix entries and hence of the first partial derivatives.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, $k:=s-1\ge4$, let
$O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval, let
$F:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\mathbb R^{m'}$ and
$A:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to M_{m'}(\mathbb R)$ be smooth, let
$K\subseteq O$ be compact and let $R\ge0$. Then there is
$C=C(F,A,s,m,m',K,R)$ such that for every $u:I\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$
with $u(t)(x)\in K$ and $\|u(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$ for all $t$, the following hold,
where compositions use the continuous representatives of
[[lem-gr-periodic-sobolev-embedding]]:

**(a)** for every integer $0\le r\le s$, $\|F(t,\cdot,u(t))\|_{H^r}\le C\,(1+\|u(t)\|_{H^s})$;

**(b)** if $C_1\subseteq O$ is compact and convex, $u,v$ take values in $C_1$
and $\|v(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$, then
$$\|F(t,\cdot,u(t))-F(t,\cdot,v(t))\|_{H^k}\le C\,\|u(t)-v(t)\|_{H^k};$$

**(c)** for every $1\le|\alpha|\le k$ and every $w\in H^{|\alpha|-1}$,
$$\bigl\|D^\alpha\bigl(A(t,\cdot,u(t))\,w\bigr)-A(t,\cdot,u(t))\,D^\alpha w\bigr\|_2\le C\,\bigl(1+\|w\|_{H^{|\alpha|-1}}\bigr);$$

**(d)** for every $0\le j\le k$ and every $w\in H^j$, $\|A(t,\cdot,u(t))\,w\|_{H^j}\le C\,\|w\|_{H^j}$.

Let $k\in\mathbb N$, let $m,q\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, and let $f:U\to\mathbb R^q$. A map $f:U\to\mathbb R^q$ is of class $C^k$ when each component is of class $C^k$. Each scalar component uses the word-derivative convention of [[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]], whose source dimension is positive. The map is **smooth**, or $C^\infty$, when it is $C^k$ for every $k\in\mathbb N$.

Let $n\ge1$ and let $U,V\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open. A bijection $f:U\to V$ is a **$C^k$ diffeomorphism** when both $f$ and $f^{-1}$ are $C^k$. For $k\ge1$, a **local $C^k$ diffeomorphism at $a\in U$** is a restriction $f|_P:P\to Q$ between open neighbourhoods of $a$ and $f(a)$ that is a $C^k$ diffeomorphism. At $k=1$ this agrees with [[def-c-one-map-and-local-inverse]]: continuous first partial derivatives give the required total derivative by [[thm-continuous-partial-derivatives-imply-total-differentiability]], while continuity of the total derivative gives continuity of its matrix entries and hence of the first partial derivatives.

derivations.claim: (The finite-dimensional form of the Galerkin system.) Fix a basis of $X_N$ and let $\pi:\mathbb R^{d_N}\to X_N$ be the coordinate isomorphism. Define $V:=\{z\in\mathbb R^{d_N}:\pi(z)(x)\in O\ \forall x\}$, an open set containing the coordinates of $P_Nu_0$, and for $z\in V$ and $v\in X_N$ define $M(t,z)v:=P_N[A^0(t,\cdot,\pi(z))\,v]$. For $v\ne0$, self-adjointness [L1] gives $\langle v,M(t,z)v\rangle_{L^2}=\int v^{\mathsf T}A^0(t,\cdot,\pi(z))v\,d\mu\ge a_z\|v\|_2^2$ with $a_z>0$ by [L2] applied to a compact set containing the values of $\pi(z)$; on compact subsets of $V$ the bound is uniform, so $M(t,z)$ is invertible with smooth inverse there by [[lem-gr-positive-definite-symmetric-matrix-bounds]] clause (d). Define $G(t,z):=M(t,z)^{-1}\bigl(-P_N[\sum_iA^i(t,\cdot,\pi(z))\partial_i\pi(z)+B(t,\cdot,\pi(z))]\bigr)$, which is smooth in $(t,z)$ on $I\times V$ by [L4] and the smoothness of the inverse; then $u_N(t)=\pi(z(t))$ solves the Galerkin system iff $z'(t)=G(t,z(t))$, and $z(0)$ is the coordinate of $P_Nu_0$.

(Local existence and smooth dependence (a), (c).) Since $G$ is continuous and locally Lipschitz on the open set $I\times V$ and the initial point lies in it, Picard--Lindelöf [L3] gives a unique local solution through the initial point, defined on an open interval $J_N\ni0$; smoothness of $G$ and the smooth-dependence theorem [L3] give the smooth finite-dimensional flow, hence (c), and (a) follows by transporting through $\pi$.

(Continuation criterion (b).) Suppose the maximal forward interval is $[0,T_*)$ with $T_*<\infty$ and the trajectory remains in a compact $C_1\subseteq V$ for $t\in[0,T_*)$. The set $K_1:=\{u\in X_N:u\text{ takes values in }C\}$ is compact, being closed and bounded in the finite-dimensional space $X_N$, and $\pi^{-1}(K_1)$ is a compact subset of $V$; the image of $C_1$ under $\pi$ is likewise a compact subset of $O$. On a compact neighborhood of $C_1$ in $V$, realized as the coordinate set of a compact $C\subseteq O$ as in the statement, $G$ is Lipschitz with constant $L$ and bounded by $M$. For the equivalent integral equation $z(t)=z(T_*-\tau)+\int_{T_*-\tau}^tG(s,z(s))\,ds$ the uniform Picard--Lindelöf step size $\min\{\tau_0,1/(2L),...\}$ is the same at every point of $C_1$ by [L3]; therefore a solution can be extended by a fixed positive amount beyond any $t<T_*$ close enough to $T_*$, contradicting maximality. Hence no finite forward endpoint occurs while the stated compact-value and $H^s$ bounds hold.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $m\ge1$, $N\ge0$, and let $P_N$ be the Galerkin
projection and $X_N$ the Galerkin space of [[def-gr-galerkin-fourier-projection]]
on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$. Then:

**(a)** $P_N$ is linear on $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$, self-adjoint
($\langle P_Nu,v\rangle_2=\langle u,P_Nv\rangle_2$ for all $u,v\in L^2$) and
idempotent ($P_N^2=P_N$), with range $X_N$ and kernel the classes with vanishing
coefficients on $\Lambda_N$;

**(b)** for every multi-index $\alpha$ with $|\alpha|\le s$ and every
$u\in H^s$, $P_ND^\alpha u=D^\alpha P_Nu$;

**(c)** for every $0\le r\le s$ and every $u\in H^r$,
$\|P_Nu\|_{H^r}\le\|u\|_{H^r}$;

**(d)** for every $0\le r\le s$ and every $u\in H^r$, $P_Nu\to u$ in $H^r$ as
$N\to\infty$;

**(e)** for every $s\ge1$, every $u\in H^s$ and every $N\ge0$,
$$\|u-P_Nu\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C_s\,(1+N^2)^{-1/2}\,\|u\|_{H^s}$$
with $C_s$ depending only on $s$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, $\mu$, $\chi_k$ and the
spaces $H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ be as in
[[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]] ($m\ge1$).

**(a) Mode sets.** For $N\ge0$ put
$\Lambda_N:=\{k\in\mathbb Z^3:|k|\le N\}$ with $|k|$ the Euclidean norm, and
$$X_N:=\Bigl\{\sum_{k\in\Lambda_N}a_k\chi_k:\ a_k\in\mathbb C^m,\ a_{-k}=\overline{a_k}\Bigr\}\subseteq C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m),$$
the **Galerkin space of modes up to $N$**; it is a finite-dimensional real
vector space of dimension $d_N:=m\,|\Lambda_N|$, and $X_N\subseteq X_{N'}$ for
$N\le N'$. (The reality condition $a_{-k}=\overline{a_k}$ is exactly the
condition that the trigonometric polynomial be real-valued.)

**(b) Projection.** For $u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ define
$$P_Nu:=\sum_{k\in\Lambda_N}\widehat u(k)\chi_k,\qquad (P_Nu)(x)=\sum_{k\in\Lambda_N}\widehat u(k)\chi_k(x),$$
with $\widehat u(k)$ the Fourier coefficients of clause (c) of
[[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]]; the second expression is a finite
sum, so $P_Nu\in X_N$; and $P_N:X_N\to X_N$ is the identity.
$P_N$ is called the **Galerkin (Fourier) projection**.

The definition fixes the projection only. Its self-adjointness,
derivative-commutation and operator-norm properties are proved in
[[lem-gr-galerkin-projection-properties]].

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open,
let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric hyperbolic coefficient family on $O$ over
an open interval $I\ni0$ ([[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]]), let
$u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ take values in a compact
$K\subseteq O$ with $\|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R$, and let $P_N$, $X_N$ be the Galerkin
projection and space ([[def-gr-galerkin-fourier-projection]]). Then for every
$N\ge0$:

**(a)** there is an open interval $J_N\ni0$ and a $C^1$ map $u_N:J_N\to X_N$
such that for all $t\in J_N$
$$P_N\Bigl[A^0(t,\cdot,u_N(t))\,\partial_tu_N(t)+\sum_{i=1}^3A^i(t,\cdot,u_N(t))\,\partial_iu_N(t)+B(t,\cdot,u_N(t))\Bigr]=0\quad\text{in }L^2,$$
with $u_N(0)=P_Nu_0$;

**(b)** [continuation criterion] if $[0,T_*)$ is the forward-maximal interval of
existence of $u_N$ and there are a compact $C\subseteq O$ and a constant
$R_1\ge0$ with $u_N(t)$ taking values in $C$ and $\|u_N(t)\|_{H^s}\le R_1$ for
all $t\in[0,T_*)$, then $u_N$ does not have $T_*$ as a finite forward endpoint:
the solution extends beyond $T_*$;

**(c)** the solution is unique and its local flow depends smoothly on the
finite-dimensional coordinates of the initial data.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix an integer $m\ge1$, an open set
$O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ with the subspace topology and a nondegenerate open
interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ containing $0$. All functions on
$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ are those of [[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]],
and smoothness on $I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O$ means smoothness of the
representative in the sense of clause (e) of that item.

**(a) Coefficients.** A **periodic symmetric hyperbolic coefficient family** on
$O$ consists of smooth maps
$$A^\mu:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)\quad(\mu=0,1,2,3),\qquad B:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\mathbb R^m,$$
such that $A^0(t,x,u)$ is positive definite for every
$(t,x,u)\in I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O$; here
$\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$ is the real vector space of symmetric
$m\times m$ matrices, identified with symmetric endomorphisms of $\mathbb R^m$
through the standard coordinate inner product, and positive definiteness means
$z^TA^0(t,x,u)z>0$ for every nonzero $z\in\mathbb R^m$
([[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]]).

**(b) The system.** The associated **symmetric hyperbolic system** is
$$A^0(t,x,u)\,\partial_tu+\sum_{i=1}^3A^i(t,x,u)\,\partial_iu+B(t,x,u)=0 .\qquad(\star)$$

**(c) Values and norms.** A map $u:J\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$
on an interval $J$ **takes values in a set $E\subseteq\mathbb R^m$** when
$u(t)(x)\in E$ for every $t\in J$ and every $x\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, with
$u(t)$ read through its continuous representative when $s>3/2$. For compact
$K\subseteq O$ and $R\ge0$ put
$$\mathcal S(K,R):=\bigl\{u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m):u_0\text{ takes values in }K,\ \|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R\bigr\}.$$

**(d) Classical solutions.** Let $s\ge2$. A **classical solution of $(\star)$ on
$J\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$** is a $C^1$ map
$u:J\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\to\mathbb R^m$ with $u(t,x)\in O$ for all
$(t,x)$ and $(\star)$ satisfied at every point, such that
$u\in L^\infty(J;H^s)$ and $\partial_tu\in L^\infty(J;H^{s-1})$. (For $s\ge2$
the embedding clause gives a continuous representative, so the pointwise
conditions are meaningful.)

**(e) Sobolev solutions.** Let $s\ge5$ and let $J$ be an open interval. A map
$u:J\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ is a **Sobolev solution of
$(\star)$ on $J$** when

1. $u\in L^\infty(J;H^s)\cap C^0(J;H^{s-1})$ and the distributional time
   derivative $\partial_tu$ lies in $L^\infty(J;H^{s-1})$;
2. $u$ takes values in $O$;
3. for almost every $t\in J$ the identity $(\star)$ holds in
   $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$, the coefficients being composed with
   the continuous representative of $u(t)$; all products are defined because
   $A^0(t,\cdot,u(t))$ and $A^i(t,\cdot,u(t))$ lie in $H^s$ with norm bounded
   by a function of $\|u(t)\|_{H^s}$, $\partial_tu(t)$ and $\partial_iu(t)$ lie
   in $H^{s-1}$, and $B(t,\cdot,u(t))$ lies in $H^s$.

**(f) Initial data.** **Initial data for $(\star)$ at time $0$** are a class
$u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ with $s\ge5$ whose values lie in a
compact subset of $O$; a solution **has initial value $u_0$** when
$u(t)\to u_0$ in $H^{s-1}$ as $t\to0$ within $J$.

The definition introduces the system and its solution classes only; existence,
uniqueness, continuous dependence and smooth persistence are asserted and
proved in [[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-existence]],
[[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-uniqueness-stability]] and
[[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-smooth-persistence]].

Let $m\ge1$ and let $B\in\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$ be positive definite,
that is $B^{\mathsf T}=B$ and $z^{\mathsf T}Bz>0$ for every nonzero
$z\in\mathbb R^m$ with the standard coordinate inner product.

**(a)** There are real numbers $0<a\le b$ with $a\,|z|^2\le z^{\mathsf T}Bz\le b\,|z|^2$
for every $z\in\mathbb R^m$; equivalently $aI\le B\le bI$ in the Loewner
order. They can be taken to be the least and largest eigenvalues of $B$.

**(b)** $B$ is invertible and $\tfrac1bI\le B^{-1}\le\tfrac1aI$, so in
particular $\|B^{-1}z\|\le a^{-1}\|z\|$.

**(c)** Let $\Lambda$ be a compact topological space and let
$B:\Lambda\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$ be continuous with $B(\lambda)$
positive definite for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$. Then there are constants
$0<a\le b$ with $aI\le B(\lambda)\le bI$ for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$.

**(d)** Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^p$ be open and let $B:D\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$
be smooth with $B(x)\ge aI$ for a constant $a>0$ and all $x\in D$. Then
$x\mapsto B(x)^{-1}$ is smooth on $D$ and $B(x)^{-1}\le a^{-1}I$ there.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, $k:=s-1\ge4$, let
$O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval, let
$F:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\mathbb R^{m'}$ and
$A:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to M_{m'}(\mathbb R)$ be smooth, let
$K\subseteq O$ be compact and let $R\ge0$. Then there is
$C=C(F,A,s,m,m',K,R)$ such that for every $u:I\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$
with $u(t)(x)\in K$ and $\|u(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$ for all $t$, the following hold,
where compositions use the continuous representatives of
[[lem-gr-periodic-sobolev-embedding]]:

**(a)** for every integer $0\le r\le s$, $\|F(t,\cdot,u(t))\|_{H^r}\le C\,(1+\|u(t)\|_{H^s})$;

**(b)** if $C_1\subseteq O$ is compact and convex, $u,v$ take values in $C_1$
and $\|v(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$, then
$$\|F(t,\cdot,u(t))-F(t,\cdot,v(t))\|_{H^k}\le C\,\|u(t)-v(t)\|_{H^k};$$

**(c)** for every $1\le|\alpha|\le k$ and every $w\in H^{|\alpha|-1}$,
$$\bigl\|D^\alpha\bigl(A(t,\cdot,u(t))\,w\bigr)-A(t,\cdot,u(t))\,D^\alpha w\bigr\|_2\le C\,\bigl(1+\|w\|_{H^{|\alpha|-1}}\bigr);$$

**(d)** for every $0\le j\le k$ and every $w\in H^j$, $\|A(t,\cdot,u(t))\,w\|_{H^j}\le C\,\|w\|_{H^j}$.

Let $m\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, and let $f:U\to\mathbb R$. A **multi-index** is $\alpha=(\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_{m-1})\in\mathbb N^m$. Put

$$|\alpha|:=\sum_{i<m}\alpha_i,\qquad \alpha!:=\prod_{i<m}\alpha_i!,\qquad h^\alpha:=\prod_{i<m}h_i^{\alpha_i}\quad(h\in\mathbb R^m).$$

Here $|\alpha|$ and $\alpha!$ use the natural-number sum and product of [[def-nat-finite-sum-and-product]], and $n!$ is the factorial of [[def-factorial-and-falling-factorial]]. By contrast, $h^\alpha$ is the finite product in $\mathbb R$ of [[def-finite-sum]], with the natural exponents interpreted by [[def-integer-power]]. For the zero multi-index $0$, set $D^0f:=f$. For nonzero $\alpha$, write

$$D^\alpha f:=\partial_0^{\alpha_0}\cdots\partial_{m-1}^{\alpha_{m-1}}f$$

for this displayed, canonical order whenever it exists. Coordinate partial derivatives have the meaning fixed in [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]].

For $k\in\mathbb N$, $f$ is of class $C^k$ on $U$ when, for every word $(i_1,\ldots,i_r)$ of coordinate indices with $0\le r\le k$, the iterated derivative $\partial_{i_r}\cdots\partial_{i_1}f$ exists and is continuous on $U$; the word of length $0$ denotes $f$. Thus this definition does **not** presuppose that differently ordered derivatives are equal. Equality of their values is a later theorem under these regularity hypotheses.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $m\ge1$, $N\ge0$, and let $P_N$ be the Galerkin
projection and $X_N$ the Galerkin space of [[def-gr-galerkin-fourier-projection]]
on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$. Then:

**(a)** $P_N$ is linear on $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$, self-adjoint
($\langle P_Nu,v\rangle_2=\langle u,P_Nv\rangle_2$ for all $u,v\in L^2$) and
idempotent ($P_N^2=P_N$), with range $X_N$ and kernel the classes with vanishing
coefficients on $\Lambda_N$;

**(b)** for every multi-index $\alpha$ with $|\alpha|\le s$ and every
$u\in H^s$, $P_ND^\alpha u=D^\alpha P_Nu$;

**(c)** for every $0\le r\le s$ and every $u\in H^r$,
$\|P_Nu\|_{H^r}\le\|u\|_{H^r}$;

**(d)** for every $0\le r\le s$ and every $u\in H^r$, $P_Nu\to u$ in $H^r$ as
$N\to\infty$;

**(e)** for every $s\ge1$, every $u\in H^s$ and every $N\ge0$,
$$\|u-P_Nu\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C_s\,(1+N^2)^{-1/2}\,\|u\|_{H^s}$$
with $C_s$ depending only on $s$.

derivations.claim: (Order zero.) Pair the Galerkin equation [L2] with $\partial_tu_N$: since $\partial_tu_N\in X_N$, self-adjointness [L1] gives $\int(\partial_tu_N)^{\mathsf T}P_N[A^0\partial_tu_N]=\int(\partial_tu_N)^{\mathsf T}A^0\partial_tu_N\ge a\|\partial_tu_N\|_2^2$ by [L3]; the right-hand side is $-\int(\partial_tu_N)^{\mathsf T}P_N[A^i\partial_iu_N+B]\le\|\partial_tu_N\|_2\|A^i\partial_iu_N+B\|_2$, and $\|A^i\partial_iu_N+B\|_{L^2}\le C_R(1+\|u_N\|_{H^s})$ by [L4] (the composition $A^i(t,\cdot,u_N)$ lies in $H^s\subseteq C^0$, so its sup norm is at most $C_R$, and $\|\partial_iu_N\|_2\le\|u_N\|_{H^s}$; the term $B$ is similar). Hence $a\|\partial_tu_N\|_2\le C_R(1+\|u_N\|_{H^s})$.

(Induction on the order: the estimate at order $j$.) Fix $j$ with $1\le j\le s-1$ and suppose the bound holds for all orders below $j$; fix $|\alpha|=j$. Applying $P_ND^\alpha$ to the Galerkin equation [L2] (legitimate by commutation [L1]) and pairing with $D^\alpha u_N\in X_N$ gives, after moving the leading term and using self-adjointness [L1], $a\|D^\alpha\partial_tu_N\|_2\le\bigl\|[D^\alpha,A^0(t,\cdot,u_N)]\partial_tu_N\bigr\|_2+\bigl\|D^\alpha(A^i(t,\cdot,u_N)\partial_iu_N+B(t,\cdot,u_N))\bigr\|_2$: indeed $D^\alpha(A^0\partial_tu_N)=A^0D^\alpha\partial_tu_N+[D^\alpha,A^0]\partial_tu_N$ by [L5], and the pairing of $P_ND^\alpha(A^0\partial_tu_N)$ with $D^\alpha u_N$ removes $P_N$. The first term is at most $C_R(1+\|\partial_tu_N\|_{H^{j-1}})$ by [L4], hence at most $C_R'(1+\|u_N\|_{H^s})$ by the induction hypothesis; the second is at most $C_R(1+\|u_N\|_{H^s})$ by [L4] applied to the compositions $A^i(t,\cdot,u_N)$ and the product bound, since $\|\partial_iu_N\|_{H^{j-1}}\le\|u_N\|_{H^s}$. Summing over the finitely many $|\alpha|\le j$ gives the estimate at order $j$.
(Conclusion.) The induction of step 2.1, starting from step 1.1, gives the stated bound for every $0\le j\le s-1$ after enlarging the constant to be independent of $j$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, $\mu$, $\chi_k$,
$\widehat u(k)$, the weak derivatives $D^\alpha$ and the spaces
$H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be as in
[[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]], and put
$$N_s(u)^2:=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+|k|^2)^s\,|\widehat u(k)|^2,\qquad |k|^2:=k_1^2+k_2^2+k_3^2 .$$

**(a)** Let $u\in H^s$ and let $\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^3$ with $|\alpha|\le s$. Then
$D^\alpha u\in H^{s-|\alpha|}$ and
$$\widehat{D^\alpha u}(k)=(ik)^\alpha\,\widehat u(k)\qquad(k\in\mathbb Z^3),\qquad (ik)^\alpha:=\prod_{j=1}^3(ik_j)^{\alpha_j}.$$

**(b)** Let $u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ satisfy $N_s(u)<\infty$.
Then $u\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$, and there are constants
$0<c_s\le C_s<\infty$, depending only on $s$, such that
$$c_s\,N_s(u)^2\le\|u\|_{H^s}^2\le C_s\,N_s(u)^2 .$$
The right-hand inequality holds for every $u\in H^s$, so the two norms are
equivalent on $H^s$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $m\ge1$, $N\ge0$, and let $P_N$ be the Galerkin
projection and $X_N$ the Galerkin space of [[def-gr-galerkin-fourier-projection]]
on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$. Then:

**(a)** $P_N$ is linear on $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$, self-adjoint
($\langle P_Nu,v\rangle_2=\langle u,P_Nv\rangle_2$ for all $u,v\in L^2$) and
idempotent ($P_N^2=P_N$), with range $X_N$ and kernel the classes with vanishing

**(b)** for every multi-index $\alpha$ with $|\alpha|\le s$ and every

**(c)** for every $0\le r\le s$ and every $u\in H^r$,
$\|P_Nu\|_{H^r}\le\|u\|_{H^r}$;

**(d)** for every $0\le r\le s$ and every $u\in H^r$, $P_Nu\to u$ in $H^r$ as

**(e)** for every $s\ge1$, every $u\in H^s$ and every $N\ge0$,

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]) for the quotient, product-measure and integration
clauses below, as in [[def-the-one-dimensional-torus-and-normalized-haar-integral]].

**(a) The 2 pi-periodic torus.** Let $\mathbb T_{2\pi}:=\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z$
carry the quotient topology, and let
$$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}:=\mathbb T_{2\pi}\times\mathbb T_{2\pi}\times\mathbb T_{2\pi}$$
with the product topology; write $q:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ for the
quotient map and $[x]:=(x^1+2\pi\mathbb Z,x^2+2\pi\mathbb Z,x^3+2\pi\mathbb Z)$.
The map $[0,2\pi)^3\to\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, $x\mapsto[x]$, is a bijection. The
normalized product measure $\mu$ is $\mu_{\mathbb T}\otimes\mu_{\mathbb T}\otimes\mu_{\mathbb T}$,
where $\mu_{\mathbb T}$ is the normalized measure of
[[def-the-one-dimensional-torus-and-normalized-haar-integral]] transported by
$t\mapsto2\pi t$; it is a probability measure on the Borel sets of
$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ and $\int f\,d\mu=(2\pi)^{-3}\int_{[0,2\pi)^3}f\circ q\,d\lambda_3$
for bounded measurable $f$ ([[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]).

**(b) Test functions and continuous classes.** For $N\ge1$ let
$C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be the set of compositions
$u\circ q$ of smooth maps $u:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^N$ that are $2\pi$-periodic
in each variable; these are the **smooth test functions** (real-valued when
$N=1$). For $m\ge0$ let $C^m(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be the set of
$u\circ q$ with $u\in C^m(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^N)$ $2\pi$-periodic in each
variable ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]), with
$$\|u\|_{C^m}:=\max_{|\alpha|\le m}\ \sup_{x\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}\bigl|(D^\alpha u)(x)\bigr| ,$$
where $D^\alpha$ is the multi-index derivative of
[[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]] applied to any
periodic representative; the displayed expression is independent of the
representative.

**(c) The Hilbert space $L^2$.** For $N\ge1$ let
$L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be the quotient of the set of measurable
$u$ with $\int|u|^2\,d\mu<\infty$ by the $\mu$-a.e. zero functions
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[thm-the-l-p-norm-descends-to-the-quotient-and-makes-l-p-a-normed-space]]),
with inner product $\langle u,v\rangle_2=\int u\cdot v\,d\mu$ and norm
$\|u\|_2=\langle u,u\rangle_2^{1/2}$; it is a real Hilbert space
([[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]). For
$u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ and $k\in\mathbb Z^3$ the
**$k$-th Fourier coefficient** is the vector
$$\widehat u(k):=\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}u(x)\,e^{-ik\cdot x}\,d\mu(x)\in\mathbb C^N ,$$
where $e^{-ik\cdot x}:=\chi_{-k}$ with $\chi_k([x]):=\exp(i\,k\cdot x)$; here
$u$ is read through any representative. Write $\chi_k:\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\to\mathbb C$,
$k\in\mathbb Z^3$, for these **characters**; under the identification
$x=2\pi y$ they are the characters $\exp(2\pi i\,k\cdot y)$ of
[[thm-fourier-basis-and-parseval-on-the-n-torus]], so $(\chi_k)_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}$
is an orthonormal basis of the complex space $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb C)$.

**(d) Weak derivatives and the periodic Sobolev spaces.** For
$u,v\in L^1(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$ and $\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^3$ say that
$v$ is the **weak derivative** $D^\alpha u$ if
$$\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,d\mu=(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}v\,\varphi\,d\mu$$
for every $\varphi\in C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$, where $D^\alpha\varphi$
is the multi-index derivative of the periodic representative
([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]] records the
Euclidean analogue). For an integer $s\ge0$ let
$$H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N):=\Bigl\{u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N):\ \text{for every }|\alpha|\le s\text{ there is }v_\alpha\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)\text{ with }v_\alpha=D^\alpha u\Bigr\},$$
the vector-valued weak derivative being componentwise, and put
$$\|u\|_{H^s}:=\Bigl(\sum_{|\alpha|\le s}\|D^\alpha u\|_2^2\Bigr)^{1/2}.$$
The classes $L^2\subseteq L^1$ on the probability space, so the integrals in the
test identity are finite: $|\int u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,d\mu|\le\|u\|_2\|D^\alpha\varphi\|_2$
by Cauchy--Schwarz. The definition asserts neither that the weak derivative
exists nor that the two norms compared in the next item are equivalent; those
are proved in [[lem-gr-periodic-fourier-differentiation-and-norm-equivalence]].

**(e) Conventions.** $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ open, $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ an
interval and maps $F:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\mathbb R^{m'}$ are
called smooth when their representatives $F(t,q(x),u)=G(t,x,u)$ have
$G\in C^\infty$. Throughout this page the torus is always this
$2\pi$-periodic one; a statement "for every $x$" means for every point of
$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, and "a.e." means $\mu$-a.e.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $m\ge1$, $N\ge0$, and let $P_N$ be the Galerkin
projection and $X_N$ the Galerkin space of [[def-gr-galerkin-fourier-projection]]
on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$. Then:

**(a)** $P_N$ is linear on $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$, self-adjoint
($\langle P_Nu,v\rangle_2=\langle u,P_Nv\rangle_2$ for all $u,v\in L^2$) and
idempotent ($P_N^2=P_N$), with range $X_N$ and kernel the classes with vanishing
coefficients on $\Lambda_N$;

**(b)** for every multi-index $\alpha$ with $|\alpha|\le s$ and every
$u\in H^s$, $P_ND^\alpha u=D^\alpha P_Nu$;

**(c)** for every $0\le r\le s$ and every $u\in H^r$,
$\|P_Nu\|_{H^r}\le\|u\|_{H^r}$;

**(d)** for every $0\le r\le s$ and every $u\in H^r$, $P_Nu\to u$ in $H^r$ as
$N\to\infty$;

**(e)** for every $s\ge1$, every $u\in H^s$ and every $N\ge0$,
$$\|u-P_Nu\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C_s\,(1+N^2)^{-1/2}\,\|u\|_{H^s}$$
with $C_s$ depending only on $s$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, $\mu$, $\chi_k$ and the
spaces $H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ be as in
[[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]] ($m\ge1$).

**(a) Mode sets.** For $N\ge0$ put
$\Lambda_N:=\{k\in\mathbb Z^3:|k|\le N\}$ with $|k|$ the Euclidean norm, and
$$X_N:=\Bigl\{\sum_{k\in\Lambda_N}a_k\chi_k:\ a_k\in\mathbb C^m,\ a_{-k}=\overline{a_k}\Bigr\}\subseteq C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m),$$
the **Galerkin space of modes up to $N$**; it is a finite-dimensional real
vector space of dimension $d_N:=m\,|\Lambda_N|$, and $X_N\subseteq X_{N'}$ for
$N\le N'$. (The reality condition $a_{-k}=\overline{a_k}$ is exactly the
condition that the trigonometric polynomial be real-valued.)

**(b) Projection.** For $u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ define
$$P_Nu:=\sum_{k\in\Lambda_N}\widehat u(k)\chi_k,\qquad (P_Nu)(x)=\sum_{k\in\Lambda_N}\widehat u(k)\chi_k(x),$$
with $\widehat u(k)$ the Fourier coefficients of clause (c) of
[[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]]; the second expression is a finite
sum, so $P_Nu\in X_N$; and $P_N:X_N\to X_N$ is the identity.
$P_N$ is called the **Galerkin (Fourier) projection**.

The definition fixes the projection only. Its self-adjointness,
derivative-commutation and operator-norm properties are proved in
[[lem-gr-galerkin-projection-properties]].

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$
([[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]]), let $K\subseteq O$ be compact
and $R\ge0$, and let $u_N:J\to X_N$ be a Galerkin solution of
[[lem-gr-galerkin-ode-local-solution]] for some $N\ge0$. Suppose that
$u_N(t)$ takes values in $K$ and satisfies $\|u_N(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$ for every
$t\in J$. Then there is $C=C(A^\mu,B,K,R,s)$ such that for every
$0\le j\le s-1$ and every $t\in J$
$$\|\partial_tu_N(t)\|_{H^j}\le C\,\bigl(1+\|u_N(t)\|_{H^s}\bigr).$$

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) for the Lebesgue-measure interfaces. Let $X$ be a real or complex Banach space, let $a<b$, and let $f:[a,b]\to X$ be continuous. Differentiation uses the underlying real structure. Then $G(t):=\int_a^t f(s)\,ds$ is differentiable on $(a,b)$ and has the corresponding one-sided derivatives at $a,b$, with $G'(t)=f(t)$, and this derivative extends continuously to $[a,b]$. Consequently, if $\varphi:[a,b]\to X$ is continuous, differentiable on $(a,b)$ with $\varphi'$ continuous on $(a,b)$ and extendable to a continuous $X$-valued function on $[a,b]$, then $\int_a^b\varphi'(s)\,ds=\varphi(b)-\varphi(a)$. The Bochner integral here is the one of [[def-bochner-integrable-function]]; the identities also hold for continuous curves on $[0,\infty)$ restricted to compact subintervals.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge0$ be an integer and $N\ge1$, write
$H^s=H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ for the periodic Sobolev space with
its norm $\|\cdot\|_{H^s}$ and Fourier coefficients
$\widehat u(k)\in\mathbb C^N$ of [[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]],
and put
$$N_s(u)^2:=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+|k|^2)^s\,|\widehat u(k)|^2\le+\infty .$$
Then:

**(a)** every Cauchy sequence in $(H^s,\|\cdot\|_{H^s})$ converges in
$(H^s,\|\cdot\|_{H^s})$; that is, $H^s$ is a real Banach space;

**(b)** more precisely, for every Cauchy sequence $(u_n)$ in $H^s$ there is
$u\in H^s$ with $N_s(u_n-u)\to0$, and then
$\|u_n-u\|_{H^s}\le C_s^{1/2}N_s(u_n-u)\to0$, where $C_s$ is the constant of
clause (b) of
[[lem-gr-periodic-fourier-differentiation-and-norm-equivalence]]; this $u$ is
the unique limit of $(u_n)$.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $X_0$ be a complete normed space over
$\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$ ([[def-banach-space]],
[[def-complete-metric-space]]) and let $X_1\subseteq X_0$ be a linear subspace
carrying a norm $\|\cdot\|_1$ such that ([[def-normed-subspace]]):

**(i)** there is $\kappa\ge0$ with $\|x\|_0\le\kappa\|x\|_1$ for every
$x\in X_1$; and

**(ii)** every sequence in $X_1$ bounded in $\|\cdot\|_1$ has a subsequence
converging in $X_0$ ([[def-metric-convergence]]).

Let $T>0$, $R\ge0$, $C\ge0$, and for $j\in\mathbb N$ let
$f_j:(-T,T)\to X_1$ satisfy
$$\|f_j(t)\|_1\le R,\qquad \|f_j(t)-f_j(t')\|_0\le C\,|t-t'|\qquad(t,t'\in(-T,T),\ j\in\mathbb N).$$

Then there are a strictly increasing sequence $j_1<j_2<\cdots$ in $\mathbb N$
and a continuous map $f:(-T,T)\to X_0$ ([[def-continuous-map-top]]) such that
$f_{j_n}\to f$ uniformly on every compact subinterval of $(-T,T)$; moreover
$\|f(t)-f(t')\|_0\le C\,|t-t'|$ for all $t,t'\in(-T,T)$.

derivations.claim: (Compact embedding (a).) Let $(v_j)$ be bounded by $R$ in $H^{r}$. For fixed $M$, the projections $P_Mv_j$ lie in the bounded subset $\{w\in X_M:\|w\|_{H^{r}}\le R\}$ of the finite-dimensional space $X_M$, hence are relatively compact in $X_M$; recursively extract, for each $M$, a subsequence of the previous one whose $P_M$-projections converge in $X_M$ (countably many selections, permitted by [L6]). The diagonal subsequence $(w_j)$ satisfies: for $\varepsilon>0$ choose $M$ with $2RC_r(1+M^2)^{-1/2}<\varepsilon/2$ [L1], then $j,l$ large so that $\|P_M(w_j-w_l)\|_{H^{r-1}}<\varepsilon/2$; then $\|w_j-w_l\|_{H^{r-1}}\le\|P_M(w_j-w_l)\|_{H^{r-1}}+\|(I-P_M)(w_j-w_l)\|_{H^{r-1}}<\varepsilon$, because $I-P_M$ is bounded with norm $C_r(1+M^2)^{-1/2}$ from $H^{r}$ to $H^{r-1}$ by [L1]. Hence the diagonal subsequence is Cauchy in $H^{r-1}$ and converges there by [L5]. This is (a).

(Equicontinuity (b).) For $t,t'\in(-T,T)$ the curve $s\mapsto u_N(s)$ is $C^1$ into the normed space $H^{s-1}$, so by [L4] $\|u_N(t)-u_N(t')\|_{H^{s-1}}\le\bigl|\int_{t'}^t\|\partial_tu_N(s)\|_{H^{s-1}}ds\bigr|\le C_R(1+R)|t-t'|$ by [L3]. This proves (b) with $C_0=C_R(1+R)$, a constant depending only on $A^\mu,B,K,R,s$.

(Locally uniform subsequence (c).) Apply [L7] with $X_0:=H^{s-1}(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ and $X_1:=H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$: $X_0$ is complete by [L5], the inclusion bound $\|x\|_{X_0}\le\|x\|_{X_1}$ holds by [L1], property (ii) of [L7] is clause (a) with $r=s$ (legitimate since $s\ge5\ge1$), and the family $u_N$ satisfies the two bounds of [L7] by the hypothesis and step 1.2. The extraction lemma therefore yields a strictly increasing sequence $N_j\to\infty$ and a continuous $u:(-T,T)\to H^{s-1}$ with $u_{N_j}\to u$ uniformly on every compact subinterval of $(-T,T)$. This is (c).

boundaries.reason: No empty set, empty family or empty index range is formed: the quantified objects (points, fields, mode families, data sets) are nonempty by the hypotheses, and the proofs never split off an empty case.
The value zero is not a distinguished boundary of this claim: no step divides by a quantity that can vanish and no separate zero case is required.
No cardinality-one case is separated: the arguments treat general finite or countable families and the one-element case is included without special treatment.

The hypotheses exclude degenerate configurations: the metric is Lorentzian/nondegenerate, the time matrix or coefficient is positive definite, velocity fields are unit and nonzero where required, and no degenerate limit is claimed.
The assertions are local in open domains around the initial surface or open time intervals, and no endpoint behaviour (completeness, boundary extension or endpoint regularity) is claimed.

boundaries.evidence: step 1.1 performs the countable diagonal extraction, and step 2.1 invokes [[lem-gr-rational-diagonal-extraction]], whose extraction over the rationals is a countable selection; all selections are covered by the stated Countable Choice hypothesis.

citations.quote:
Let $m\ge1$ and let $B\in\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$ be positive definite,
that is $B^{\mathsf T}=B$ and $z^{\mathsf T}Bz>0$ for every nonzero
$z\in\mathbb R^m$ with the standard coordinate inner product.

**(a)** There are real numbers $0<a\le b$ with $a\,|z|^2\le z^{\mathsf T}Bz\le b\,|z|^2$
for every $z\in\mathbb R^m$; equivalently $aI\le B\le bI$ in the Loewner
order. They can be taken to be the least and largest eigenvalues of $B$.

**(b)** $B$ is invertible and $\tfrac1bI\le B^{-1}\le\tfrac1aI$, so in
particular $\|B^{-1}z\|\le a^{-1}\|z\|$.

**(c)** Let $\Lambda$ be a compact topological space and let
$B:\Lambda\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$ be continuous with $B(\lambda)$
positive definite for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$. Then there are constants
$0<a\le b$ with $aI\le B(\lambda)\le bI$ for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$.

**(d)** Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^p$ be open and let $B:D\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$
be smooth with $B(x)\ge aI$ for a constant $a>0$ and all $x\in D$. Then
$x\mapsto B(x)^{-1}$ is smooth on $D$ and $B(x)^{-1}\le a^{-1}I$ there.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open,
let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric hyperbolic coefficient family on $O$ over
an open interval $I\ni0$ ([[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]]), let
$u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ take values in a compact
$K\subseteq O$ with $\|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R$, and let $P_N$, $X_N$ be the Galerkin
projection and space ([[def-gr-galerkin-fourier-projection]]). Then for every
$N\ge0$:

**(a)** there is an open interval $J_N\ni0$ and a $C^1$ map $u_N:J_N\to X_N$
such that for all $t\in J_N$
$$P_N\Bigl[A^0(t,\cdot,u_N(t))\,\partial_tu_N(t)+\sum_{i=1}^3A^i(t,\cdot,u_N(t))\,\partial_iu_N(t)+B(t,\cdot,u_N(t))\Bigr]=0\quad\text{in }L^2,$$
with $u_N(0)=P_Nu_0$;

**(b)** [continuation criterion] if $[0,T_*)$ is the forward-maximal interval of
existence of $u_N$ and there are a compact $C\subseteq O$ and a constant
$R_1\ge0$ with $u_N(t)$ taking values in $C$ and $\|u_N(t)\|_{H^s}\le R_1$ for
all $t\in[0,T_*)$, then $u_N$ does not have $T_*$ as a finite forward endpoint:
the solution extends beyond $T_*$;

**(c)** the solution is unique and its local flow depends smoothly on the
finite-dimensional coordinates of the initial data.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $m\ge1$, $N\ge0$, and let $P_N$ be the Galerkin
projection and $X_N$ the Galerkin space of [[def-gr-galerkin-fourier-projection]]
on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$. Then:

**(a)** $P_N$ is linear on $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$, self-adjoint
($\langle P_Nu,v\rangle_2=\langle u,P_Nv\rangle_2$ for all $u,v\in L^2$) and
idempotent ($P_N^2=P_N$), with range $X_N$ and kernel the classes with vanishing
coefficients on $\Lambda_N$;

**(b)** for every multi-index $\alpha$ with $|\alpha|\le s$ and every
$u\in H^s$, $P_ND^\alpha u=D^\alpha P_Nu$;

**(c)** for every $0\le r\le s$ and every $u\in H^r$,
$\|P_Nu\|_{H^r}\le\|u\|_{H^r}$;

**(d)** for every $0\le r\le s$ and every $u\in H^r$, $P_Nu\to u$ in $H^r$ as
$N\to\infty$;

**(e)** for every $s\ge1$, every $u\in H^s$ and every $N\ge0$,
$$\|u-P_Nu\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C_s\,(1+N^2)^{-1/2}\,\|u\|_{H^s}$$
with $C_s$ depending only on $s$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, $k:=s-1\ge4$, let
$O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval, let
$F:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\mathbb R^{m'}$ and
$A:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to M_{m'}(\mathbb R)$ be smooth, let
$K\subseteq O$ be compact and let $R\ge0$. Then there is
$C=C(F,A,s,m,m',K,R)$ such that for every $u:I\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$
with $u(t)(x)\in K$ and $\|u(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$ for all $t$, the following hold,
where compositions use the continuous representatives of
[[lem-gr-periodic-sobolev-embedding]]:

**(a)** for every integer $0\le r\le s$, $\|F(t,\cdot,u(t))\|_{H^r}\le C\,(1+\|u(t)\|_{H^s})$;

**(b)** if $C_1\subseteq O$ is compact and convex, $u,v$ take values in $C_1$
and $\|v(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$, then
$$\|F(t,\cdot,u(t))-F(t,\cdot,v(t))\|_{H^k}\le C\,\|u(t)-v(t)\|_{H^k};$$

**(c)** for every $1\le|\alpha|\le k$ and every $w\in H^{|\alpha|-1}$,
$$\bigl\|D^\alpha\bigl(A(t,\cdot,u(t))\,w\bigr)-A(t,\cdot,u(t))\,D^\alpha w\bigr\|_2\le C\,\bigl(1+\|w\|_{H^{|\alpha|-1}}\bigr);$$

**(d)** for every $0\le j\le k$ and every $w\in H^j$, $\|A(t,\cdot,u(t))\,w\|_{H^j}\le C\,\|w\|_{H^j}$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$
([[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]]), let $K\subseteq O$ be compact
and $R\ge0$, and let $u_N:J\to X_N$ be a Galerkin solution of
[[lem-gr-galerkin-ode-local-solution]] for some $N\ge0$. Suppose that
$u_N(t)$ takes values in $K$ and satisfies $\|u_N(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$ for every
$t\in J$. Then there is $C=C(A^\mu,B,K,R,s)$ such that for every
$0\le j\le s-1$ and every $t\in J$
$$\|\partial_tu_N(t)\|_{H^j}\le C\,\bigl(1+\|u_N(t)\|_{H^s}\bigr).$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open,
let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric hyperbolic coefficient family on $O$ over
an open interval $I\ni0$ ([[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]]), let
$u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ take values in a compact
$K\subseteq O$ with $\|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R$, and let $P_N$, $X_N$ be the Galerkin
projection and space ([[def-gr-galerkin-fourier-projection]]). Then for every
$N\ge0$:

**(a)** there is an open interval $J_N\ni0$ and a $C^1$ map $u_N:J_N\to X_N$
such that for all $t\in J_N$
$$P_N\Bigl[A^0(t,\cdot,u_N(t))\,\partial_tu_N(t)+\sum_{i=1}^3A^i(t,\cdot,u_N(t))\,\partial_iu_N(t)+B(t,\cdot,u_N(t))\Bigr]=0\quad\text{in }L^2,$$
with $u_N(0)=P_Nu_0$;

**(b)** [continuation criterion] if $[0,T_*)$ is the forward-maximal interval of
existence of $u_N$ and there are a compact $C\subseteq O$ and a constant
$R_1\ge0$ with $u_N(t)$ taking values in $C$ and $\|u_N(t)\|_{H^s}\le R_1$ for
all $t\in[0,T_*)$, then $u_N$ does not have $T_*$ as a finite forward endpoint:
the solution extends beyond $T_*$;

**(c)** the solution is unique and its local flow depends smoothly on the
finite-dimensional coordinates of the initial data.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]) for the quotient, product-measure and integration
clauses below, as in [[def-the-one-dimensional-torus-and-normalized-haar-integral]].

**(a) The 2 pi-periodic torus.** Let $\mathbb T_{2\pi}:=\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z$
carry the quotient topology, and let
$$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}:=\mathbb T_{2\pi}\times\mathbb T_{2\pi}\times\mathbb T_{2\pi}$$
with the product topology; write $q:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ for the
quotient map and $[x]:=(x^1+2\pi\mathbb Z,x^2+2\pi\mathbb Z,x^3+2\pi\mathbb Z)$.
The map $[0,2\pi)^3\to\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, $x\mapsto[x]$, is a bijection. The
normalized product measure $\mu$ is $\mu_{\mathbb T}\otimes\mu_{\mathbb T}\otimes\mu_{\mathbb T}$,
where $\mu_{\mathbb T}$ is the normalized measure of
[[def-the-one-dimensional-torus-and-normalized-haar-integral]] transported by
$t\mapsto2\pi t$; it is a probability measure on the Borel sets of
$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ and $\int f\,d\mu=(2\pi)^{-3}\int_{[0,2\pi)^3}f\circ q\,d\lambda_3$
for bounded measurable $f$ ([[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]).

**(b) Test functions and continuous classes.** For $N\ge1$ let
$C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be the set of compositions
$u\circ q$ of smooth maps $u:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^N$ that are $2\pi$-periodic
in each variable; these are the **smooth test functions** (real-valued when
$N=1$). For $m\ge0$ let $C^m(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be the set of
$u\circ q$ with $u\in C^m(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^N)$ $2\pi$-periodic in each
variable ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]), with
$$\|u\|_{C^m}:=\max_{|\alpha|\le m}\ \sup_{x\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}\bigl|(D^\alpha u)(x)\bigr| ,$$
where $D^\alpha$ is the multi-index derivative of
[[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]] applied to any
periodic representative; the displayed expression is independent of the
representative.

**(c) The Hilbert space $L^2$.** For $N\ge1$ let
$L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be the quotient of the set of measurable
$u$ with $\int|u|^2\,d\mu<\infty$ by the $\mu$-a.e. zero functions
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[thm-the-l-p-norm-descends-to-the-quotient-and-makes-l-p-a-normed-space]]),
with inner product $\langle u,v\rangle_2=\int u\cdot v\,d\mu$ and norm
$\|u\|_2=\langle u,u\rangle_2^{1/2}$; it is a real Hilbert space
([[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]). For
$u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ and $k\in\mathbb Z^3$ the
**$k$-th Fourier coefficient** is the vector
$$\widehat u(k):=\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}u(x)\,e^{-ik\cdot x}\,d\mu(x)\in\mathbb C^N ,$$
where $e^{-ik\cdot x}:=\chi_{-k}$ with $\chi_k([x]):=\exp(i\,k\cdot x)$; here
$u$ is read through any representative. Write $\chi_k:\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\to\mathbb C$,
$k\in\mathbb Z^3$, for these **characters**; under the identification
$x=2\pi y$ they are the characters $\exp(2\pi i\,k\cdot y)$ of
[[thm-fourier-basis-and-parseval-on-the-n-torus]], so $(\chi_k)_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}$
is an orthonormal basis of the complex space $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb C)$.

**(d) Weak derivatives and the periodic Sobolev spaces.** For
$u,v\in L^1(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$ and $\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^3$ say that
$v$ is the **weak derivative** $D^\alpha u$ if
$$\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,d\mu=(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}v\,\varphi\,d\mu$$
for every $\varphi\in C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$, where $D^\alpha\varphi$
is the multi-index derivative of the periodic representative
([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]] records the
Euclidean analogue). For an integer $s\ge0$ let
$$H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N):=\Bigl\{u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N):\ \text{for every }|\alpha|\le s\text{ there is }v_\alpha\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)\text{ with }v_\alpha=D^\alpha u\Bigr\},$$
the vector-valued weak derivative being componentwise, and put
$$\|u\|_{H^s}:=\Bigl(\sum_{|\alpha|\le s}\|D^\alpha u\|_2^2\Bigr)^{1/2}.$$
The classes $L^2\subseteq L^1$ on the probability space, so the integrals in the
test identity are finite: $|\int u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,d\mu|\le\|u\|_2\|D^\alpha\varphi\|_2$
by Cauchy--Schwarz. The definition asserts neither that the weak derivative
exists nor that the two norms compared in the next item are equivalent; those
are proved in [[lem-gr-periodic-fourier-differentiation-and-norm-equivalence]].

**(e) Conventions.** $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ open, $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ an
interval and maps $F:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\mathbb R^{m'}$ are
called smooth when their representatives $F(t,q(x),u)=G(t,x,u)$ have
$G\in C^\infty$. Throughout this page the torus is always this
$2\pi$-periodic one; a statement "for every $x$" means for every point of
$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, and "a.e." means $\mu$-a.e.

derivations.claim: (Equivalence (a).) For each $|\alpha|\le s$ the integrand $(D^\alpha u_N)^{\mathsf T}A^0D^\alpha u_N$ lies between $a|D^\alpha u_N|^2$ and $b|D^\alpha u_N|^2$ pointwise by [L1]; integrating and summing over $\alpha$ gives $a\|u_N\|_{H^s}^2\le e\le b\|u_N\|_{H^s}^2$.

(Substituting the Galerkin equation into $e'$.) For each $|\alpha|\le s$ use $D^\alpha u_N\in X_N$ and self-adjoint commutativity [L2]: $\int(D^\alpha u_N)^{\mathsf T}A^0D^\alpha\partial_tu_N=\int(D^\alpha u_N)^{\mathsf T}D^\alpha(A^0\partial_tu_N)-\int(D^\alpha u_N)^{\mathsf T}[D^\alpha,A^0]\partial_tu_N$ and $\int(D^\alpha u_N)^{\mathsf T}P_ND^\alpha(A^0\partial_tu_N)=-\int(D^\alpha u_N)^{\mathsf T}D^\alpha(A^i\partial_iu_N+B)$ by the Galerkin equation and self-adjointness. Substituting into [L4] and splitting $D^\alpha(A^i\partial_iu_N)=A^iD^\alpha\partial_iu_N+[D^\alpha,A^i]\partial_iu_N$, the symmetric term integrates by parts on the torus: $\int(D^\alpha u_N)^{\mathsf T}A^iD^\alpha\partial_iu_N=-\tfrac12\int(D^\alpha u_N)^{\mathsf T}(\partial_iA^i)(D^\alpha u_N)$. Hence $e'(t)=\sum_{|\alpha|\le s}\bigl[-2\int(D^\alpha u_N)^{\mathsf T}[D^\alpha,A^0]\partial_tu_N-2\int(D^\alpha u_N)^{\mathsf T}[D^\alpha,A^i]\partial_iu_N+\int(D^\alpha u_N)^{\mathsf T}(\partial_iA^i)D^\alpha u_N-2\int(D^\alpha u_N)^{\mathsf T}D^\alpha B+\int(D^\alpha u_N)^{\mathsf T}(\partial_tA^0)D^\alpha u_N\bigr]$.

(Bounding the terms by $1+e$.) Each of the five sums is bounded using Cauchy--Schwarz and [L3]: $\bigl|\int(D^\alpha u_N)^{\mathsf T}[D^\alpha,A^0]\partial_tu_N\bigr|\le\|D^\alpha u_N\|_2\,C_R(1+\|\partial_tu_N\|_{H^{|\alpha|-1}})\le C_R(1+\|u_N\|_{H^s})\|D^\alpha u_N\|_2$; similarly for the spatial commutators with $\|\partial_iu_N\|_{H^{s-1}}\le\|u_N\|_{H^s}$; the $\partial_iA^i$ and $\partial_tA^0$ terms are bounded by a constant times $\|D^\alpha u_N\|_2^2$; and $\bigl|\int(D^\alpha u_N)^{\mathsf T}D^\alpha B\bigr|\le C_R(1+\|u_N\|_{H^s})\|D^\alpha u_N\|_2$. Summing over $|\alpha|\le s$, using Young's inequality [L5] and $\|u_N\|^2_{H^s}\le a^{-1}e$ from step 1.1, gives $e'\le C(1+e)$ with $C=C(A^\mu,B,K,R,s)$.

(Gronwall consequence.) By step 1.1 and step 2.1, $e(t)\le(1+e(0))e^{C|t-t_0|}$ on every interval where the bounds hold, by Gronwall's integral inequality ([[thm-gronwall-integral-inequality]]); this uses only $e'\le C(1+e)$ and the differentiability of $e$ from [L4].
