citations.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let integers $s\ge m\ge0$ satisfy $s-m>3/2$, and
let $u\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ with the objects and notation of
[[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]]. Then:

**(a)** There is a unique representative $u^*\in C^m(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$
of the class $u$, and for every $|\alpha|\le m$ the series
$\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(ik)^\alpha\widehat u(k)\chi_k$ converges absolutely and
uniformly on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ to $D^\alpha u^*$; moreover there is
$C=C(s,m,N)$ with
$$\|u^*\|_{C^m}\le C\,\|u\|_{H^s}.$$

**(b)** Writing $d(x,y):=\min\{\,|x-y+2\pi l|:l\in\mathbb Z^3\,\}$ for the
induced metric on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ and fixing
$0<\theta\le\min\{1,s-m-\tfrac32\}$, there is $C'=C'(s,m,N,\theta)$ with
$$\bigl|D^\alpha u^*(x)-D^\alpha u^*(y)\bigr|\le C'\,\|u\|_{H^s}\,d(x,y)^\theta\qquad(x,y\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi},\ |\alpha|\le m).$$

**(c)** The assignment $u\mapsto u^*$ is linear; and if $(u_j)$ is a sequence in
$H^s$ with $u_j\to u$ in $H^s$, then $u_j^*\to u^*$ uniformly together with all
derivatives of order at most $m$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]) for the quotient, product-measure and integration
clauses below, as in [[def-the-one-dimensional-torus-and-normalized-haar-integral]].

**(a) The 2 pi-periodic torus.** Let $\mathbb T_{2\pi}:=\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z$
carry the quotient topology, and let
$$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}:=\mathbb T_{2\pi}\times\mathbb T_{2\pi}\times\mathbb T_{2\pi}$$
with the product topology; write $q:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ for the
quotient map and $[x]:=(x^1+2\pi\mathbb Z,x^2+2\pi\mathbb Z,x^3+2\pi\mathbb Z)$.
The map $[0,2\pi)^3\to\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, $x\mapsto[x]$, is a bijection. The
normalized product measure $\mu$ is $\mu_{\mathbb T}\otimes\mu_{\mathbb T}\otimes\mu_{\mathbb T}$,
where $\mu_{\mathbb T}$ is the normalized measure of
[[def-the-one-dimensional-torus-and-normalized-haar-integral]] transported by
$t\mapsto2\pi t$; it is a probability measure on the Borel sets of
$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ and $\int f\,d\mu=(2\pi)^{-3}\int_{[0,2\pi)^3}f\circ q\,d\lambda_3$
for bounded measurable $f$ ([[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]).

**(b) Test functions and continuous classes.** For $N\ge1$ let
$C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be the set of compositions
$u\circ q$ of smooth maps $u:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^N$ that are $2\pi$-periodic
in each variable; these are the **smooth test functions** (real-valued when
$N=1$). For $m\ge0$ let $C^m(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be the set of
$u\circ q$ with $u\in C^m(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^N)$ $2\pi$-periodic in each
variable ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]), with
$$\|u\|_{C^m}:=\max_{|\alpha|\le m}\ \sup_{x\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}\bigl|(D^\alpha u)(x)\bigr| ,$$
where $D^\alpha$ is the multi-index derivative of
[[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]] applied to any
periodic representative; the displayed expression is independent of the
representative.

**(c) The Hilbert space $L^2$.** For $N\ge1$ let
$L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be the quotient of the set of measurable
$u$ with $\int|u|^2\,d\mu<\infty$ by the $\mu$-a.e. zero functions
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[thm-the-l-p-norm-descends-to-the-quotient-and-makes-l-p-a-normed-space]]),
with inner product $\langle u,v\rangle_2=\int u\cdot v\,d\mu$ and norm
$\|u\|_2=\langle u,u\rangle_2^{1/2}$; it is a real Hilbert space
([[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]). For
$u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ and $k\in\mathbb Z^3$ the
**$k$-th Fourier coefficient** is the vector
$$\widehat u(k):=\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}u(x)\,e^{-ik\cdot x}\,d\mu(x)\in\mathbb C^N ,$$
where $e^{-ik\cdot x}:=\chi_{-k}$ with $\chi_k([x]):=\exp(i\,k\cdot x)$; here
$u$ is read through any representative. Write $\chi_k:\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\to\mathbb C$,
$k\in\mathbb Z^3$, for these **characters**; under the identification
$x=2\pi y$ they are the characters $\exp(2\pi i\,k\cdot y)$ of
[[thm-fourier-basis-and-parseval-on-the-n-torus]], so $(\chi_k)_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}$
is an orthonormal basis of the complex space $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb C)$.

**(d) Weak derivatives and the periodic Sobolev spaces.** For
$u,v\in L^1(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$ and $\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^3$ say that
$v$ is the **weak derivative** $D^\alpha u$ if
$$\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,d\mu=(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}v\,\varphi\,d\mu$$
for every $\varphi\in C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$, where $D^\alpha\varphi$
is the multi-index derivative of the periodic representative
([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]] records the
Euclidean analogue). For an integer $s\ge0$ let
$$H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N):=\Bigl\{u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N):\ \text{for every }|\alpha|\le s\text{ there is }v_\alpha\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)\text{ with }v_\alpha=D^\alpha u\Bigr\},$$
the vector-valued weak derivative being componentwise, and put
$$\|u\|_{H^s}:=\Bigl(\sum_{|\alpha|\le s}\|D^\alpha u\|_2^2\Bigr)^{1/2}.$$
The classes $L^2\subseteq L^1$ on the probability space, so the integrals in the
test identity are finite: $|\int u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,d\mu|\le\|u\|_2\|D^\alpha\varphi\|_2$
by Cauchy--Schwarz. The definition asserts neither that the weak derivative
exists nor that the two norms compared in the next item are equivalent; those
are proved in [[lem-gr-periodic-fourier-differentiation-and-norm-equivalence]].

**(e) Conventions.** $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ open, $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ an
interval and maps $F:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\mathbb R^{m'}$ are
called smooth when their representatives $F(t,q(x),u)=G(t,x,u)$ have
$G\in C^\infty$. Throughout this page the torus is always this
$2\pi$-periodic one; a statement "for every $x$" means for every point of
$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, and "a.e." means $\mu$-a.e.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open,
let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric hyperbolic coefficient family on $O$ over
an open interval $I\ni0$ ([[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]]), let
$u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ take values in a compact
$K\subseteq O$ with $\|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R$, and let $P_N$, $X_N$ be the Galerkin
projection and space ([[def-gr-galerkin-fourier-projection]]). Then for every
$N\ge0$:

**(a)** there is an open interval $J_N\ni0$ and a $C^1$ map $u_N:J_N\to X_N$
such that for all $t\in J_N$
$$P_N\Bigl[A^0(t,\cdot,u_N(t))\,\partial_tu_N(t)+\sum_{i=1}^3A^i(t,\cdot,u_N(t))\,\partial_iu_N(t)+B(t,\cdot,u_N(t))\Bigr]=0\quad\text{in }L^2,$$
with $u_N(0)=P_Nu_0$;

**(b)** [continuation criterion] if $[0,T_*)$ is the forward-maximal interval of
existence of $u_N$ and there are a compact $C\subseteq O$ and a constant
$R_1\ge0$ with $u_N(t)$ taking values in $C$ and $\|u_N(t)\|_{H^s}\le R_1$ for
all $t\in[0,T_*)$, then $u_N$ does not have $T_*$ as a finite forward endpoint:
the solution extends beyond $T_*$;

**(c)** the solution is unique and its local flow depends smoothly on the
finite-dimensional coordinates of the initial data.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $m\ge1$, $N\ge0$, and let $P_N$ be the Galerkin
projection and $X_N$ the Galerkin space of [[def-gr-galerkin-fourier-projection]]
on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$. Then:

**(a)** $P_N$ is linear on $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$, self-adjoint
($\langle P_Nu,v\rangle_2=\langle u,P_Nv\rangle_2$ for all $u,v\in L^2$) and
idempotent ($P_N^2=P_N$), with range $X_N$ and kernel the classes with vanishing
coefficients on $\Lambda_N$;

**(b)** for every multi-index $\alpha$ with $|\alpha|\le s$ and every
$u\in H^s$, $P_ND^\alpha u=D^\alpha P_Nu$;

**(c)** for every $0\le r\le s$ and every $u\in H^r$,
$\|P_Nu\|_{H^r}\le\|u\|_{H^r}$;

**(d)** for every $0\le r\le s$ and every $u\in H^r$, $P_Nu\to u$ in $H^r$ as
$N\to\infty$;

**(e)** for every $s\ge1$, every $u\in H^s$ and every $N\ge0$,
$$\|u-P_Nu\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C_s\,(1+N^2)^{-1/2}\,\|u\|_{H^s}$$
with $C_s$ depending only on $s$.

Let $m\ge1$ and let $B\in\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$ be positive definite,
that is $B^{\mathsf T}=B$ and $z^{\mathsf T}Bz>0$ for every nonzero
$z\in\mathbb R^m$ with the standard coordinate inner product.

**(a)** There are real numbers $0<a\le b$ with $a\,|z|^2\le z^{\mathsf T}Bz\le b\,|z|^2$
for every $z\in\mathbb R^m$; equivalently $aI\le B\le bI$ in the Loewner
order. They can be taken to be the least and largest eigenvalues of $B$.

**(b)** $B$ is invertible and $\tfrac1bI\le B^{-1}\le\tfrac1aI$, so in
particular $\|B^{-1}z\|\le a^{-1}\|z\|$.

**(c)** Let $\Lambda$ be a compact topological space and let
$B:\Lambda\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$ be continuous with $B(\lambda)$
positive definite for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$. Then there are constants
$0<a\le b$ with $aI\le B(\lambda)\le bI$ for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$.

**(d)** Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^p$ be open and let $B:D\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$
be smooth with $B(x)\ge aI$ for a constant $a>0$ and all $x\in D$. Then
$x\mapsto B(x)^{-1}$ is smooth on $D$ and $B(x)^{-1}\le a^{-1}I$ there.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, $k:=s-1\ge4$, let
$O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval, let
$F:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\mathbb R^{m'}$ and
$A:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to M_{m'}(\mathbb R)$ be smooth, let
$K\subseteq O$ be compact and let $R\ge0$. Then there is
$C=C(F,A,s,m,m',K,R)$ such that for every $u:I\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$
with $u(t)(x)\in K$ and $\|u(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$ for all $t$, the following hold,
where compositions use the continuous representatives of
[[lem-gr-periodic-sobolev-embedding]]:

**(a)** for every integer $0\le r\le s$, $\|F(t,\cdot,u(t))\|_{H^r}\le C\,(1+\|u(t)\|_{H^s})$;

**(b)** if $C_1\subseteq O$ is compact and convex, $u,v$ take values in $C_1$
and $\|v(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$, then
$$\|F(t,\cdot,u(t))-F(t,\cdot,v(t))\|_{H^k}\le C\,\|u(t)-v(t)\|_{H^k};$$

**(c)** for every $1\le|\alpha|\le k$ and every $w\in H^{|\alpha|-1}$,
$$\bigl\|D^\alpha\bigl(A(t,\cdot,u(t))\,w\bigr)-A(t,\cdot,u(t))\,D^\alpha w\bigr\|_2\le C\,\bigl(1+\|w\|_{H^{|\alpha|-1}}\bigr);$$

**(d)** for every $0\le j\le k$ and every $w\in H^j$, $\|A(t,\cdot,u(t))\,w\|_{H^j}\le C\,\|w\|_{H^j}$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$
([[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]]), let $K\subseteq O$ be compact
and $R\ge0$, and let $u_N:J\to X_N$ be a Galerkin solution of
[[lem-gr-galerkin-ode-local-solution]] for some $N\ge0$. Suppose that
$u_N(t)$ takes values in $K$ and satisfies $\|u_N(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$ for every
$t\in J$. Then there is $C=C(A^\mu,B,K,R,s)$ such that for every
$0\le j\le s-1$ and every $t\in J$
$$\|\partial_tu_N(t)\|_{H^j}\le C\,\bigl(1+\|u_N(t)\|_{H^s}\bigr).$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, let
$K\subseteq O$ be compact and convex, and let $R\ge0$. Let $u_N:J\to X_N$ be a
Galerkin solution of [[lem-gr-galerkin-ode-local-solution]] on an open interval
$J\ni0$ for some $N\ge0$, and suppose that $u_N(t)$ takes values in $K$ and
satisfies $\|u_N(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$ for every $t\in J$.

Then there is a constant $C_1=C_1(A^\mu,B,K,s)$ such that
$$\bigl\|\partial_tu_N(t)-\partial_tu_N(t')\bigr\|_{H^{s-2}}\le C_1\,(1+R)^2\,|t-t'|\qquad(t,t'\in J).$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]).

**(a)** For every integer $r\ge1$, every $R\ge0$ and every sequence $(v_j)$
in $H^r(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ with $\|v_j\|_{H^r}\le R$ there is a
subsequence converging in $H^{r-1}(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$.

**(b)** Let $s\ge5$, $R\ge0$, $T>0$, let $K\subseteq O$ be compact, and let
$u_N:(-T,T)\to X_N$ ($N=0,1,2,\dots$) be a family of Galerkin solutions with
$u_N(t)$ taking values in $K$ and $\|u_N(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$ for all $t$. Then the
family is equicontinuous in the $H^{s-1}$ metric: there is
$C_0=C_0(A^\mu,B,K,R,s)$ with
$$\|u_N(t)-u_N(t')\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C_0\,|t-t'|\qquad(t,t'\in(-T,T),\ N\ge0).$$

**(c)** Under the hypotheses of (b) there are a strictly increasing sequence
$N_j\to\infty$ and $u\in C^0((-T,T);H^{s-1}(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m))$
with $u_{N_j}\to u$ uniformly on every compact subinterval of $(-T,T)$ in the
$H^{s-1}$ norm.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge0$ be an integer and $N\ge1$, write
$H^s=H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ for the periodic Sobolev space with
its norm $\|\cdot\|_{H^s}$ and Fourier coefficients
$\widehat u(k)\in\mathbb C^N$ of [[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]],
and put
$$N_s(u)^2:=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+|k|^2)^s\,|\widehat u(k)|^2\le+\infty .$$
Then:

**(a)** every Cauchy sequence in $(H^s,\|\cdot\|_{H^s})$ converges in
$(H^s,\|\cdot\|_{H^s})$; that is, $H^s$ is a real Banach space;

**(b)** more precisely, for every Cauchy sequence $(u_n)$ in $H^s$ there is
$u\in H^s$ with $N_s(u_n-u)\to0$, and then
$\|u_n-u\|_{H^s}\le C_s^{1/2}N_s(u_n-u)\to0$, where $C_s$ is the constant of
clause (b) of
[[lem-gr-periodic-fourier-differentiation-and-norm-equivalence]]; this $u$ is
the unique limit of $(u_n)$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $X_0$ be a complete normed space over
$\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$ ([[def-banach-space]],
[[def-complete-metric-space]]) and let $X_1\subseteq X_0$ be a linear subspace
carrying a norm $\|\cdot\|_1$ such that ([[def-normed-subspace]]):

**(i)** there is $\kappa\ge0$ with $\|x\|_0\le\kappa\|x\|_1$ for every
$x\in X_1$; and

**(ii)** every sequence in $X_1$ bounded in $\|\cdot\|_1$ has a subsequence
converging in $X_0$ ([[def-metric-convergence]]).

Let $T>0$, $R\ge0$, $C\ge0$, and for $j\in\mathbb N$ let
$f_j:(-T,T)\to X_1$ satisfy
$$\|f_j(t)\|_1\le R,\qquad \|f_j(t)-f_j(t')\|_0\le C\,|t-t'|\qquad(t,t'\in(-T,T),\ j\in\mathbb N).$$

Then there are a strictly increasing sequence $j_1<j_2<\cdots$ in $\mathbb N$
and a continuous map $f:(-T,T)\to X_0$ ([[def-continuous-map-top]]) such that
$f_{j_n}\to f$ uniformly on every compact subinterval of $(-T,T)$; moreover
$\|f(t)-f(t')\|_0\le C\,|t-t'|$ for all $t,t'\in(-T,T)$.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) for the Lebesgue-measure interfaces. Let $X$ be a real or complex Banach space, let $a<b$, and let $f:[a,b]\to X$ be continuous. Differentiation uses the underlying real structure. Then $G(t):=\int_a^t f(s)\,ds$ is differentiable on $(a,b)$ and has the corresponding one-sided derivatives at $a,b$, with $G'(t)=f(t)$, and this derivative extends continuously to $[a,b]$. Consequently, if $\varphi:[a,b]\to X$ is continuous, differentiable on $(a,b)$ with $\varphi'$ continuous on $(a,b)$ and extendable to a continuous $X$-valued function on $[a,b]$, then $\int_a^b\varphi'(s)\,ds=\varphi(b)-\varphi(a)$. The Bochner integral here is the one of [[def-bochner-integrable-function]]; the identities also hold for continuous curves on $[0,\infty)$ restricted to compact subintervals.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, $\mu$, $\chi_k$,
$\widehat u(k)$, the weak derivatives $D^\alpha$ and the spaces
$H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be as in
[[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]], and put
$$N_s(u)^2:=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+|k|^2)^s\,|\widehat u(k)|^2,\qquad |k|^2:=k_1^2+k_2^2+k_3^2 .$$

**(a)** Let $u\in H^s$ and let $\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^3$ with $|\alpha|\le s$. Then
$D^\alpha u\in H^{s-|\alpha|}$ and
$$\widehat{D^\alpha u}(k)=(ik)^\alpha\,\widehat u(k)\qquad(k\in\mathbb Z^3),\qquad (ik)^\alpha:=\prod_{j=1}^3(ik_j)^{\alpha_j}.$$

**(b)** Let $u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ satisfy $N_s(u)<\infty$.
Then $u\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$, and there are constants
$0<c_s\le C_s<\infty$, depending only on $s$, such that
$$c_s\,N_s(u)^2\le\|u\|_{H^s}^2\le C_s\,N_s(u)^2 .$$
The right-hand inequality holds for every $u\in H^s$, so the two norms are
equivalent on $H^s$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]) for the quotient, product-measure and integration
clauses below, as in [[def-the-one-dimensional-torus-and-normalized-haar-integral]].

**(a) The 2 pi-periodic torus.** Let $\mathbb T_{2\pi}:=\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z$
carry the quotient topology, and let
$$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}:=\mathbb T_{2\pi}\times\mathbb T_{2\pi}\times\mathbb T_{2\pi}$$
with the product topology; write $q:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ for the
quotient map and $[x]:=(x^1+2\pi\mathbb Z,x^2+2\pi\mathbb Z,x^3+2\pi\mathbb Z)$.
The map $[0,2\pi)^3\to\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, $x\mapsto[x]$, is a bijection. The
normalized product measure $\mu$ is $\mu_{\mathbb T}\otimes\mu_{\mathbb T}\otimes\mu_{\mathbb T}$,
where $\mu_{\mathbb T}$ is the normalized measure of
[[def-the-one-dimensional-torus-and-normalized-haar-integral]] transported by
$t\mapsto2\pi t$; it is a probability measure on the Borel sets of
$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ and $\int f\,d\mu=(2\pi)^{-3}\int_{[0,2\pi)^3}f\circ q\,d\lambda_3$
for bounded measurable $f$ ([[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]).

**(b) Test functions and continuous classes.** For $N\ge1$ let
$C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be the set of compositions
$u\circ q$ of smooth maps $u:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^N$ that are $2\pi$-periodic
in each variable; these are the **smooth test functions** (real-valued when
$N=1$). For $m\ge0$ let $C^m(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be the set of
$u\circ q$ with $u\in C^m(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^N)$ $2\pi$-periodic in each
variable ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]), with
$$\|u\|_{C^m}:=\max_{|\alpha|\le m}\ \sup_{x\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}\bigl|(D^\alpha u)(x)\bigr| ,$$
where $D^\alpha$ is the multi-index derivative of
[[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]] applied to any
periodic representative; the displayed expression is independent of the
representative.

**(c) The Hilbert space $L^2$.** For $N\ge1$ let
$L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be the quotient of the set of measurable
$u$ with $\int|u|^2\,d\mu<\infty$ by the $\mu$-a.e. zero functions
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[thm-the-l-p-norm-descends-to-the-quotient-and-makes-l-p-a-normed-space]]),
with inner product $\langle u,v\rangle_2=\int u\cdot v\,d\mu$ and norm
$\|u\|_2=\langle u,u\rangle_2^{1/2}$; it is a real Hilbert space
([[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]). For
$u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ and $k\in\mathbb Z^3$ the
**$k$-th Fourier coefficient** is the vector
$$\widehat u(k):=\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}u(x)\,e^{-ik\cdot x}\,d\mu(x)\in\mathbb C^N ,$$
where $e^{-ik\cdot x}:=\chi_{-k}$ with $\chi_k([x]):=\exp(i\,k\cdot x)$; here
$u$ is read through any representative. Write $\chi_k:\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\to\mathbb C$,
$k\in\mathbb Z^3$, for these **characters**; under the identification
$x=2\pi y$ they are the characters $\exp(2\pi i\,k\cdot y)$ of
[[thm-fourier-basis-and-parseval-on-the-n-torus]], so $(\chi_k)_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}$
is an orthonormal basis of the complex space $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb C)$.

**(d) Weak derivatives and the periodic Sobolev spaces.** For
$u,v\in L^1(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$ and $\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^3$ say that
$v$ is the **weak derivative** $D^\alpha u$ if
$$\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,d\mu=(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}v\,\varphi\,d\mu$$
for every $\varphi\in C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$, where $D^\alpha\varphi$
is the multi-index derivative of the periodic representative
([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]] records the
Euclidean analogue). For an integer $s\ge0$ let
$$H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N):=\Bigl\{u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N):\ \text{for every }|\alpha|\le s\text{ there is }v_\alpha\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)\text{ with }v_\alpha=D^\alpha u\Bigr\},$$
the vector-valued weak derivative being componentwise, and put
$$\|u\|_{H^s}:=\Bigl(\sum_{|\alpha|\le s}\|D^\alpha u\|_2^2\Bigr)^{1/2}.$$
The classes $L^2\subseteq L^1$ on the probability space, so the integrals in the
test identity are finite: $|\int u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,d\mu|\le\|u\|_2\|D^\alpha\varphi\|_2$
by Cauchy--Schwarz. The definition asserts neither that the weak derivative
exists nor that the two norms compared in the next item are equivalent; those
are proved in [[lem-gr-periodic-fourier-differentiation-and-norm-equivalence]].

**(e) Conventions.** $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ open, $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ an
interval and maps $F:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\mathbb R^{m'}$ are
called smooth when their representatives $F(t,q(x),u)=G(t,x,u)$ have
$G\in C^\infty$. Throughout this page the torus is always this
$2\pi$-periodic one; a statement "for every $x$" means for every point of
$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, and "a.e." means $\mu$-a.e.

derivations.claim: (The limit is in $H^s$ with the uniform bound (a).) Fix $t$. For every finite $F\subseteq\mathbb Z^3$, [L7] gives $\sum_{k\in F}(1+|k|^2)^s|\widehat u(t)(k)|^2=\lim_j\sum_{k\in F}(1+|k|^2)^s|\widehat{u_{N_j}(t)}(k)|^2\le R_1^2$; taking the supremum over finite $F$ gives $N_s(u(t))^2\le R_1^2$, so $u(t)\in H^s$ and $\|u(t)\|_{H^s}\le C_sR_1$ by the norm equivalence, the bound being uniform in $t$. Values in $K_1$ and continuity into $H^{s-1}$ follow from [L1]. This is (a).

(A convergent subsequence of the time derivatives.) Put $g_j:=\partial_tu_{N_j}$. By [L4] the family is bounded in $H^{s-1}$ and Lipschitz in $H^{s-2}$; by [L5] there is a strictly increasing $j_n$ with $g_{j_n}\to g$ uniformly on every compact subinterval of $(-T,T)$ in $H^{s-2}$, for some $g\in C^0((-T,T);H^{s-2})$. Discarding the complementary terms, rename the subsequence by $N_j$: still $u_{N_j}\to u$ on compact subintervals in $H^{s-1}$ and now $g_j\to g$ on compact subintervals in $H^{s-2}$.

(The time derivative (b).) (i) Let $\psi\in C_c^\infty((-T,T))$ and $v\in H^{s-2}$; put $J':=\operatorname{supp}\psi$. By [L6], $\int_{J'}\psi'(t)\langle u_{N_j}(t),v\rangle dt=-\int_{J'}\psi(t)\langle g_j(t),v\rangle dt$ for every $j$; by step 1.2 the limits $\int_{J'}\psi'\langle u,v\rangle dt$ and $\int_{J'}\psi\langle g,v\rangle dt$ are attained uniformly on $J'$, so $\int\psi'\langle u,v\rangle dt=-\int\psi\langle g,v\rangle dt$. Hence the $H^{s-2}$-valued distributional derivative $\partial_tu$ equals the class of $g$. (ii) Fix $t$; by step 1.2, $\widehat{g_j(t)}(k)\to\widehat g(t)(k)$ for every $k$ [L7], so for every finite $K\subseteq\mathbb Z^3$ the finite sums $\sum_{k\in K}(1+|k|^2)^{s-1}|\widehat{g_j(t)}(k)|^2$ are at most $c_{s-1}^{-1}\|g_j(t)\|_{H^{s-1}}^2\le c_{s-1}^{-1}C_{R_1}^2$ by [L4]; passing to the limit and taking the supremum over finite $K$ gives $N_{s-1}(g(t))^2\le c_{s-1}^{-1}C_{R_1}^2$, so $g(t)\in H^{s-1}$ with $\|g(t)\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C_{s-1}^{1/2}c_{s-1}^{-1/2}C_{R_1}$ by [L7]. Thus $\partial_tu$ is represented by the function $g\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^{s-1})$, uniformly bounded as asserted. This is (b).

(The limit solves the equation distributionally (c), first part.) Let $\psi\in C^\infty((-T,T)\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ have compact support in $t$. Testing the Galerkin equation [L2] with $\psi$ and using self-adjointness of $P_{N_j}$ gives $\int\!\!\int\psi^{\mathsf T}[A^0(u_{N_j})\partial_tu_{N_j}+A^i(u_{N_j})\partial_iu_{N_j}+B(u_{N_j})]=\int\!\!\int(\psi-P_{N_j}\psi)^{\mathsf T}[\cdots]$, and the right-hand side tends to $0$ because $\psi-P_{N_j}\psi\to0$ in $L^2$ [L2] while the bracket is bounded in $L^\infty L^2$ by [L3] and [L4]. On the left, all factors converge on the compact $t$-support of $\psi$: $A^0(u_{N_j})\to A^0(u)$, $A^i(u_{N_j})\to A^i(u)$ and $B(u_{N_j})\to B(u)$ uniformly by [L1]; $\partial_iu_{N_j}\to\partial_iu$ uniformly by [L1]; and $\partial_tu_{N_j}=g_j\to g=\partial_tu$ uniformly in $H^{s-2}\subseteq L^2$ by step 1.2 and step 2.1; hence the limit is $\int\!\!\int\psi^{\mathsf T}[A^0(u)\partial_tu+A^i(u)\partial_iu+B(u)]=0$ for every test $\psi$, which is the distributional form of $(\star)$.

(Classical regularity and initial value.) From the distributional equation of step 3.1, $\partial_tu=-(A^0(t,\cdot,u))^{-1}[A^i(t,\cdot,u)\partial_iu+B(t,\cdot,u)]$ as $H^{s-2}$-valued distributions; the right-hand side agrees with the continuous function $g=\partial_tu\in C^0((-T,T);H^{s-2})$ as a distribution, so the classical identity $\partial_tu(t)=-(A^0(t,\cdot,u(t)))^{-1}[A^i(t,\cdot,u(t))\partial_iu(t)+B(t,\cdot,u(t))]$ holds for every $t$, both sides being continuous in $t$. The right-hand side is continuous in $(t,x)$: indeed $u\in C^0H^{s-1}$ gives $\partial_iu\in C^0H^{s-2}\subseteq C^0$ with $s-2>3/2$; the inverse coefficient is continuous by [L3]; hence $\partial_tu$ has a continuous representative in $(t,x)$. Therefore $t\mapsto u(t)$ is $C^1$ into $H^{s-2}$ with continuous derivative and the first spatial derivatives are continuous, so $u\in C^1((-T,T)\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi})$ and $(\star)$ holds pointwise. Finally $u_{N_j}(0)=P_{N_j}u_0\to u_0$ in $H^{s-1}$ and $u_{N_j}(0)\to u(0)$ by the convergence of step 1.2, so $u(0)=u_0$.

citations.quote:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
signature $(-+++)$ and metric-selected connection $\nabla$, and let $(\rho,u)$
be a dust model on an open matter domain $U_0\subseteq M$
([[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]), so $\rho>0$ is the rest density,
$u$ is the future-directed unit timelike four-velocity and
$T^{ab}=\rho u^au^b$. Fix a constant $c>0$ (the speed of light of the
framework, [[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]) and make the following
**reduction conventions**, all local to an open set $U\subseteq U_0$:

**(a) Signature flip.** Put $\gamma:=-g$, a smooth metric of signature
$(+---)$ on $U$, with inverse $\gamma^{-1}=-g^{-1}$; all indices in the
reduction are raised and lowered with $\gamma$
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]). Put
$$U:=u,\qquad r:=\rho c^2 .$$
Then $\gamma(U,U)=1$, and the Einstein equation of the framework reads
$G(\gamma)-\Lambda\gamma=\kappa\,r\,U^\flat_\gamma\otimes U^\flat_\gamma$ with
the same constant $\kappa$ and the Einstein tensor of $\gamma$
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). The original metric and
frame connection are recovered by the constant signs $g=-\gamma$; no physical
equation is changed.

**(b) Orthonormal frame.** Choose a smooth orthonormal frame
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ on $U$ with $e_0=U$ and
$\gamma(e_i,e_j)=\eta_{ij}:=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1)_{ij}$
([[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]], [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]).
Its connection coefficients are defined by
$$\nabla_ie_j=\Gamma_i{}^k{}_j\,e_k,\qquad \Gamma_{ijk}:=\gamma_{kl}\Gamma_i{}^l{}_j=-\Gamma_{ikj},$$
and the frame components of $U$ are $U^i=\delta^i_0$.
The **spatial projection** onto the $\gamma$-orthogonal complement of $U$ and the tensor
$$h_{ij}:=\gamma_{ij}-U_iU_j,\qquad l_{ij}:=h_{ij}-U_iU_j$$
coincide with $\gamma$-orthogonal projection onto $\operatorname{span}(e_1,e_2,e_3)$
when restricted to spatial pairs.

**(c) Kinematics.** With $\nabla$ the metric connection of $\gamma$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) put
$$\chi_{ij}:=h_i{}^k\nabla_kU_j,\qquad \chi:=h^{ij}\chi_{ij},\qquad \chi^{ij}:=h^{ik}h^{jl}\chi_{kl},$$
and let $D$ denote fully projected covariant differentiation: for a spatial
tensor field $T$, $(DT)_{i\ldots}:=(h_i{}^j\cdots)\nabla_j(T_\ldots)$, so
$D_ih_{jk}=0$ and $D_i\epsilon_{jkl}=0$. Let $\epsilon_{ijkl}$ be the
$\gamma$-volume tensor with $\epsilon_{0123}=1$ and set
$\epsilon_{ijk}:=\epsilon_{0ijk}$ (so $\epsilon_{123}=1$).

**(d) Comoving-parallel gauge.** Assume the coordinates
$(x^0=s,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ on $U$ are **comoving** ($e_0=\partial_s$ and $x^\alpha$
constant along the flow lines of $e_0$, $s$ a parameter on them) and
**parallel** ($\Gamma_0{}^i{}_j=0$, i.e. the spatial frame is parallelly
transported along $U$). This gauge is admissible for tilted configurations: the
initial surface $s=0$ is the given spacelike surface and need not be orthogonal
to $U$.

**(e) Unknowns.** The unknowns of the reduction are the coefficients
$$u_{\mathrm{red}}:=\bigl(e_a{}^\mu,\ \Gamma_a{}^i{}_j,\ E_{ij},\ B_{ij},\ r\bigr),\qquad a=1,2,3,$$
where $E$ and $B$ are the electric and magnetic parts of the Weyl curvature
defined in [[def-gr-dust-electric-magnetic-weyl-variables-and-schouten]]; the transport,
evolution and subsidiary equations they satisfy are stated and derived in
[[def-gr-dust-electric-magnetic-weyl-variables-and-schouten]],
[[lem-gr-dust-reduced-evolution-equations]],
[[lem-gr-dust-symmetric-hyperbolic-reduction]] and
[[thm-gr-dust-subsidiary-and-residual-vanishing]].

Work in the reduction conventions of
[[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]]: $\gamma$ is the signature
$(+---)$ metric, $U$ the unit future timelike vector $U=n$, $r=\rho c^2$, the
frame $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ is $\gamma$-orthonormal with $e_0=U$,
$\gamma(e_i,e_j)=\eta_{ij}$ on spatial pairs, and indices are moved with
$\gamma$.

**(a) Schouten tensor.** The **reduction Schouten tensor** of $\gamma$ is
$$S_{ij}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ij}-\tfrac16S_\gamma\,\gamma_{ij},$$
where $\operatorname{Ric}$ and $S_\gamma=\gamma^{ab}\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ are
the Ricci tensor and scalar curvature of $\gamma$
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). If the dust field equation
$G(\gamma)-\Lambda\gamma=\kappa\,r\,U^\flat\otimes U^\flat$ holds, then
$$S_{ij}=\kappa r\Bigl(U_iU_j-\tfrac13\gamma_{ij}\Bigr)-\tfrac13\Lambda\,\gamma_{ij}.$$
This normalization is fixed so that the standard Kulkarni--Nomizu decomposition
$$R_{ijkl}=C_{ijkl}+\tfrac12\bigl(S_{ik}\gamma_{jl}-S_{il}\gamma_{jk}+S_{jl}\gamma_{ik}-S_{jk}\gamma_{il}\bigr)$$
holds for every metric of dimension four, with $C$ the Weyl tensor
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]); the identity is checked on
constant-curvature metrics in the Remarks.

**(b) Prescribed curvature.** The **prescribed curvature tensor** of a
configuration $(C,E,B,r)$ is the tensor field with frame components
$$R^{\mathrm{pre}}{}_{ijkl}:=C_{ijkl}+\tfrac12\bigl(S_{ik}\gamma_{jl}-S_{il}\gamma_{jk}+S_{jl}\gamma_{ik}-S_{jk}\gamma_{il}\bigr),\qquad S_{ij}\text{ as in (a)} ,$$
where $C=C[E,B]$ is the Weyl tensor reconstructed from the electric and
magnetic variables in (d). A **reduced configuration** is a smooth assignment
$(e_a{}^\mu,\Gamma_a{}^i{}_j,E_{ij},B_{ij},r)$ in the gauge of
[[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]] such that the actual curvature
tensor of the tentative frame connection equals $R^{\mathrm{pre}}$; the reduced
evolution system that enforces this is derived in
[[lem-gr-dust-reduced-evolution-equations]].

**(c) Electric and magnetic Weyl variables.** For a smooth Weyl-type tensor $C$
of type $(0,4)$ with the curvature symmetries write
$C^*{}_{ijkl}:=\tfrac12C_{ij}{}^{pq}\epsilon_{klpq}$ for its right dual
([[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]] clause (c) for
$\epsilon_{ijkl}$). The **electric and magnetic parts with respect to $U$** are
the spatial fields
$$E_{ij}:=C_{0i0j},\qquad B_{ij}:=C^*{}_{0i0j},$$
with frame indices; they are symmetric and spatial in all indices and
trace-free with respect to $h$ whenever $C$ has the Weyl symmetries.

**(d) Reconstruction formula.** Define the dependent tensor
$$C_{ijkl}:=2\bigl(l_{j[k}E_{l]i}-l_{i[k}E_{l]j}\bigr)-2\bigl(U_{[k}B_{l]p}\epsilon^p{}_{ij}+U_{[i}B_{j]p}\epsilon^p{}_{kl}\bigr),$$
with brackets of weight $\tfrac12$ and $l_{ij}=h_{ij}-U_iU_j$; this expression
is the **reconstruction** of a Weyl tensor from a pair $(E,B)$ of symmetric
spatial trace-free fields. The verification that the reconstructed tensor has
the curvature antisymmetries, pair symmetry, cyclic identity and zero traces —
and that its electric and magnetic parts recover $(E,B)$ — is the content of
[[lem-gr-dust-weyl-reconstruction-from-electric-magnetic]].

The definition fixes the objects and conventions only; the evolution and
subsidiary equations, the initial-data determination and the local existence
theorem are proved in the items named above and in
[[lem-gr-dust-reduced-evolution-equations]] and
[[thm-gr-dust-local-evolution]].

derivations.claim: (Skew-adjointness (a).) Compute $\langle C(\xi)B,B'\rangle=\epsilon_{kl(i}\xi^kB_{j)}{}^lB'^{ij}$. Using the symmetry of $B,B'$ to symmetrize the $i,j$ pair and the epsilon identity [L1], this equals $-\epsilon_{kl(i}\xi^kB'_{j)}{}^lB^{ij}=-\langle B,C(\xi)B'\rangle$.

(Norm bound (b).) By [L2], $C(\xi)$ is the average of the actions on the two slots of the skew-adjoint rotation $A(\xi)$, which has operator norm $|\xi|$ on each slot; the norm of the sum of two contractions is at most the sum of the norms, so $\|C(\xi)\|\le\tfrac12(|\xi|+|\xi|)=|\xi|$.

(Blocks and positivity (c), (d).) Self-adjointness of the block follows from (a): its adjoint is $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&-C(\xi)^*\\C(\xi)^*&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&C(\xi)\\-C(\xi)&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. For (d), [L3] gives that the quadratic form of the symbol matrix is at least $z-\|C(\zeta_\perp)\|\ge z-|\zeta_\perp|>0$ on unit vectors, so the time matrix is positive definite; a future-positive timelike conormal satisfies $z>\vert\zeta_\perp\vert$ by the standard covector classification. Combining with the transport and algebraic blocks of [[lem-gr-dust-reduced-evolution-equations]] gives the symmetric hyperbolic form of the reduced dust system. [step 1.1, step 1.2, L3, algebra] ∎



- **Role.** This is the symbol-theoretic core of the dust hyperbolicity claim; it is independent of the metric dynamics and is a finite-dimensional linear-algebra statement.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
signature $(-+++)$ and metric-selected connection $\nabla$, and let $(\rho,u)$
be a dust model on an open matter domain $U_0\subseteq M$
([[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]), so $\rho>0$ is the rest density,
$u$ is the future-directed unit timelike four-velocity and
$T^{ab}=\rho u^au^b$. Fix a constant $c>0$ (the speed of light of the
framework, [[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]) and make the following
**reduction conventions**, all local to an open set $U\subseteq U_0$:

**(a) Signature flip.** Put $\gamma:=-g$, a smooth metric of signature
$(+---)$ on $U$, with inverse $\gamma^{-1}=-g^{-1}$; all indices in the
reduction are raised and lowered with $\gamma$
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]). Put
$$U:=u,\qquad r:=\rho c^2 .$$
Then $\gamma(U,U)=1$, and the Einstein equation of the framework reads
$G(\gamma)-\Lambda\gamma=\kappa\,r\,U^\flat_\gamma\otimes U^\flat_\gamma$ with
the same constant $\kappa$ and the Einstein tensor of $\gamma$
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). The original metric and
frame connection are recovered by the constant signs $g=-\gamma$; no physical
equation is changed.

**(b) Orthonormal frame.** Choose a smooth orthonormal frame
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ on $U$ with $e_0=U$ and
$\gamma(e_i,e_j)=\eta_{ij}:=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1)_{ij}$
([[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]], [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]).
Its connection coefficients are defined by
$$\nabla_ie_j=\Gamma_i{}^k{}_j\,e_k,\qquad \Gamma_{ijk}:=\gamma_{kl}\Gamma_i{}^l{}_j=-\Gamma_{ikj},$$
and the frame components of $U$ are $U^i=\delta^i_0$.
The **spatial projection** onto the $\gamma$-orthogonal complement of $U$ and the tensor
$$h_{ij}:=\gamma_{ij}-U_iU_j,\qquad l_{ij}:=h_{ij}-U_iU_j$$
coincide with $\gamma$-orthogonal projection onto $\operatorname{span}(e_1,e_2,e_3)$
when restricted to spatial pairs.

**(c) Kinematics.** With $\nabla$ the metric connection of $\gamma$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) put
$$\chi_{ij}:=h_i{}^k\nabla_kU_j,\qquad \chi:=h^{ij}\chi_{ij},\qquad \chi^{ij}:=h^{ik}h^{jl}\chi_{kl},$$
and let $D$ denote fully projected covariant differentiation: for a spatial
tensor field $T$, $(DT)_{i\ldots}:=(h_i{}^j\cdots)\nabla_j(T_\ldots)$, so
$D_ih_{jk}=0$ and $D_i\epsilon_{jkl}=0$. Let $\epsilon_{ijkl}$ be the
$\gamma$-volume tensor with $\epsilon_{0123}=1$ and set
$\epsilon_{ijk}:=\epsilon_{0ijk}$ (so $\epsilon_{123}=1$).

**(d) Comoving-parallel gauge.** Assume the coordinates
$(x^0=s,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ on $U$ are **comoving** ($e_0=\partial_s$ and $x^\alpha$
constant along the flow lines of $e_0$, $s$ a parameter on them) and
**parallel** ($\Gamma_0{}^i{}_j=0$, i.e. the spatial frame is parallelly
transported along $U$). This gauge is admissible for tilted configurations: the
initial surface $s=0$ is the given spacelike surface and need not be orthogonal
to $U$.

**(e) Unknowns.** The unknowns of the reduction are the coefficients
$$u_{\mathrm{red}}:=\bigl(e_a{}^\mu,\ \Gamma_a{}^i{}_j,\ E_{ij},\ B_{ij},\ r\bigr),\qquad a=1,2,3,$$
where $E$ and $B$ are the electric and magnetic parts of the Weyl curvature
defined in [[def-gr-dust-electric-magnetic-weyl-variables-and-schouten]]; the transport,
evolution and subsidiary equations they satisfy are stated and derived in
[[def-gr-dust-electric-magnetic-weyl-variables-and-schouten]],
[[lem-gr-dust-reduced-evolution-equations]],
[[lem-gr-dust-symmetric-hyperbolic-reduction]] and
[[thm-gr-dust-subsidiary-and-residual-vanishing]].

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $r,s\ge0$ be integers.

**(a) Tensors at a point.** For $p\in M$, the tangent space $T_pM$ is the real
vector space of derivations at $p$
([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]) and the cotangent space is
its algebraic dual, $T_p^*M=(T_pM)^*$
([[def-cotangent-space-and-cotangent-bundle-as-a-disjoint-union]]). A **type
$(r,s)$ tensor at $p$** is a multilinear map

$$T_p:(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\longrightarrow\mathbb R,$$

in the sense of [[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]:
the first $r$ arguments are covectors and the last $s$ are vectors. In
particular a type $(1,0)$ tensor is a vector, a type $(0,1)$ tensor is a
covector and a type $(0,2)$ tensor is a bilinear form, so the covariant
$2$-tensors of [[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]] are exactly the
type $(0,2)$ tensors of this definition.

**(b) The tensor bundle and smooth fields.** The **type $(r,s)$ tensor bundle**
$T^r_sM$ is the disjoint union of the fibres $T^r_sM|_p=\operatorname{Mult}((T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s,\mathbb R)$
over $p\in M$ ([[def-type-r-s-tensor-bundle]]); it carries the smooth
vector-bundle structure defined by the tensor-coordinate change rules
([[thm-tensor-transition-laws-define-a-smooth-vector-bundle]]). A **smooth
tensor field of type $(r,s)$** on $M$ is a family $T=(T_p)_{p\in M}$ assigning
to each $p$ a type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$, such that for every smooth chart
$(U,x)$ of the maximal smooth atlas the **component functions**

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}(q):=T_q\bigl(dx^{a_1}|_q,\dots,dx^{a_r}|_q,\ \partial_{b_1}|_q,\dots,\partial_{b_s}|_q\bigr),\qquad q\in U,$$

are $C^\infty$ on $U$; here the coordinate derivations
$\partial_b|_q=\partial/\partial x^b|_q$ form a basis of $T_qM$
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]) and the
coordinate differentials $dx^a|_q$ form the dual basis of $T_q^*M$
([[thm-coordinate-differentials-form-the-dual-cotangent-basis]]). This is
equivalent to $T$ being a smooth section of $T^r_sM$ in the sense of
[[def-smooth-tensor-field]]: the component functions are the frame
coefficients of the section in the local frame induced by the chart. The
smoothness condition is independent of the chosen smooth atlas and the
components in two overlapping charts are related by the transformation law
proved in the lemma on this page; the definition is therefore chart
independent rather than merely chart-wise.

**(c) Index conventions.** Indices are written $a,b,c,\dots$ for components in
a chart, with the Einstein summation convention: a repeated index, once upper
and once lower, is summed over $0,1,2,3$. An upper index is a contravariant
slot in which a covector is evaluated, a lower index a covariant slot in which
a vector is evaluated. Slots are moved between these positions with the
musical isomorphisms $\flat_p,\sharp_p$ of
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]; for example, lowering the
first slot of a type $(1,1)$ field uses $(g^\flat T)^a{}_b=g_{ac}T^c{}_b$ and
raising uses $g^{ac}$. This is an identification of slots, not a change of the
field into a field of another kind, and it uses the metric nondegeneracy.

**(d) Scope.** The definition is purely local and chart-based; no global
triviality of $T^r_sM$, no global frame and no choice of metric-compatible
fields is assumed or implied. All fields are smooth ($C^\infty$); no
lower-regularity or distributional tensor field is defined here. The smooth
structure of the tangent bundle, and hence of $T^r_sM$
([[thm-tensor-transition-laws-define-a-smooth-vector-bundle]]), inherits the
axiom $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]] recorded with
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]; the component formulation of smoothness
itself makes no choice.

derivations.claim: (Rest-frame expansion (a).) Put all indices down with $\gamma$ and use [L1] to evaluate the four building blocks of the reconstruction: $l_{j[k}E_{l]i}$ is nonzero only for spatial indices, where $l_{jk}=-2\delta_{jk}$ (so these terms carry a factor $-2$ with the spatial Kronecker deltas); the terms $U_{[k}B_{l]p}\epsilon^p{}_{ij}$ are nonzero only when exactly one of $k,l$ is $0$ (since $U$ has only the $0$-component), in which case they contribute $\pm\tfrac12B_{?p}\epsilon^p{}_{ij}$. Antisymmetry in $(k,l)$ and in $(i,j)$ is manifest in the bracket notation; pair symmetry follows from the symmetry $E=E^{\mathsf T}$, $B=B^{\mathsf T}$, the antisymmetry $l_{ij}=l_{ji}$, the identity $\epsilon^p{}_{ij}=-\epsilon^p{}_{ji}$ and the two displayed terms being exchanged by $(ij)\leftrightarrow(kl)$ up to the sign convention of the last pair; the cyclic identity $C_{i[jkl]}=0$ is a finite check in the rest frame: it vanishes term by term separately for the $E$-terms and the $B$-terms by the three-dimensional Bianchi-type identity for symmetric trace-free spatial tensors. Trace-freeness: contracting over the pair $(i,j)$ uses $E^{ij}l_{ij}$-type contractions and [L2]; the algebraic identities of [L2] reduce every contraction either to $\gamma^{ij}E_{ij}$ (which vanishes in three spatial dimensions for the $E$-terms by the index symmetry, or is handled in (c) for the trace-free case) or to the same contraction of the other pair, so all traces vanish after symmetrization.

(Recovery of $E,B$ (b).) Set $i=0$ and $j$ spatial (no sum): the $E$-terms give $2l_{?[k}E_{l]}...$ evaluated with $l$ having a $0$-index only in $l_{00}=-1$, and the $B$-terms support exactly the mixed components; the result is $C_{0k0l}=E_{kl}$ in the frame. Similarly, since the right dual acts only on the last pair, $C^*{}_{0i0j}=\tfrac12C_{0i}{}^{pq}\epsilon_{jpq}$: substituting the reconstruction and using [L2] to contract the epsilon symbols produces $B_{ij}$, with the spatial trace terms cancelling by the elementary identity $\delta_{[k}{}^p\delta_{l]}{}^q\epsilon_{pqj}=-\epsilon_{klj}$.

(Bijection (c).) By (a) the reconstructed tensor has Weyl symmetries whenever it is trace-free in the sense of (a); the trace-freeness in the two index pairs is automatic from $E,B$ spatial; the remaining vanishing $C^{ij}{}_{ij}$-type traces impose exactly $\operatorname{tr}_hE=\operatorname{tr}_hB=0$, and then (a) applies with no qualification. The map $(E,B)\mapsto C$ is linear; (b) shows that the map from Weyl tensors to pairs $(E,B)$ is a left inverse on the image, and it is injective on the space of Weyl tensors because a Weyl tensor vanishes iff both its $U$-electric and $U$-magnetic parts vanish (a Weyl tensor with a vanishing electric part has $C_{0i0j}=0$, and with vanishing magnetic part has $C^*{}_{0i0j}=0$, which together with the Weyl symmetries force all components to vanish by the same index count). Hence it is a bijection onto the pairs with vanishing traces. [step 2.1, algebra] ∎



- **Role.** This item is the algebraic kernel of the dust reduction: it allows the Weyl curvature variable in the reduced system to be replaced by the pair $(E,B)$ without loss of information, and it justifies the reconstruction inserted into $R^{\mathrm{pre}}$.
- **Verification.** The bracket and index-symmetry checks above are finite rest-frame computations; no convergence or regularity statement is involved.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open,
let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric hyperbolic coefficient family on $O$ over
an open interval $I\ni0$ ([[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]]), let
$u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ take values in a compact
$K\subseteq O$ with $\|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R$, and let $P_N$, $X_N$ be the Galerkin
projection and space ([[def-gr-galerkin-fourier-projection]]). Then for every
$N\ge0$:

**(a)** there is an open interval $J_N\ni0$ and a $C^1$ map $u_N:J_N\to X_N$
such that for all $t\in J_N$
$$P_N\Bigl[A^0(t,\cdot,u_N(t))\,\partial_tu_N(t)+\sum_{i=1}^3A^i(t,\cdot,u_N(t))\,\partial_iu_N(t)+B(t,\cdot,u_N(t))\Bigr]=0\quad\text{in }L^2,$$
with $u_N(0)=P_Nu_0$;

**(b)** [continuation criterion] if $[0,T_*)$ is the forward-maximal interval of
existence of $u_N$ and there are a compact $C\subseteq O$ and a constant
$R_1\ge0$ with $u_N(t)$ taking values in $C$ and $\|u_N(t)\|_{H^s}\le R_1$ for
all $t\in[0,T_*)$, then $u_N$ does not have $T_*$ as a finite forward endpoint:
the solution extends beyond $T_*$;

**(c)** the solution is unique and its local flow depends smoothly on the
finite-dimensional coordinates of the initial data.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, $\mu$, $\chi_k$ and the
spaces $H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ be as in
[[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]] ($m\ge1$).

**(a) Mode sets.** For $N\ge0$ put
$\Lambda_N:=\{k\in\mathbb Z^3:|k|\le N\}$ with $|k|$ the Euclidean norm, and
$$X_N:=\Bigl\{\sum_{k\in\Lambda_N}a_k\chi_k:\ a_k\in\mathbb C^m,\ a_{-k}=\overline{a_k}\Bigr\}\subseteq C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m),$$
the **Galerkin space of modes up to $N$**; it is a finite-dimensional real
vector space of dimension $d_N:=m\,|\Lambda_N|$, and $X_N\subseteq X_{N'}$ for
$N\le N'$. (The reality condition $a_{-k}=\overline{a_k}$ is exactly the
condition that the trigonometric polynomial be real-valued.)

**(b) Projection.** For $u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ define
$$P_Nu:=\sum_{k\in\Lambda_N}\widehat u(k)\chi_k,\qquad (P_Nu)(x)=\sum_{k\in\Lambda_N}\widehat u(k)\chi_k(x),$$
with $\widehat u(k)$ the Fourier coefficients of clause (c) of
[[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]]; the second expression is a finite
sum, so $P_Nu\in X_N$; and $P_N:X_N\to X_N$ is the identity.
$P_N$ is called the **Galerkin (Fourier) projection**.

The definition fixes the projection only. Its self-adjointness,
derivative-commutation and operator-norm properties are proved in
[[lem-gr-galerkin-projection-properties]].

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, let
$K\subseteq O$ be compact and $R\ge0$, and let $u_N:J\to X_N$ be a Galerkin
solution ([[lem-gr-galerkin-ode-local-solution]]) with $u_N(t)$ taking values
in $K$ and $\|u_N(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$ for all $t\in J$. Define the **weighted
energy**
$$e(t):=\sum_{|\alpha|\le s}\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}\bigl(D^\alpha u_N(t)\bigr)^{\mathsf T}A^0\bigl(t,x,u_N(t)\bigr)\bigl(D^\alpha u_N(t)\bigr)\,d\mu(x).$$
Then:

**(a)** there are $0<a\le b$, depending on $A^0$, $K$ and $s$, with
$a\|u_N(t)\|_{H^s}^2\le e(t)\le b\|u_N(t)\|_{H^s}^2$ for all $t\in J$;

**(b)** $e$ is $C^1$ on $J$ and there is $C=C(A^\mu,B,K,R,s)$ with
$$e'(t)\le C\,\bigl(1+e(t)\bigr)\qquad(t\in J).$$
Consequently $e(t)\le(1+e(0))e^{C|t|}$ for $t\in J$ by Gronwall's inequality.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$
([[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]]), let $K\subseteq O$ be compact
and $R\ge0$, and let $u_N:J\to X_N$ be a Galerkin solution of
[[lem-gr-galerkin-ode-local-solution]] for some $N\ge0$. Suppose that
$u_N(t)$ takes values in $K$ and satisfies $\|u_N(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$ for every
$t\in J$. Then there is $C=C(A^\mu,B,K,R,s)$ such that for every
$0\le j\le s-1$ and every $t\in J$
$$\|\partial_tu_N(t)\|_{H^j}\le C\,\bigl(1+\|u_N(t)\|_{H^s}\bigr).$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]).

**(a)** For every integer $r\ge1$, every $R\ge0$ and every sequence $(v_j)$
in $H^r(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ with $\|v_j\|_{H^r}\le R$ there is a
subsequence converging in $H^{r-1}(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$.

**(b)** Let $s\ge5$, $R\ge0$, $T>0$, let $K\subseteq O$ be compact, and let
$u_N:(-T,T)\to X_N$ ($N=0,1,2,\dots$) be a family of Galerkin solutions with
$u_N(t)$ taking values in $K$ and $\|u_N(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$ for all $t$. Then the
family is equicontinuous in the $H^{s-1}$ metric: there is
$C_0=C_0(A^\mu,B,K,R,s)$ with
$$\|u_N(t)-u_N(t')\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C_0\,|t-t'|\qquad(t,t'\in(-T,T),\ N\ge0).$$

**(c)** Under the hypotheses of (b) there are a strictly increasing sequence
$N_j\to\infty$ and $u\in C^0((-T,T);H^{s-1}(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m))$
with $u_{N_j}\to u$ uniformly on every compact subinterval of $(-T,T)$ in the
$H^{s-1}$ norm.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, let
$K\subseteq K_1\subseteq O$ be compact, let $R\ge0$, and let
$u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ take values in $K$ with
$\|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R$. Let $T>0$, let $N_j\to\infty$ be strictly
increasing, and let $u_{N_j}:(-T,T)\to X_{N_j}$ be Galerkin solutions with
$u_{N_j}(0)=P_{N_j}u_0$, values in $K_1$ and $\|u_{N_j}(t)\|_{H^s}\le R_1$ for
all $t$, such that $u_{N_j}\to u$ uniformly on every compact subinterval of
$(-T,T)$ in $H^{s-1}$ (as provided by [[lem-gr-galerkin-compactness]] clauses
(b) and (c)). Then:

**(a)** $u(t)\in H^s$ for every $t$ and $\|u(t)\|_{H^s}\le C_{R_1}$ with
$C_{R_1}$ independent of $t$; $u$ takes values in $K_1$; and
$u\in C^0((-T,T);H^{s-1})\cap L^\infty((-T,T);H^s)$;

**(b)** the distributional time derivative $\partial_tu$ is represented by a
function in $L^\infty((-T,T);H^{s-1})$ and
$\|\partial_tu\|_{L^\infty H^{s-1}}\le C(C_{R_1})$;

**(c)** $u$ satisfies the system $(\star)$ of
[[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]] in the sense of Sobolev
solutions, and in fact $u\in C^1((-T,T)\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi})$ and solves
$(\star)$ classically with $u(0)=u_0$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let integers $s\ge m\ge0$ satisfy $s-m>3/2$, and
let $u\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ with the objects and notation of
[[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]]. Then:

**(a)** There is a unique representative $u^*\in C^m(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$
of the class $u$, and for every $|\alpha|\le m$ the series
$\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(ik)^\alpha\widehat u(k)\chi_k$ converges absolutely and
uniformly on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ to $D^\alpha u^*$; moreover there is
$C=C(s,m,N)$ with
$$\|u^*\|_{C^m}\le C\,\|u\|_{H^s}.$$

**(b)** Writing $d(x,y):=\min\{\,|x-y+2\pi l|:l\in\mathbb Z^3\,\}$ for the
induced metric on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ and fixing
$0<\theta\le\min\{1,s-m-\tfrac32\}$, there is $C'=C'(s,m,N,\theta)$ with
$$\bigl|D^\alpha u^*(x)-D^\alpha u^*(y)\bigr|\le C'\,\|u\|_{H^s}\,d(x,y)^\theta\qquad(x,y\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi},\ |\alpha|\le m).$$

**(c)** The assignment $u\mapsto u^*$ is linear; and if $(u_j)$ is a sequence in
$H^s$ with $u_j\to u$ in $H^s$, then $u_j^*\to u^*$ uniformly together with all
derivatives of order at most $m$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $m\ge1$, $N\ge0$, and let $P_N$ be the Galerkin
projection and $X_N$ the Galerkin space of [[def-gr-galerkin-fourier-projection]]
on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$. Then:

**(a)** $P_N$ is linear on $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$, self-adjoint
($\langle P_Nu,v\rangle_2=\langle u,P_Nv\rangle_2$ for all $u,v\in L^2$) and
idempotent ($P_N^2=P_N$), with range $X_N$ and kernel the classes with vanishing
coefficients on $\Lambda_N$;

**(b)** for every multi-index $\alpha$ with $|\alpha|\le s$ and every
$u\in H^s$, $P_ND^\alpha u=D^\alpha P_Nu$;

**(c)** for every $0\le r\le s$ and every $u\in H^r$,
$\|P_Nu\|_{H^r}\le\|u\|_{H^r}$;

**(d)** for every $0\le r\le s$ and every $u\in H^r$, $P_Nu\to u$ in $H^r$ as
$N\to\infty$;

**(e)** for every $s\ge1$, every $u\in H^s$ and every $N\ge0$,
$$\|u-P_Nu\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C_s\,(1+N^2)^{-1/2}\,\|u\|_{H^s}$$
with $C_s$ depending only on $s$.

derivations.claim: (Choice of constants.) Since $K\subseteq\operatorname{int}K'$, there is $\delta>0$ with $K+B(0,2\delta)\subseteq K'$, where $B(0,r)$ is the open ball in $\mathbb R^m$. Put $R_1:=C_1'(1+R)$, a bound for the energy inequality [L2] on the compact value set $K'$ which is larger than $R$; let $a,b,C_1$ be the constants of [L2] for $K'$ and $R_1$, and let $C_2$ be the constant of [L3] on the same sets. Choose $T>0$ so small that $(1+bR^2)e^{C_1T}\le aR_1^2$ and $TC_2(1+R_1)\le\delta$.

(Uniform existence of the Galerkin solutions on $(-T,T)$.) For $N\ge0$ let $u_N$ be the Galerkin solution with $u_N(0)=P_Nu_0$ [L1]. Suppose its forward-maximal interval were $[0,T_*)$ with $T_*<T$. As long as $0\le t<T_*$ and $u_N$ stays in $K'$ with $\|u_N\|_{H^s}\le R_1$, [L2] gives $e_N(t)\le(1+e_N(0))e^{C_1t}<aR_1^2$, hence $\|u_N(t)\|_{H^s}<R_1$; and [L3] with [L6] bounds the pointwise drift $|u_N(t,x)-u_N(0,x)|\le\int_0^t\sup|\partial_tu_N|\,ds\le TC_2(1+R_1)\le\delta$. If some $t_1\le T_*$ were the first time at which $u_N(t_1)$ leaves $K'$, then for all $s<t_1$ the trajectory lies in $K'$, so the estimates apply and give $|u_N(t_1,x)-u_N(0,x)|\le\delta$ for every $x$, placing $u_N(t_1)$ in $K+B(0,\delta)\subseteq K'$, a contradiction; hence values remain in $K'$ and the $H^s$ bound remains strict on $[0,T_*)$, so the continuation criterion [L1] contradicts a finite endpoint $T_*<T$. The backward direction is identical. Hence each $u_N$ exists on $(-T,T)$ with values in $K'$ and $\|u_N(t)\|_{H^s}\le R_1$, and $\|\partial_tu_N(t)\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C_2(1+R_1)$ by [L3].

(Extraction of a limit and conclusion.) By [L4] there is a subsequence $u_{N_j}\to u$ uniformly on every compact subinterval of $(-T,T)$ in $H^{s-1}$. By [L5] $u$ is a classical solution of $(\star)$ with $u(0)=u_0$, $u\in L^\infty H^s\cap C^0H^{s-1}$, $\partial_tu\in L^\infty H^{s-1}$, values in $K'$ and the bounds with constant $C=C(R)$ obtained from $R_1,C_2$. This is the asserted solution.

citations.quote:
Work in the reduction conventions of
[[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]], so a tentative frame
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$, its dual coframe $\theta^i$ and tentative connection
coefficients $\Gamma_i{}^k{}_j$ are given.

**(a) Connection forms.** The **connection $1$-forms** are
$\omega^i{}_j:=\Gamma_k{}^i{}_j\,\theta^k$, and the **torsion $2$-forms** and
**curvature $2$-forms** are the Cartan expressions
$$\Theta^i:=d\theta^i+\omega^i{}_j\wedge\theta^j,\qquad \Omega^i{}_j:=d\omega^i{}_j+\omega^i{}_k\wedge\omega^k{}_j .$$
The exterior derivatives are those of the frame-coordinate calculus, and the
wedge products are on the coframe; components are denoted
$\Theta^i=\tfrac12\Theta^i{}_{jk}\theta^j\wedge\theta^k$ and similarly for
$\Omega$. The actual curvature uses the frame bracket in its component formula:
$R^i{}_{jkl}=\partial_k\Gamma_l{}^i{}_j-\partial_l\Gamma_k{}^i{}_j+\Gamma_k{}^i{}_m\Gamma_l{}^m{}_j-\Gamma_l{}^i{}_m\Gamma_k{}^m{}_j-\Gamma_m{}^i{}_j\,[e_k,e_l]^m$,
not the antisymmetrized connection coefficients alone, precisely so that no
torsion conclusion is assumed.

**(b) Curvature residual.** With the prescribed curvature $R^{\mathrm{pre}}$
of [[def-gr-dust-electric-magnetic-weyl-variables-and-schouten]] the
**curvature residual $2$-forms** are
$$\Delta^i{}_j:=\Omega^i{}_j-\tfrac12R^{\mathrm{pre}\,i}{}_{jkl}\,\theta^k\wedge\theta^l .$$

**(c) Zero quantities.** The **zero quantities** of the reduction are the
collections
$$z:=\bigl(T^i{}_{jk},\ \Delta^i{}_{jkl},\ F_{jkl},\ q_k\bigr),$$
namely the frame components of the torsion, of the curvature residual, of the
Bianchi residual $F_{jkl}=\nabla^i(C_{ijkl}+S\text{-terms})$ of
[[lem-gr-dust-reduced-evolution-equations]] and the flux quantity
$q_k:=\kappa^{-1}\nabla_aT^a{}_k$ of the matter model. The reduced system sets
$z=0$; the identities satisfied by $z$ off the reduced system, and the theorem
that $z=0$ on the domain of dependence of an initial surface on which $z=0$
and the constraints hold, are proved in
[[thm-gr-dust-subsidiary-and-residual-vanishing]].

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
signature $(-+++)$ and metric-selected connection $\nabla$, and let $(\rho,u)$
be a dust model on an open matter domain $U_0\subseteq M$
([[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]), so $\rho>0$ is the rest density,
$u$ is the future-directed unit timelike four-velocity and
$T^{ab}=\rho u^au^b$. Fix a constant $c>0$ (the speed of light of the
framework, [[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]) and make the following
**reduction conventions**, all local to an open set $U\subseteq U_0$:

**(a) Signature flip.** Put $\gamma:=-g$, a smooth metric of signature
$(+---)$ on $U$, with inverse $\gamma^{-1}=-g^{-1}$; all indices in the
reduction are raised and lowered with $\gamma$
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]). Put
$$U:=u,\qquad r:=\rho c^2 .$$
Then $\gamma(U,U)=1$, and the Einstein equation of the framework reads
$G(\gamma)-\Lambda\gamma=\kappa\,r\,U^\flat_\gamma\otimes U^\flat_\gamma$ with
the same constant $\kappa$ and the Einstein tensor of $\gamma$
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). The original metric and
frame connection are recovered by the constant signs $g=-\gamma$; no physical
equation is changed.

**(b) Orthonormal frame.** Choose a smooth orthonormal frame
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ on $U$ with $e_0=U$ and
$\gamma(e_i,e_j)=\eta_{ij}:=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1)_{ij}$
([[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]], [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]).
Its connection coefficients are defined by
$$\nabla_ie_j=\Gamma_i{}^k{}_j\,e_k,\qquad \Gamma_{ijk}:=\gamma_{kl}\Gamma_i{}^l{}_j=-\Gamma_{ikj},$$
and the frame components of $U$ are $U^i=\delta^i_0$.
The **spatial projection** onto the $\gamma$-orthogonal complement of $U$ and the tensor
$$h_{ij}:=\gamma_{ij}-U_iU_j,\qquad l_{ij}:=h_{ij}-U_iU_j$$
coincide with $\gamma$-orthogonal projection onto $\operatorname{span}(e_1,e_2,e_3)$
when restricted to spatial pairs.

**(c) Kinematics.** With $\nabla$ the metric connection of $\gamma$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) put
$$\chi_{ij}:=h_i{}^k\nabla_kU_j,\qquad \chi:=h^{ij}\chi_{ij},\qquad \chi^{ij}:=h^{ik}h^{jl}\chi_{kl},$$
and let $D$ denote fully projected covariant differentiation: for a spatial
tensor field $T$, $(DT)_{i\ldots}:=(h_i{}^j\cdots)\nabla_j(T_\ldots)$, so
$D_ih_{jk}=0$ and $D_i\epsilon_{jkl}=0$. Let $\epsilon_{ijkl}$ be the
$\gamma$-volume tensor with $\epsilon_{0123}=1$ and set
$\epsilon_{ijk}:=\epsilon_{0ijk}$ (so $\epsilon_{123}=1$).

**(d) Comoving-parallel gauge.** Assume the coordinates
$(x^0=s,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ on $U$ are **comoving** ($e_0=\partial_s$ and $x^\alpha$
constant along the flow lines of $e_0$, $s$ a parameter on them) and
**parallel** ($\Gamma_0{}^i{}_j=0$, i.e. the spatial frame is parallelly
transported along $U$). This gauge is admissible for tilted configurations: the
initial surface $s=0$ is the given spacelike surface and need not be orthogonal
to $U$.

**(e) Unknowns.** The unknowns of the reduction are the coefficients
$$u_{\mathrm{red}}:=\bigl(e_a{}^\mu,\ \Gamma_a{}^i{}_j,\ E_{ij},\ B_{ij},\ r\bigr),\qquad a=1,2,3,$$
where $E$ and $B$ are the electric and magnetic parts of the Weyl curvature
defined in [[def-gr-dust-electric-magnetic-weyl-variables-and-schouten]]; the transport,
evolution and subsidiary equations they satisfy are stated and derived in
[[def-gr-dust-electric-magnetic-weyl-variables-and-schouten]],
[[lem-gr-dust-reduced-evolution-equations]],
[[lem-gr-dust-symmetric-hyperbolic-reduction]] and
[[thm-gr-dust-subsidiary-and-residual-vanishing]].

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), whose existence and
uniqueness are supplied by
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; that theorem also
extends $\nabla$ to a derivative on tensor fields commuting with contractions
and annihilating $g$ and $g^{-1}$. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open and let
$X,Y,Z$ be smooth vector fields on $U$; brackets are those of
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]], and contractions those of
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]].

**(a) The curvature operator.** The **curvature operator** of $\nabla$ is the
assignment

$$R(X,Y)Z:=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z .$$

The right-hand side is a smooth vector field on $U$: $\nabla_YZ$ is smooth
because $\nabla$ is an affine connection
([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]), $[X,Y]$ is smooth, and
$\nabla_X(\cdot)$ and $\nabla_{[X,Y]}(\cdot)$ preserve smoothness. The
assignment is defined for the given smooth fields; that its value at a point
depends only on the values of $X,Y,Z$ at that point, so that $R$ is a smooth
tensor field of type $(1,3)$, is the content of
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a), and
likewise the algebraic symmetries used below are proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]].

**(b) Component functions.** Let $(V,x)$ be a smooth chart of $M$ and let
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ be the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in this chart,
characterized by $\nabla_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\sum_a\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]); the coordinate fields
commute, so $\nabla_{\partial_c}\partial_d$ and $\nabla_{\partial_d}\partial_c$
are obtained from the same symbols. The **components** of the curvature in the
chart are the smooth functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ on $V$ defined by

$$R(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=\sum_a R^a{}_{bcd}\,\partial_a .$$

The first index is the output slot, the second is the differentiated slot and
the last two are the two directions of the loop; indices are $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$
and the Einstein summation convention of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] applies.

**(c) Lowered tensor, Ricci tensor, scalar curvature, Einstein tensor.** On
the chart domain define, using the inverse metric
$g^{ab}$ of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],

$$R_{abcd}:=\sum_e g_{ae}R^e{}_{bcd},\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{bd}:=\sum_{a,c}g^{ac}R_{abcd},\qquad S:=\sum_{b,d}g^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}_{bd},\qquad G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 S\,g_{ab}.$$

The fields $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ are called
the **Riemann tensor with lowered indices**, the **Ricci tensor**, the
**scalar curvature** and the **Einstein tensor** of the metric-selected
connection. That $R_{abcd}$ are the components of a smooth $(0,4)$-tensor
field and that $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ are the components of a smooth
symmetric $(0,2)$-tensor field, so that the contractions above are
basis-independent and do not depend on the chart, is proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]] clauses (a)-(d); the Ricci symmetry
is part of that statement.

Work in the frame conventions of
[[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]] and let $E_{ij},B_{ij}$ be
symmetric spatial fields (i.e. $E_{ij}U^j=B_{ij}U^j=0$). Define $C$ by the
reconstruction formula of
[[def-gr-dust-electric-magnetic-weyl-variables-and-schouten]] clause (d). Then:

**(a)** $C_{ijkl}$ is antisymmetric in $(i,j)$ and in $(k,l)$, symmetric under
the exchange of the pairs $(ij)\leftrightarrow(kl)$, satisfies the first
Bianchi (cyclic) identity $C_{i[jkl]}=0$, and is trace-free in every pair of
contracted indices;

**(b)** the electric and magnetic parts of $C$ with respect to $U$ are
$C_{0i0j}=E_{ij}$ and $C^*{}_{0i0j}=B_{ij}$;

**(c)** consequently if $E,B$ are in addition trace-free with respect to $h$,
then $C$ is a Weyl tensor and the map $(E,B)\mapsto C$ is a bijection onto the
Weyl tensors with the given $U$-electric and $U$-magnetic parts.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\nabla$ be an affine connection
on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]). Smooth vector fields
are smooth sections of the tangent bundle
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]); as there, their use
rests on the canonical smooth structure of $TM$, which assumes the axiom
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]]. This is the only use of that
axiom in this definition.

**(a) Metric compatibility.** The connection $\nabla$ is **$g$-compatible**, or
**compatible with the metric** $g$, when for all smooth vector fields $X,Y,Z$ on
$M$ the identity of smooth functions

$$X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$$

holds on $M$. Here $g(Y,Z)$ is the smooth function $p\mapsto g_p(Y_p,Z_p)$ and
$X$ acts on functions as a derivation; the identity uses only the action of
$\nabla$ on vector fields and requires no extension of $\nabla$ to tensor
fields. When such an extension is available, this identity is the statement
$\nabla_Xg=0$, and the compatibility of $\nabla$ with the inverse metric
$g^{-1}$ follows; neither statement is part of this definition.

**(b) Torsion freedom.** The **torsion** of $\nabla$ is the tangent-valued
$2$-tensor $T(X,Y)=\nabla_XY-\nabla_YX-[X,Y]$ of
[[def-torsion-tensor-of-an-affine-connection]], with bracket as in
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]]. The connection is **torsion-free**
when $T(X,Y)=0$ for all smooth $X,Y$, that is, when
$\nabla_XY-\nabla_YX=[X,Y]$ identically.

**(c) Metric-selected connections.** A **metric-selected connection** for
$(M,g)$ is an affine connection on $M$ that is both torsion-free and
$g$-compatible. Equivalently, it is an element of the class

$$\operatorname{LC}(M,g):=\{\nabla:\nabla\text{ is an affine connection on }M,\ \nabla\text{ is torsion-free and }g\text{-compatible}\}.$$

The name records that the pair of conditions selects the connection out of all
affine connections; it is the pair of conditions imposed on the connection that
conventional general relativity uses, and the connection so selected is called
the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]],
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]). This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on the tensor bundles
of [[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]. Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

Let $V$ be the real vector space of symmetric $3\times3$ matrices with the
positive Frobenius product $\langle B,B'\rangle=B^{ij}B'_{ij}$, and for
$\xi\in\mathbb R^3$ define
$$C(\xi):V\to V,\qquad (C(\xi)B)_{ij}=\epsilon_{kl(i}\xi^kB_{j)}{}^l ,$$
with indices raised and lowered by the Euclidean metric and $\epsilon$ the
Levi-Civita symbol on the spatial frame of
[[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]]. Then:

**(a)** $C(\xi)$ is skew-adjoint: $\langle C(\xi)B,B'\rangle=-\langle B,C(\xi)B'\rangle$;

**(b)** $\|C(\xi)\|\le|\xi|$ for the operator norm induced by the Frobenius
product;

**(c)** the block operator $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&C(\xi)\\-C(\xi)&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$
on $V\oplus V$ is symmetric (self-adjoint) with operator norm at most $|\xi|$;

**(d)** if $\zeta$ is a covector with $\zeta(U)=z$ and spatial part
$\zeta_\perp$, the symbol matrix
$\left(\begin{smallmatrix}zI&C(\zeta_\perp)\\-C(\zeta_\perp)&zI\end{smallmatrix}\right)$
is positive definite whenever $z>|\zeta_\perp|$, in particular for every
future-positive timelike conormal $\zeta$; hence the reduced dust system is
symmetric hyperbolic with positive time matrix on a spacelike initial surface.

derivations.claim: (Derivation of (a).) Insert the reconstructed $C=C[E,B]$ and the Schouten tensor $S$ of [[def-gr-dust-electric-magnetic-weyl-variables-and-schouten]] into the symmetric spatial projections $F_{(i|0|j)}-\tfrac13h_{ij}h^{kl}F_{k0l}$ and $\tfrac12\epsilon_{(i}{}^{kl}F_{j)kl}$ of the curvature-Bianchi residual $F_{jkl}=\nabla^i(C_{ijkl}+S\text{-terms})$ of [L1]. Expanding the projected derivative produces the Lie-derivative terms $\mathcal L_UE,\mathcal L_UB$, the curl terms $D_kB\epsilon$, $D_kE\epsilon$, the $\chi$-coupling terms collected in the displayed equations, and the matter term $\tfrac12\kappa r(\chi_{(ij)}-\tfrac13\chi h_{ij})$ from the Ricci part; the derivative of $r$ in the trace part cancels against $q=U(r)+r\chi=0$, and the spatial derivative of $r$ has no symmetric tracefree component in these projections, which is why no density-derivative coupling appears in the principal block. This gives (a).

(Transport equations (c).) The first equation is the vanishing of the time torsion in the parallel-comoving gauge: with $\Gamma_0{}^i{}_j=0$ and $e_0=U$ the zero-torsion identity is exactly $\partial_se_a{}^\mu=-\Gamma_a{}^j{}_0e_j{}^\mu$, the displayed transport equation. The second is the vanishing of the time-curvature residual $\Delta^i{}_{j0a}=0$ written in the same gauge; for tentative data the actual curvature is defined with the frame bracket, so the identity holds by definition of the tentative curvature in the reduced system. The third is $q=0$ with $r>0$: $U(r)+r\chi=0$ reads $\partial_sr=-r\chi$.

(Trace preservation (b).) Contract the two equations of (a) with $h^{ij}$ and commute $h$ through $\mathcal L_U$ using $\mathcal L_Uh_{ij}=2\chi_{(ij)}$ [L3]; the curl terms contract to divergences of $E,B$ and the coupling terms combine into multiples of the traces, giving homogeneous transport equations for the traces. Hence the subspace of tracefree pairs is invariant, and zero initial traces stay zero.

(Symmetry and positivity (d).) With the positive Frobenius product on spatial symmetric tensors, [L3] gives $C(\xi)^*=-C(\xi)$ and $\|C(\xi)\|\le|\xi|$; hence the $E,B$ block of the principal symbol is the symmetric matrix $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&C(\xi)\\-C(\xi)&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ with eigenvalues bounded by $|\xi|$, while all other blocks are multiples of the transport direction $U$: their symbol contributions are $\zeta(U)$ times the identity or zero. The full time matrix at a covector $\zeta$ is therefore positive definite whenever $\zeta(U)>|\zeta_\perp|$, which holds exactly for future-positive timelike conormals; the displayed $P,Q$ system with the transport equations is thus symmetric hyperbolic. [step 1.2, L3, algebra] ∎



- **Role.** Clause (d) is the hyperbolicity input for the local dust existence theorem; the residual and subsidiary equations that make the reduced system equivalent to the full Einstein-dust system are analysed in [[thm-gr-dust-subsidiary-and-residual-vanishing]] and [[thm-gr-dust-subsidiary-and-residual-vanishing]].
