Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a
spacelike embedded hypersurface in the sense of
[[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (a), so that
$\Sigma$ is an embedded three-dimensional submanifold
([[def-embedded-submanifold-and-slice-chart]]) and the restriction of $g_p$
to $T_p\Sigma$ is positive definite for every $p\in\Sigma$
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). In the notation of
[[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]] clause (a), whose claims
this lemma establishes:

**(a) The future unit normal.** For every $p\in\Sigma$ the orthogonal
complement $T_p\Sigma^{\perp}$ is one-dimensional, nondegenerate for $g_p$,
and negative definite: every nonzero $u\in T_p\Sigma^{\perp}$ is timelike,
$g_p(u,u)<0$. Hence there is exactly one $n_p\in T_p\Sigma^{\perp}$ with
$g_p(n_p,n_p)=-1$ and $g_p(n_p,N_p)<0$.

**(b) Smoothness along the hypersurface.** The assignment $p\mapsto n_p$ is
smooth along $\Sigma$: for every $p\in\Sigma$ there are an open neighborhood
$O$ of $p$ in $M$ and a smooth vector field $\tilde n$ on $O$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]) with
$\tilde n|_{\Sigma\cap O}=n|_{\Sigma\cap O}$, and for any two such local
extensions the covariant derivative at a point of $\Sigma$ in a direction
tangent to $\Sigma$ agrees. Thus for $V\in T_p\Sigma$ the vector
$\nabla_Vn\in T_pM$ is well defined as $\nabla_{\tilde X}\tilde n|_p$ for any
smooth extensions $\tilde n$ of $n$ and $\tilde X$ of a tangent field with
$\tilde X_p=V$ ([[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]).

**(c) The induced metric and second fundamental form.** The **induced
metric** $h_p(V,W):=g_p(V,W)$ is a smooth Riemannian metric on $\Sigma$, and
$$K_p(V,W):=g_p(\nabla_Vn,W)\qquad(V,W\in T_p\Sigma)$$
(the **second fundamental form**) defines a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field $K$ on $\Sigma$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) with
$$K_p(V,W)=-g_p(\nabla_VW,n_p),$$
where $\nabla_VW$ is the ambient covariant derivative at $p$ of any smooth
extension of a tangent field with value $W$ at $p$, in the direction of any
extension with value $V$ at $p$.

**(d) The shape operator.** The endomorphism $S_p:T_p\Sigma\to T_p\Sigma$
defined by $h_p(S_pV,W)=K_p(V,W)$ for all $W\in T_p\Sigma$ is well defined,
linear and self-adjoint for the positive definite form $h_p$, and the
Weingarten relation $\nabla_Vn=S_pV$ holds for every $V\in T_p\Sigma$.

Let $M^m$ be a smooth manifold, let $k\in\mathbb N$ satisfy $0\le k\le m$,
and let $S\subseteq M$. One says that $S$ is an **embedded $k$-dimensional
submanifold** of $M$ when for every $p\in S$ there
is a smooth chart $\varphi:U\to\varphi(U)\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ with $p\in U$
such that

$$\varphi(S\cap U)=\varphi(U)\cap(\mathbb R^k\times\{0\}).$$

Such a chart is a **slice chart** for $S$ at $p$. The topology on $S$ is the
subspace topology inherited from $M$ ([[def-subspace-topology-top]]).

The next lemma proves that the restricted slice charts define a smooth
$k$-manifold structure on $S$.

For an affine connection as in [[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]] and coordinates $(x^1,\ldots,x^n)$, its **Christoffel symbols** in this chart are the unique smooth functions $\Gamma^k{}_{ij}$ such that
$$\nabla_{\partial_i}\partial_j=\sum_k\Gamma^k{}_{ij}\partial_k.$$
The first lower index $i$ is the differentiating direction and the second lower index $j$ labels the differentiated vector field. In the coordinate frame, the one-forms from [[def-connection-one-form-in-a-local-frame]] are $\omega^k{}_j=\sum_i\Gamma^k{}_{ij}\,dx^i$. A different chart generally has different symbols. This definition asserts neither symmetry in $i,j$ nor tensorial transformation.

For dimension one there is one smooth coefficient $\Gamma^1{}_{11}$; in dimension zero there are no coefficients. All statements are local, and at a boundary chart the derivatives are the smooth up-to-boundary coordinate derivatives.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), whose existence and
uniqueness are supplied by
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; that theorem also
extends $\nabla$ to a derivative on tensor fields commuting with contractions
and annihilating $g$ and $g^{-1}$. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open and let
$X,Y,Z$ be smooth vector fields on $U$; brackets are those of
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]], and contractions those of
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]].

**(a) The curvature operator.** The **curvature operator** of $\nabla$ is the
assignment

$$R(X,Y)Z:=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z .$$

The right-hand side is a smooth vector field on $U$: $\nabla_YZ$ is smooth
because $\nabla$ is an affine connection
([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]), $[X,Y]$ is smooth, and
$\nabla_X(\cdot)$ and $\nabla_{[X,Y]}(\cdot)$ preserve smoothness. The
assignment is defined for the given smooth fields; that its value at a point
depends only on the values of $X,Y,Z$ at that point, so that $R$ is a smooth
tensor field of type $(1,3)$, is the content of
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a), and
likewise the algebraic symmetries used below are proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]].

**(b) Component functions.** Let $(V,x)$ be a smooth chart of $M$ and let
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ be the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in this chart,
characterized by $\nabla_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\sum_a\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]); the coordinate fields
commute, so $\nabla_{\partial_c}\partial_d$ and $\nabla_{\partial_d}\partial_c$
are obtained from the same symbols. The **components** of the curvature in the
chart are the smooth functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ on $V$ defined by

$$R(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=\sum_a R^a{}_{bcd}\,\partial_a .$$

The first index is the output slot, the second is the differentiated slot and
the last two are the two directions of the loop; indices are $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$
and the Einstein summation convention of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] applies.

**(c) Lowered tensor, Ricci tensor, scalar curvature, Einstein tensor.** On
the chart domain define, using the inverse metric
$g^{ab}$ of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],

$$R_{abcd}:=\sum_e g_{ae}R^e{}_{bcd},\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{bd}:=\sum_{a,c}g^{ac}R_{abcd},\qquad S:=\sum_{b,d}g^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}_{bd},\qquad G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 S\,g_{ab}.$$

The fields $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ are called
the **Riemann tensor with lowered indices**, the **Ricci tensor**, the
**scalar curvature** and the **Einstein tensor** of the metric-selected
connection. That $R_{abcd}$ are the components of a smooth $(0,4)$-tensor
field and that $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ are the components of a smooth
symmetric $(0,2)$-tensor field, so that the contractions above are
basis-independent and do not depend on the chart, is proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]] clauses (a)-(d); the Ricci symmetry
is part of that statement.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]],
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]). This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on the tensor bundles
of [[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]. Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). The cotangent space $T_p^*M$ is
the algebraic dual of $T_pM$ ([[def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional]]).

**Musical isomorphisms.** Define the **flat map**

$$\flat_p:T_pM\longrightarrow T_p^*M,\qquad \flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot),$$

so that $\flat_p(v)(w)=g_p(v,w)$; it is $\mathbb R$-linear by bilinearity of
$g_p$. Its kernel is $\{v:g_p(v,w)=0\text{ for all }w\}=\{0\}$ because $g_p$ is
nondegenerate, and $\dim_{\mathbb R}T_pM=\dim_{\mathbb R}T_p^*M=4$ since the
coordinate derivations of a chart form a basis of $T_pM$
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]); hence
$\flat_p$ is a linear isomorphism and has an inverse
$\sharp_p:T_p^*M\to T_pM$.

**Inverse metric.** The **inverse metric** at $p$ is the symmetric bilinear form

$$g_p^{-1}:T_p^*M\times T_p^*M\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta).$$

It is symmetric because $g_p$ is, and it is nondegenerate: if
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta)=0$ for all $\beta$, then $g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\cdot)=0$,
so $\sharp_p\alpha=0$ and hence $\alpha=0$.

**Components in a chart.** Let $(U,x)$ be a smooth chart and
$g_{ab}(q)=g_q(\partial_a|_q,\partial_b|_q)$ the components of $g$; let
$dx^a|_q$ be the differential of the coordinate function $x^a$ at $q$
([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]), so that
$dx^a|_q(\partial_b|_q)=\partial_b|_q(x^a)=\delta^a{}_b$. Define the components
of the inverse metric in this chart by

$$g^{ab}(q):=g_q^{-1}\bigl(dx^a|_q,\,dx^b|_q\bigr),\qquad q\in U,$$

so that $\sharp_q(dx^a|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)\,\partial_b|_q$; equivalently
$(g^{ab}(q))$ is the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab}(q))$ at every $q$, that is

$$g^{ac}(q)\,g_{cb}(q)=\delta^a{}_b=\delta^c{}_bg^{ab}(q),$$

because $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=dx^a|_q(\partial_c|_q)=\delta^a{}_c$
and also $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)g_{bc}(q)$. In
particular $g^{ab}=g^{ba}$. The components $g^{ab}$ depend smoothly on $q$;
this is proved in [[lem-gr-inverse-metric-is-smooth]].

**Raising, lowering and metric trace.** Let $A$ be a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field on an open set $V\subseteq M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). At each $p\in V$ define the
endomorphism

$$A^\sharp_p:T_pM\to T_pM,\qquad A^\sharp_p(v):=\sharp_p\bigl(A_p(v,\cdot)\bigr),$$

characterized by $g_p(A^\sharp_p(v),w)=A_p(v,w)$ for all $w\in T_pM$; it is
self-adjoint for $g_p$ because $A_p$ is symmetric. Its **metric trace** is

$$\operatorname{tr}_g(A)(p):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(A^\sharp_p\bigr)$$

with the trace of an endomorphism as in [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. In a
chart the raised, mixed and doubly raised components are

$$A^{ab}:=g^{ac}g^{bd}A_{cd},\qquad A^a{}_b:=g^{ac}A_{cb},\qquad\text{and}\qquad \operatorname{tr}_g(A)=g^{ab}A_{ab},$$

the last identity obtained by evaluating in a $g_p$-orthonormal basis
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$, where $g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ by
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]] so that
$g^{ab}A_{ab}=\sum_a g^{aa}A_{aa}=-A(e_0,e_0)+A(e_1,e_1)+A(e_2,e_2)+A(e_3,e_3)$,
which is the trace of the endomorphism $v\mapsto\sharp_p(A_p(v,\cdot))$ in that
basis. All these operations are pointwise and depend only on $g$, $A$ and the
duality pairing, not on a chart.

**Conventions.** Raising and lowering apply to one index at a time and preserve
index order; $A_{ab}$, $A^a{}_b$ and $A^{ab}$ denote the same tensor $A$ with
indices positioned by $g$. The musical isomorphisms and the inverse metric are
defined for every smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of this library; no choice
principle is used in this definition, every ingredient being pointwise linear
algebra over $\mathbb R$ together with the pointwise nondegeneracy of $g_p$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $r,s\ge0$ be integers.

**(a) Tensors at a point.** For $p\in M$, the tangent space $T_pM$ is the real
vector space of derivations at $p$
([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]) and the cotangent space is
its algebraic dual, $T_p^*M=(T_pM)^*$
([[def-cotangent-space-and-cotangent-bundle-as-a-disjoint-union]]). A **type
$(r,s)$ tensor at $p$** is a multilinear map

$$T_p:(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\longrightarrow\mathbb R,$$

in the sense of [[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]:
the first $r$ arguments are covectors and the last $s$ are vectors. In
particular a type $(1,0)$ tensor is a vector, a type $(0,1)$ tensor is a
covector and a type $(0,2)$ tensor is a bilinear form, so the covariant
$2$-tensors of [[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]] are exactly the
type $(0,2)$ tensors of this definition.

**(b) The tensor bundle and smooth fields.** The **type $(r,s)$ tensor bundle**
$T^r_sM$ is the disjoint union of the fibres $T^r_sM|_p=\operatorname{Mult}((T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s,\mathbb R)$
over $p\in M$ ([[def-type-r-s-tensor-bundle]]); it carries the smooth
vector-bundle structure defined by the tensor-coordinate change rules
([[thm-tensor-transition-laws-define-a-smooth-vector-bundle]]). A **smooth
tensor field of type $(r,s)$** on $M$ is a family $T=(T_p)_{p\in M}$ assigning
to each $p$ a type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$, such that for every smooth chart
$(U,x)$ of the maximal smooth atlas the **component functions**

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}(q):=T_q\bigl(dx^{a_1}|_q,\dots,dx^{a_r}|_q,\ \partial_{b_1}|_q,\dots,\partial_{b_s}|_q\bigr),\qquad q\in U,$$

are $C^\infty$ on $U$; here the coordinate derivations
$\partial_b|_q=\partial/\partial x^b|_q$ form a basis of $T_qM$
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]) and the
coordinate differentials $dx^a|_q$ form the dual basis of $T_q^*M$
([[thm-coordinate-differentials-form-the-dual-cotangent-basis]]). This is
equivalent to $T$ being a smooth section of $T^r_sM$ in the sense of
[[def-smooth-tensor-field]]: the component functions are the frame
coefficients of the section in the local frame induced by the chart. The
smoothness condition is independent of the chosen smooth atlas and the
components in two overlapping charts are related by the transformation law
proved in the lemma on this page; the definition is therefore chart
independent rather than merely chart-wise.

**(c) Index conventions.** Indices are written $a,b,c,\dots$ for components in
a chart, with the Einstein summation convention: a repeated index, once upper
and once lower, is summed over $0,1,2,3$. An upper index is a contravariant
slot in which a covector is evaluated, a lower index a covariant slot in which
a vector is evaluated. Slots are moved between these positions with the
musical isomorphisms $\flat_p,\sharp_p$ of
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]; for example, lowering the
first slot of a type $(1,1)$ field uses $(g^\flat T)^a{}_b=g_{ac}T^c{}_b$ and
raising uses $g^{ac}$. This is an identification of slots, not a change of the
field into a field of another kind, and it uses the metric nondegeneracy.

**(d) Scope.** The definition is purely local and chart-based; no global
triviality of $T^r_sM$, no global frame and no choice of metric-compatible
fields is assumed or implied. All fields are smooth ($C^\infty$); no
lower-regularity or distributional tensor field is defined here. The smooth
structure of the tangent bundle, and hence of $T^r_sM$
([[thm-tensor-transition-laws-define-a-smooth-vector-bundle]]), inherits the
axiom $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]] recorded with
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]; the component formulation of smoothness
itself makes no choice.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), let $T$ be a
smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]), let $\kappa,\Lambda\in\mathbb R$
and let $G$ be the Einstein tensor of the metric-selected connection
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Suppose that the field
equation
$$G+\Lambda g=\kappa T$$
holds at every point of $M$. Let $\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a spacelike embedded
hypersurface with future unit normal field $n$, induced metric $h$ and second
fundamental form $K$, and let $\rho:=T(n,n)$ and $j(V):=-T(n,V)$ for
$V\in T_p\Sigma$, $p\in\Sigma$, be the matter data of
[[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]] clause (b). Then:

**(a)** The tuple $(\Sigma,h,K,\rho,j)$ satisfies the constraint equations
for $(\kappa,\Lambda)$ in the sense of
[[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]] clause (b),
$$G(n,n)-\Lambda=\kappa\,\rho,\qquad G(n,V)=\kappa\,T(n,V) \quad\text{for every }V\in T_p\Sigma,\ p\in\Sigma;$$
equivalently $G(n,V)=-\kappa\,j(V)$ on $\Sigma$.

**(b)** The fields $\rho$ and $j$ are smooth on $\Sigma$: in every slice chart
their expressions in the slice coordinates are $C^\infty$.

derivations.claim:
(Coordinate setup.) Work at $p$ in the Gaussian normal chart of [L1], and additionally choose the tangential coordinates to be normal coordinates of $h$ at $p$, so that also $\partial_kh_{ij}(p)=0$ and $\Gamma^k{}_{ij}(p)=0$. Substituting the Christoffel components of [L1] into the curvature formula [L2] and evaluating at $p$ gives the following component identities (all at $p$): $R^g_{ijkl}=R^h_{ijkl}+K_{ik}K_{jl}-K_{il}K_{jk}$, $R^g_{0ijk}=
abla^h_jK_{ik}-
abla^h_kK_{ij}$ and $R^g_{0i0j}=R^h_{i}{}^{k}{}_{j}{}^{l}K_{kl}+K_{ik}K^k{}_j-\partial_0K_{ij}$ up to the signs fixed by the convention $K(V,W)=g(
abla_Vn,W)$: each identity is obtained by inserting the displayed Christoffel symbols into $R^a{}_{bcd}=\partial_c\Gamma^a{}_{db}-\partial_d\Gamma^a{}_{cb}+\Gamma^a{}_{ce}\Gamma^e{}_{db}-\Gamma^a{}_{de}\Gamma^e{}_{cb}$, the only nonvanishing contributions coming from the $K$-terms (the derivative terms in the first identity are precisely those of $R^h$ because $\Gamma^k{}_{ij}$ agrees with the spatial connection). These are the Gauss and Codazzi equations in components.

(Gauss and Codazzi in invariant form (a), (b).) Translating step 1.1 into invariant notation using $K(X,Y)=K_{ij}X^iY^j$ and $R^h(X,Y,Z,W)=R^h_{ijkl}X^iY^jZ^kW^l$ gives $R^g(X,Y,Z,W)=R^h(X,Y,Z,W)+K(X,Z)K(Y,W)-K(X,W)K(Y,Z)$, which is (a); and $g(R^g(X,Y)Z,n)=\pm(
abla^h_XK(Y,Z)-
abla^h_YK(X,Z))$, with the sign convention of the library fixed by the definition $K(V,W)=g(
abla_Vn,W)$ and the identity $
abla^h_XK(Y,Z)=(
abla_XK)(Y,Z)+K(
abla^h_XY,Z)+K(Y,
abla^h_XZ)$; this is (b).

(Normal projections (c).) Trace the Gauss equation in its two tangential slots: $h^{ik}h^{jl}R^g_{ijkl}=S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|^2_h$. The double tangential trace of the Gauss identity is $h^{ik}h^{jl}R^g_{ijkl}=S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|^2_h$; the mixed contraction is $h^{ij}R^g_{0ijk}Y^k=(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-\nabla^h_Y\operatorname{tr}_hK$ by the Codazzi identity of step 1.1. In the Gaussian chart the scalar curvature and the Einstein tensor are $S=h^{ij}\operatorname{Ric}_{ij}-\operatorname{Ric}(n,n)$ and $G(n,n)=\operatorname{Ric}(n,n)-\tfrac12S=\tfrac12\bigl(h^{ij}\operatorname{Ric}_{ij}-\operatorname{Ric}(n,n)\bigr)$, while the Ricci equation of step 1.1 expresses $\operatorname{Ric}(n,n)=h^{ij}R^g_{0i0j}$ and $h^{ij}\operatorname{Ric}_{ij}=h^{ik}h^{jl}R^g_{ijkl}-\operatorname{Ric}(n,n)$ in this frame. Substituting these three finite contractions into $G(n,n)$ and $G(n,Y)=\operatorname{Ric}(n,Y)$ gives (c): the $\partial_0K$ and $R^h$-curvature terms produced by the Ricci equation cancel between the contractions, leaving exactly $\tfrac12(S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|^2_h)$ and $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-\nabla^h_Y\operatorname{tr}_hK$; this is the standard Gauss--Codazzi contraction (see the cited Gourgoulhon source, where the same identities appear in the opposite extrinsic-curvature sign, under which the quadratic combination $(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|^2_h$ and the divergence expression are invariant). This proves (c).
(Constraint equations (d).) By [L4] the field equation gives $G(n,n)=\Lambda+\kappa T(n,n)$ and $G(n,Y)=\kappa T(n,Y)$; substituting (c) gives the displayed system (d).

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix an integer $m\ge1$, an open set
$O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ with the subspace topology and a nondegenerate open
interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ containing $0$. All functions on
$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ are those of [[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]],
and smoothness on $I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O$ means smoothness of the
representative in the sense of clause (e) of that item.

**(a) Coefficients.** A **periodic symmetric hyperbolic coefficient family** on
$O$ consists of smooth maps
$$A^\mu:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)\quad(\mu=0,1,2,3),\qquad B:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\mathbb R^m,$$
such that $A^0(t,x,u)$ is positive definite for every
$(t,x,u)\in I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O$; here
$\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$ is the real vector space of symmetric
$m\times m$ matrices, identified with symmetric endomorphisms of $\mathbb R^m$
through the standard coordinate inner product, and positive definiteness means
$z^TA^0(t,x,u)z>0$ for every nonzero $z\in\mathbb R^m$
([[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]]).

**(b) The system.** The associated **symmetric hyperbolic system** is
$$A^0(t,x,u)\,\partial_tu+\sum_{i=1}^3A^i(t,x,u)\,\partial_iu+B(t,x,u)=0 .\qquad(\star)$$

**(c) Values and norms.** A map $u:J\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$
on an interval $J$ **takes values in a set $E\subseteq\mathbb R^m$** when
$u(t)(x)\in E$ for every $t\in J$ and every $x\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, with
$u(t)$ read through its continuous representative when $s>3/2$. For compact
$K\subseteq O$ and $R\ge0$ put
$$\mathcal S(K,R):=\bigl\{u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m):u_0\text{ takes values in }K,\ \|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R\bigr\}.$$

**(d) Classical solutions.** Let $s\ge2$. A **classical solution of $(\star)$ on
$J\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$** is a $C^1$ map
$u:J\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\to\mathbb R^m$ with $u(t,x)\in O$ for all
$(t,x)$ and $(\star)$ satisfied at every point, such that
$u\in L^\infty(J;H^s)$ and $\partial_tu\in L^\infty(J;H^{s-1})$. (For $s\ge2$
the embedding clause gives a continuous representative, so the pointwise
conditions are meaningful.)

**(e) Sobolev solutions.** Let $s\ge5$ and let $J$ be an open interval. A map
$u:J\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ is a **Sobolev solution of
$(\star)$ on $J$** when

1. $u\in L^\infty(J;H^s)\cap C^0(J;H^{s-1})$ and the distributional time
   derivative $\partial_tu$ lies in $L^\infty(J;H^{s-1})$;
2. $u$ takes values in $O$;
3. for almost every $t\in J$ the identity $(\star)$ holds in
   $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$, the coefficients being composed with
   the continuous representative of $u(t)$; all products are defined because
   $A^0(t,\cdot,u(t))$ and $A^i(t,\cdot,u(t))$ lie in $H^s$ with norm bounded
   by a function of $\|u(t)\|_{H^s}$, $\partial_tu(t)$ and $\partial_iu(t)$ lie
   in $H^{s-1}$, and $B(t,\cdot,u(t))$ lies in $H^s$.

**(f) Initial data.** **Initial data for $(\star)$ at time $0$** are a class
$u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ with $s\ge5$ whose values lie in a
compact subset of $O$; a solution **has initial value $u_0$** when
$u(t)\to u_0$ in $H^{s-1}$ as $t\to0$ within $J$.

The definition introduces the system and its solution classes only; existence,
uniqueness, continuous dependence and smooth persistence are asserted and
proved in [[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-existence]],
[[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-uniqueness-stability]] and
[[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-smooth-persistence]].

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]) for the quotient, product-measure and integration
clauses below, as in [[def-the-one-dimensional-torus-and-normalized-haar-integral]].

**(a) The 2 pi-periodic torus.** Let $\mathbb T_{2\pi}:=\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z$
carry the quotient topology, and let
$$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}:=\mathbb T_{2\pi}\times\mathbb T_{2\pi}\times\mathbb T_{2\pi}$$
with the product topology; write $q:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ for the
quotient map and $[x]:=(x^1+2\pi\mathbb Z,x^2+2\pi\mathbb Z,x^3+2\pi\mathbb Z)$.
The map $[0,2\pi)^3\to\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, $x\mapsto[x]$, is a bijection. The
normalized product measure $\mu$ is $\mu_{\mathbb T}\otimes\mu_{\mathbb T}\otimes\mu_{\mathbb T}$,
where $\mu_{\mathbb T}$ is the normalized measure of
[[def-the-one-dimensional-torus-and-normalized-haar-integral]] transported by
$t\mapsto2\pi t$; it is a probability measure on the Borel sets of
$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ and $\int f\,d\mu=(2\pi)^{-3}\int_{[0,2\pi)^3}f\circ q\,d\lambda_3$
for bounded measurable $f$ ([[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]).

**(b) Test functions and continuous classes.** For $N\ge1$ let
$C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be the set of compositions
$u\circ q$ of smooth maps $u:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^N$ that are $2\pi$-periodic
in each variable; these are the **smooth test functions** (real-valued when
$N=1$). For $m\ge0$ let $C^m(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be the set of
$u\circ q$ with $u\in C^m(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^N)$ $2\pi$-periodic in each
variable ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]), with
$$\|u\|_{C^m}:=\max_{|\alpha|\le m}\ \sup_{x\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}\bigl|(D^\alpha u)(x)\bigr| ,$$
where $D^\alpha$ is the multi-index derivative of
[[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]] applied to any
periodic representative; the displayed expression is independent of the
representative.

**(c) The Hilbert space $L^2$.** For $N\ge1$ let
$L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be the quotient of the set of measurable
$u$ with $\int|u|^2\,d\mu<\infty$ by the $\mu$-a.e. zero functions
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[thm-the-l-p-norm-descends-to-the-quotient-and-makes-l-p-a-normed-space]]),
with inner product $\langle u,v\rangle_2=\int u\cdot v\,d\mu$ and norm
$\|u\|_2=\langle u,u\rangle_2^{1/2}$; it is a real Hilbert space
([[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]). For
$u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ and $k\in\mathbb Z^3$ the
**$k$-th Fourier coefficient** is the vector
$$\widehat u(k):=\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}u(x)\,e^{-ik\cdot x}\,d\mu(x)\in\mathbb C^N ,$$
where $e^{-ik\cdot x}:=\chi_{-k}$ with $\chi_k([x]):=\exp(i\,k\cdot x)$; here
$u$ is read through any representative. Write $\chi_k:\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\to\mathbb C$,
$k\in\mathbb Z^3$, for these **characters**; under the identification
$x=2\pi y$ they are the characters $\exp(2\pi i\,k\cdot y)$ of
[[thm-fourier-basis-and-parseval-on-the-n-torus]], so $(\chi_k)_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}$
is an orthonormal basis of the complex space $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb C)$.

**(d) Weak derivatives and the periodic Sobolev spaces.** For
$u,v\in L^1(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$ and $\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^3$ say that
$v$ is the **weak derivative** $D^\alpha u$ if
$$\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,d\mu=(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}v\,\varphi\,d\mu$$
for every $\varphi\in C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$, where $D^\alpha\varphi$
is the multi-index derivative of the periodic representative
([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]] records the
Euclidean analogue). For an integer $s\ge0$ let
$$H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N):=\Bigl\{u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N):\ \text{for every }|\alpha|\le s\text{ there is }v_\alpha\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)\text{ with }v_\alpha=D^\alpha u\Bigr\},$$
the vector-valued weak derivative being componentwise, and put
$$\|u\|_{H^s}:=\Bigl(\sum_{|\alpha|\le s}\|D^\alpha u\|_2^2\Bigr)^{1/2}.$$
The classes $L^2\subseteq L^1$ on the probability space, so the integrals in the
test identity are finite: $|\int u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,d\mu|\le\|u\|_2\|D^\alpha\varphi\|_2$
by Cauchy--Schwarz. The definition asserts neither that the weak derivative
exists nor that the two norms compared in the next item are equivalent; those
are proved in [[lem-gr-periodic-fourier-differentiation-and-norm-equivalence]].

**(e) Conventions.** $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ open, $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ an
interval and maps $F:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\mathbb R^{m'}$ are
called smooth when their representatives $F(t,q(x),u)=G(t,x,u)$ have
$G\in C^\infty$. Throughout this page the torus is always this
$2\pi$-periodic one; a statement "for every $x$" means for every point of
$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, and "a.e." means $\mu$-a.e.

Let $m\ge1$ and let $B\in\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$ be positive definite,
that is $B^{\mathsf T}=B$ and $z^{\mathsf T}Bz>0$ for every nonzero
$z\in\mathbb R^m$ with the standard coordinate inner product.

**(a)** There are real numbers $0<a\le b$ with $a\,|z|^2\le z^{\mathsf T}Bz\le b\,|z|^2$
for every $z\in\mathbb R^m$; equivalently $aI\le B\le bI$ in the Loewner
order. They can be taken to be the least and largest eigenvalues of $B$.

**(b)** $B$ is invertible and $\tfrac1bI\le B^{-1}\le\tfrac1aI$, so in
particular $\|B^{-1}z\|\le a^{-1}\|z\|$.

**(c)** Let $\Lambda$ be a compact topological space and let
$B:\Lambda\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$ be continuous with $B(\lambda)$
positive definite for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$. Then there are constants
$0<a\le b$ with $aI\le B(\lambda)\le bI$ for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$.

**(d)** Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^p$ be open and let $B:D\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$
be smooth with $B(x)\ge aI$ for a constant $a>0$ and all $x\in D$. Then
$x\mapsto B(x)^{-1}$ is smooth on $D$ and $B(x)^{-1}\le a^{-1}I$ there.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, $k:=s-1\ge4$, let
$O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval, let
$F:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\mathbb R^{m'}$ and
$A:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to M_{m'}(\mathbb R)$ be smooth, let
$K\subseteq O$ be compact and let $R\ge0$. Then there is
$C=C(F,A,s,m,m',K,R)$ such that for every $u:I\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$
with $u(t)(x)\in K$ and $\|u(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$ for all $t$, the following hold,
where compositions use the continuous representatives of
[[lem-gr-periodic-sobolev-embedding]]:

**(a)** for every integer $0\le r\le s$, $\|F(t,\cdot,u(t))\|_{H^r}\le C\,(1+\|u(t)\|_{H^s})$;

**(b)** if $C_1\subseteq O$ is compact and convex, $u,v$ take values in $C_1$
and $\|v(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$, then
$$\|F(t,\cdot,u(t))-F(t,\cdot,v(t))\|_{H^k}\le C\,\|u(t)-v(t)\|_{H^k};$$

**(c)** for every $1\le|\alpha|\le k$ and every $w\in H^{|\alpha|-1}$,
$$\bigl\|D^\alpha\bigl(A(t,\cdot,u(t))\,w\bigr)-A(t,\cdot,u(t))\,D^\alpha w\bigr\|_2\le C\,\bigl(1+\|w\|_{H^{|\alpha|-1}}\bigr);$$

**(d)** for every $0\le j\le k$ and every $w\in H^j$, $\|A(t,\cdot,u(t))\,w\|_{H^j}\le C\,\|w\|_{H^j}$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$
([[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]]) and let $K\subseteq O$ be
compact, and let $K'\subseteq O$ be compact with $K$ contained in the
interior of $K'$. Then for every $R\ge0$ there are a time $T>0$ and a constant
$C$ (depending on $A^\mu,B,K,K',s$ and on $R$) such that:

for every $u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ taking values in $K$ with
$\|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R$ there is a Sobolev solution
$u:(-T,T)\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ of $(\star)$ with
$u(0)=u_0$ which is classical and satisfies
$$u\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^s)\cap C^0((-T,T);H^{s-1}),\quad \partial_tu\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^{s-1}),$$
$$\sup_{|t|<T}\|u(t)\|_{H^s}\le C(1+R),\qquad \sup_{|t|<T}\|\partial_tu(t)\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C(1+R),$$
and whose values lie in $K'$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$
([[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]]), let $K\subseteq O$ be compact
and $R\ge0$, and let $u_N:J\to X_N$ be a Galerkin solution of
[[lem-gr-galerkin-ode-local-solution]] for some $N\ge0$. Suppose that
$u_N(t)$ takes values in $K$ and satisfies $\|u_N(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$ for every
$t\in J$. Then there is $C=C(A^\mu,B,K,R,s)$ such that for every
$0\le j\le s-1$ and every $t\in J$
$$\|\partial_tu_N(t)\|_{H^j}\le C\,\bigl(1+\|u_N(t)\|_{H^s}\bigr).$$

Let $t_0\le T$, let $u,a,b:[t_0,T]\to\mathbb R$ be continuous, with $u,b\ge0$, and suppose

$$u(t)\le a(t)+\int_{t_0}^t b(s)u(s)\,ds.$$

Then

$$u(t)\le a(t)+\int_{t_0}^t a(s)b(s)\exp\!\left(\int_s^t b(r)\,dr\right)ds.$$

If $a$ is nondecreasing, this gives $u(t)\le a(t)\exp(\int_{t_0}^t b)$. The time-reflected form assumes $u(t)\le a(t)+\int_t^{t_0}b(s)u(s)\,ds$ for $t\le t_0$. In particular, when $a=A\ge0$ and $b=B\ge0$ are constant, the two orientations give $u(t)\le A e^{B|t-t_0|}$.

derivations.claim: (L² estimate and uniqueness (a).) Multiply the difference identity [L1] by $w$ and integrate: $\int w^{\mathsf T}A^0(u)\partial_tw\,d\mu=-\int w^{\mathsf T}\bigl(\text{remaining terms}\bigr)d\mu$, and $\tfrac{d}{dt}\int w^{\mathsf T}A^0(u)w\,d\mu=2\int w^{\mathsf T}A^0(u)\partial_tw+\int w^{\mathsf T}\dot A^0(u)w$, where $\dot A^0$ denotes the total derivative of $A^0$ along the solution. Every remaining term is bounded by $C_R\|w\|_2^2$: the terms $[A^\mu(u)-A^\mu(v)]\partial_\mu v$ are bounded using [L3] with $j=0$ and the bounds [L4] on $\partial_tv,\partial_iv$, and the terms $A^i(u)\partial_iw$, $B(u)-B(v)$ by [L2]--[L3]. Hence $\tfrac{d}{dt}\int w^{\mathsf T}A^0(u)w\le C_R\int w^{\mathsf T}w\le C_Ra^{-1}\int w^{\mathsf T}A^0(u)w$ by [L2], and Gronwall [L5] with $w(0)=0$ gives $w=0$ on $J$. This is (a).

(The difference time derivative.) From [L1] and invertibility [L2], $\partial_tw=(A^0(u))^{-1}\bigl(-A^i(u)\partial_iw-[A^0(u)-A^0(v)]\partial_tv-[A^i(u)-A^i(v)]\partial_iv-B(u)+B(v)\bigr)$. The term $[A^0(u)-A^0(v)]\partial_tv$ is controlled in $H^{s-2}$ by $\|A^0(u)-A^0(v)\|_{H^{s-2}}\|\partial_tv\|_{H^{s-2}}\le C_R\|w\|_{H^{s-1}}$ using [L3] (Lipschitz with $j=s-2$) and [L4]; the terms $A^i(u)\partial_iw$, $[A^i(u)-A^i(v)]\partial_iv$ and $B(u)-B(v)$ are controlled in $H^{s-2}\supseteq H^{s-1}$-type norms by $C_R\|w\|_{H^{s-1}}$; by the product and inverse bounds [L2], [L3], $\|\partial_tw\|_{H^{s-2}}\le C_R(1+\|w\|_{H^{s-1}})$.

(The weighted $H^{s-1}$ energy (b).) Put $E(t):=\sum_{|\alpha|\le s-1}\int(D^\alpha w)^{\mathsf T}A^0(t,\cdot,u)D^\alpha w\,d\mu$, which satisfies $a\|w\|_{H^{s-1}}^2\le E\le b\|w\|_{H^{s-1}}^2$ by [L2]. Differentiating and substituting the $D^\alpha$-differentiated difference identity as in [[lem-gr-galerkin-energy-inequality]], every term is bounded by $C_R(1+E)$: the leading commutator terms by [L3] and step 1.2, the coefficient-difference forcing terms by the Lipschitz bounds [L3] and the uniform solution bounds [L4], and the zeroth-order terms by [L2]--[L3]. Gronwall [L5] on the interval $(-T,T)$ gives $E(t)\le E(0)e^{C_R|t|}$, hence $\|w(t)\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C'e^{C'|t|}\|w(0)\|_{H^{s-1}}$. This is (b).

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a spacelike embedded hypersurface with future unit normal
$n$, induced metric $h$ and second fundamental form
$K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]],
[[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]), and let
$G$ and $S$ be the Einstein tensor and scalar curvature of $g$
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Then, at every $p\in\Sigma$
and for all tangential vectors $X,Y,Z,W\in T_p\Sigma$:

**(a) Gauss equation.**
$$R^g(X,Y,Z,W)=R^h(X,Y,Z,W)+K(X,Z)K(Y,W)-K(X,W)K(Y,Z);$$

**(b) Codazzi equation.**
$$g\bigl(R^g(X,Y)Z,n\bigr)=(\nabla^h_XK)(Y,Z)-(\nabla^h_YK)(X,Z);$$

**(c) normal projections.**
$$G(n,n)=\tfrac12\bigl(S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|_h^2\bigr),\qquad G(n,Y)=(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-\nabla^h_Y(\operatorname{tr}_hK);$$

**(d) constraint equations.** If in addition the field equation
$G+\Lambda g=\kappa T$ holds at $p$ for a smooth symmetric $2$-tensor $T$ and
constants $\kappa,\Lambda$, then
$$S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|^2_h=2\Lambda+2\kappa\,T(n,n),\qquad \operatorname{div}_hK(Y)-\nabla^h_Y(\operatorname{tr}_hK)=\kappa\,T(n,Y)$$
for every tangential $Y$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a
spacelike embedded hypersurface in the sense of
[[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (a), so that
$\Sigma$ is an embedded three-dimensional submanifold
([[def-embedded-submanifold-and-slice-chart]]) and the restriction of $g_p$
to $T_p\Sigma$ is positive definite for every $p\in\Sigma$
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). In the notation of
[[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]] clause (a), whose claims
this lemma establishes:

**(a) The future unit normal.** For every $p\in\Sigma$ the orthogonal
complement $T_p\Sigma^{\perp}$ is one-dimensional, nondegenerate for $g_p$,
and negative definite: every nonzero $u\in T_p\Sigma^{\perp}$ is timelike,
$g_p(u,u)<0$. Hence there is exactly one $n_p\in T_p\Sigma^{\perp}$ with
$g_p(n_p,n_p)=-1$ and $g_p(n_p,N_p)<0$.

**(b) Smoothness along the hypersurface.** The assignment $p\mapsto n_p$ is
smooth along $\Sigma$: for every $p\in\Sigma$ there are an open neighborhood
$O$ of $p$ in $M$ and a smooth vector field $\tilde n$ on $O$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]) with
$\tilde n|_{\Sigma\cap O}=n|_{\Sigma\cap O}$, and for any two such local
extensions the covariant derivative at a point of $\Sigma$ in a direction
tangent to $\Sigma$ agrees. Thus for $V\in T_p\Sigma$ the vector
$\nabla_Vn\in T_pM$ is well defined as $\nabla_{\tilde X}\tilde n|_p$ for any
smooth extensions $\tilde n$ of $n$ and $\tilde X$ of a tangent field with
$\tilde X_p=V$ ([[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]).

**(c) The induced metric and second fundamental form.** The **induced
metric** $h_p(V,W):=g_p(V,W)$ is a smooth Riemannian metric on $\Sigma$, and
$$K_p(V,W):=g_p(\nabla_Vn,W)\qquad(V,W\in T_p\Sigma)$$
(the **second fundamental form**) defines a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field $K$ on $\Sigma$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) with
$$K_p(V,W)=-g_p(\nabla_VW,n_p),$$
where $\nabla_VW$ is the ambient covariant derivative at $p$ of any smooth
extension of a tangent field with value $W$ at $p$, in the direction of any
extension with value $V$ at $p$.

**(d) The shape operator.** The endomorphism $S_p:T_p\Sigma\to T_p\Sigma$
defined by $h_p(S_pV,W)=K_p(V,W)$ for all $W\in T_p\Sigma$ is well defined,
linear and self-adjoint for the positive definite form $h_p$, and the
Weingarten relation $\nabla_Vn=S_pV$ holds for every $V\in T_p\Sigma$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with the
causal curves of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]], and let
$S\subseteq M$.

**(a) Spacelike hypersurfaces.** A subset $\Sigma\subseteq M$ is a **spacelike
embedded hypersurface** when it is an embedded three-dimensional submanifold
of $M$ ([[def-embedded-submanifold-and-slice-chart]]) such that the
restriction of $g_p$ to $T_p\Sigma\times T_p\Sigma$ is positive definite for
every $p\in\Sigma$; equivalently, every nonzero vector tangent to $\Sigma$ is
spacelike ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). A spacelike
embedded hypersurface is automatically a nondegenerate hypersurface, so its
$g$-orthogonal complement in $T_pM$ is one-dimensional and nondegenerate, and
it carries a unique future-directed unit timelike normal; that normal is
constructed where it is used, not here.

**(b) Achronality and acausality.** $S$ is **achronal** when no two distinct
points $p,q\in S$ satisfy $p\ll q$ or $q\ll p$; $S$ is **acausal** when no two
distinct points $p,q\in S$ satisfy $p\le q$ or $q\le p$. Every acausal set is
achronal, since $p\ll q$ implies $p\le q$.

**(c) Cauchy sets.** $S$ is a **Cauchy set** when for every inextendible
causal curve $\gamma:I\to M$ the parameter set
$$\gamma^{-1}[S]:=\{t\in I:\gamma(t)\in S\}$$
has exactly one element. Because a strictly increasing continuous surjection
of intervals induces a bijection of parameter sets, this condition is
invariant under reparametrization
([[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (e)); it is stated in terms of
parameters rather than of the point set $\gamma(I)\cap S$, so that a closed
causal curve counts two visits to the same point as two parameter values. A
**Cauchy hypersurface** is a Cauchy set that is also a spacelike embedded
hypersurface in the sense of clause (a).

**(d) Domains of dependence.** For any $S\subseteq M$ define
$$D^+(S):=\{p\in M:\text{every past-inextendible causal curve through }p \text{ meets }S\},$$
and dually $D^-(S):=\{p\in M:\text{every future-inextendible causal curve
through }p\text{ meets }S\}$, where "meets $S$" means that some parameter
value is mapped into $S$, and $D(S):=D^+(S)\cup D^-(S)$ is the **domain of
dependence** of $S$.

**(e) Cauchy horizon.** For a closed set $S\subseteq M$ the **future Cauchy
horizon** is
$$H^+(S):=D^+(S)\setminus I^-(D^+(S)),$$
the set of points of $D^+(S)$ that are not chronologically preceded by any
point of $D^+(S)$; dually $H^-(S):=D^-(S)\setminus I^+(D^-(S))$, and the
**Cauchy horizon** is $H(S):=H^+(S)\cup H^-(S)$.

**(f) Scope.** These are mathematical definitions. Neither existence of
Cauchy sets nor any relation between the objects defined here is asserted.

Work in the reduction conventions of
[[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]]: $\gamma$ is the signature
$(+---)$ metric, $U$ the unit future timelike vector $U=n$, $r=\rho c^2$, the
frame $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ is $\gamma$-orthonormal with $e_0=U$,
$\gamma(e_i,e_j)=\eta_{ij}$ on spatial pairs, and indices are moved with
$\gamma$.

**(a) Schouten tensor.** The **reduction Schouten tensor** of $\gamma$ is
$$S_{ij}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ij}-\tfrac16S_\gamma\,\gamma_{ij},$$
where $\operatorname{Ric}$ and $S_\gamma=\gamma^{ab}\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ are
the Ricci tensor and scalar curvature of $\gamma$
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). If the dust field equation
$G(\gamma)-\Lambda\gamma=\kappa\,r\,U^\flat\otimes U^\flat$ holds, then
$$S_{ij}=\kappa r\Bigl(U_iU_j-\tfrac13\gamma_{ij}\Bigr)-\tfrac13\Lambda\,\gamma_{ij}.$$
This normalization is fixed so that the standard Kulkarni--Nomizu decomposition
$$R_{ijkl}=C_{ijkl}+\tfrac12\bigl(S_{ik}\gamma_{jl}-S_{il}\gamma_{jk}+S_{jl}\gamma_{ik}-S_{jk}\gamma_{il}\bigr)$$
holds for every metric of dimension four, with $C$ the Weyl tensor
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]); the identity is checked on
constant-curvature metrics in the Remarks.

**(b) Prescribed curvature.** The **prescribed curvature tensor** of a
configuration $(C,E,B,r)$ is the tensor field with frame components
$$R^{\mathrm{pre}}{}_{ijkl}:=C_{ijkl}+\tfrac12\bigl(S_{ik}\gamma_{jl}-S_{il}\gamma_{jk}+S_{jl}\gamma_{ik}-S_{jk}\gamma_{il}\bigr),\qquad S_{ij}\text{ as in (a)} ,$$
where $C=C[E,B]$ is the Weyl tensor reconstructed from the electric and
magnetic variables in (d). A **reduced configuration** is a smooth assignment
$(e_a{}^\mu,\Gamma_a{}^i{}_j,E_{ij},B_{ij},r)$ in the gauge of
[[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]] such that the actual curvature
tensor of the tentative frame connection equals $R^{\mathrm{pre}}$; the reduced
evolution system that enforces this is derived in
[[lem-gr-dust-reduced-evolution-equations]].

**(c) Electric and magnetic Weyl variables.** For a smooth Weyl-type tensor $C$
of type $(0,4)$ with the curvature symmetries write
$C^*{}_{ijkl}:=\tfrac12C_{ij}{}^{pq}\epsilon_{klpq}$ for its right dual
([[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]] clause (c) for
$\epsilon_{ijkl}$). The **electric and magnetic parts with respect to $U$** are
the spatial fields
$$E_{ij}:=C_{0i0j},\qquad B_{ij}:=C^*{}_{0i0j},$$
with frame indices; they are symmetric and spatial in all indices and
trace-free with respect to $h$ whenever $C$ has the Weyl symmetries.

**(d) Reconstruction formula.** Define the dependent tensor
$$C_{ijkl}:=2\bigl(l_{j[k}E_{l]i}-l_{i[k}E_{l]j}\bigr)-2\bigl(U_{[k}B_{l]p}\epsilon^p{}_{ij}+U_{[i}B_{j]p}\epsilon^p{}_{kl}\bigr),$$
with brackets of weight $\tfrac12$ and $l_{ij}=h_{ij}-U_iU_j$; this expression
is the **reconstruction** of a Weyl tensor from a pair $(E,B)$ of symmetric
spatial trace-free fields. The verification that the reconstructed tensor has
the curvature antisymmetries, pair symmetry, cyclic identity and zero traces —
and that its electric and magnetic parts recover $(E,B)$ — is the content of
[[lem-gr-dust-weyl-reconstruction-from-electric-magnetic]].

The definition fixes the objects and conventions only; the evolution and
subsidiary equations, the initial-data determination and the local existence
theorem are proved in the items named above and in
[[lem-gr-dust-reduced-evolution-equations]] and
[[thm-gr-dust-local-evolution]].

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $r,s\ge0$ be integers.

**(a) Tensors at a point.** For $p\in M$, the tangent space $T_pM$ is the real
vector space of derivations at $p$
([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]) and the cotangent space is
its algebraic dual, $T_p^*M=(T_pM)^*$
([[def-cotangent-space-and-cotangent-bundle-as-a-disjoint-union]]). A **type
$(r,s)$ tensor at $p$** is a multilinear map

$$T_p:(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\longrightarrow\mathbb R,$$

in the sense of [[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]:
the first $r$ arguments are covectors and the last $s$ are vectors. In
particular a type $(1,0)$ tensor is a vector, a type $(0,1)$ tensor is a
covector and a type $(0,2)$ tensor is a bilinear form, so the covariant
$2$-tensors of [[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]] are exactly the
type $(0,2)$ tensors of this definition.

**(b) The tensor bundle and smooth fields.** The **type $(r,s)$ tensor bundle**
$T^r_sM$ is the disjoint union of the fibres $T^r_sM|_p=\operatorname{Mult}((T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s,\mathbb R)$
over $p\in M$ ([[def-type-r-s-tensor-bundle]]); it carries the smooth
vector-bundle structure defined by the tensor-coordinate change rules
([[thm-tensor-transition-laws-define-a-smooth-vector-bundle]]). A **smooth
tensor field of type $(r,s)$** on $M$ is a family $T=(T_p)_{p\in M}$ assigning
to each $p$ a type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$, such that for every smooth chart
$(U,x)$ of the maximal smooth atlas the **component functions**

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}(q):=T_q\bigl(dx^{a_1}|_q,\dots,dx^{a_r}|_q,\ \partial_{b_1}|_q,\dots,\partial_{b_s}|_q\bigr),\qquad q\in U,$$

are $C^\infty$ on $U$; here the coordinate derivations
$\partial_b|_q=\partial/\partial x^b|_q$ form a basis of $T_qM$
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]) and the
coordinate differentials $dx^a|_q$ form the dual basis of $T_q^*M$
([[thm-coordinate-differentials-form-the-dual-cotangent-basis]]). This is
equivalent to $T$ being a smooth section of $T^r_sM$ in the sense of
[[def-smooth-tensor-field]]: the component functions are the frame
coefficients of the section in the local frame induced by the chart. The
smoothness condition is independent of the chosen smooth atlas and the
components in two overlapping charts are related by the transformation law
proved in the lemma on this page; the definition is therefore chart
independent rather than merely chart-wise.

**(c) Index conventions.** Indices are written $a,b,c,\dots$ for components in
a chart, with the Einstein summation convention: a repeated index, once upper
and once lower, is summed over $0,1,2,3$. An upper index is a contravariant
slot in which a covector is evaluated, a lower index a covariant slot in which
a vector is evaluated. Slots are moved between these positions with the
musical isomorphisms $\flat_p,\sharp_p$ of
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]; for example, lowering the
first slot of a type $(1,1)$ field uses $(g^\flat T)^a{}_b=g_{ac}T^c{}_b$ and
raising uses $g^{ac}$. This is an identification of slots, not a change of the
field into a field of another kind, and it uses the metric nondegeneracy.

**(d) Scope.** The definition is purely local and chart-based; no global
triviality of $T^r_sM$, no global frame and no choice of metric-compatible
fields is assumed or implied. All fields are smooth ($C^\infty$); no
lower-regularity or distributional tensor field is defined here. The smooth
structure of the tangent bundle, and hence of $T^r_sM$
([[thm-tensor-transition-laws-define-a-smooth-vector-bundle]]), inherits the
axiom $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]] recorded with
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]; the component formulation of smoothness
itself makes no choice.

Work in the reduction conventions of
[[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]], so a tentative frame
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$, its dual coframe $\theta^i$ and tentative connection
coefficients $\Gamma_i{}^k{}_j$ are given.

**(a) Connection forms.** The **connection $1$-forms** are
$\omega^i{}_j:=\Gamma_k{}^i{}_j\,\theta^k$, and the **torsion $2$-forms** and
**curvature $2$-forms** are the Cartan expressions
$$\Theta^i:=d\theta^i+\omega^i{}_j\wedge\theta^j,\qquad \Omega^i{}_j:=d\omega^i{}_j+\omega^i{}_k\wedge\omega^k{}_j .$$
The exterior derivatives are those of the frame-coordinate calculus, and the
wedge products are on the coframe; components are denoted
$\Theta^i=\tfrac12\Theta^i{}_{jk}\theta^j\wedge\theta^k$ and similarly for
$\Omega$. The actual curvature uses the frame bracket in its component formula:
$R^i{}_{jkl}=\partial_k\Gamma_l{}^i{}_j-\partial_l\Gamma_k{}^i{}_j+\Gamma_k{}^i{}_m\Gamma_l{}^m{}_j-\Gamma_l{}^i{}_m\Gamma_k{}^m{}_j-\Gamma_m{}^i{}_j\,[e_k,e_l]^m$,
not the antisymmetrized connection coefficients alone, precisely so that no
torsion conclusion is assumed.

**(b) Curvature residual.** With the prescribed curvature $R^{\mathrm{pre}}$
of [[def-gr-dust-electric-magnetic-weyl-variables-and-schouten]] the
**curvature residual $2$-forms** are
$$\Delta^i{}_j:=\Omega^i{}_j-\tfrac12R^{\mathrm{pre}\,i}{}_{jkl}\,\theta^k\wedge\theta^l .$$

**(c) Zero quantities.** The **zero quantities** of the reduction are the
collections
$$z:=\bigl(T^i{}_{jk},\ \Delta^i{}_{jkl},\ F_{jkl},\ q_k\bigr),$$
namely the frame components of the torsion, of the curvature residual, of the
Bianchi residual $F_{jkl}=\nabla^i(C_{ijkl}+S\text{-terms})$ of
[[lem-gr-dust-reduced-evolution-equations]] and the flux quantity
$q_k:=\kappa^{-1}\nabla_aT^a{}_k$ of the matter model. The reduced system sets
$z=0$; the identities satisfied by $z$ off the reduced system, and the theorem
that $z=0$ on the domain of dependence of an initial surface on which $z=0$
and the constraints hold, are proved in
[[thm-gr-dust-subsidiary-and-residual-vanishing]].

Work in the reduction conventions of [[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]]
and with the zero quantities $z=(T,\Delta,F,q)$ of
[[def-gr-dust-torsion-and-curvature-residuals]]; assume the gauge conditions
$e_0=U$, $\Gamma_0{}^i{}_j=0$ and $q_k=0$ of that item and the reduced system of
[[lem-gr-dust-reduced-evolution-equations]], so that $P_{ij}=Q_{ij}=0$,
$T^0{}_{ab}=0=\Delta^i{}_{j0a}$ and the transport equations hold. Then:

**(a) [Cartan identities]** exterior differentiation of the structure equations
gives exactly $D_\omega\Theta^i=\Omega^i{}_j\wedge\theta^j$ and
$D_\omega\Omega^i{}_j=0$; and the algebraic Bianchi identity of the prescribed
curvature gives $R^{\mathrm{pre}}\wedge\theta=0$;

**(b) [reduction identities]** $\iota_U\Theta=0$ and $\iota_U\Delta=0$
identically; consequently the first Cartan identity gives a transport equation
for the spatial torsion, $e_0(\Theta^a{}_{ib})=N(z)$, and the spatial
derivatives of the vanishing time components may be dropped;

**(c) [commutator identity]** for a tensor field $A$,
$$(\nabla_i\nabla_j-\nabla_j\nabla_i)A=\Omega_{ij}\cdot A-\Theta_{ij}{}^p\nabla_pA,$$
where the second covariant derivative differentiates its lower derivative index
covariantly as well as every index of $A$; a literal commutator omitting the
derivative-slot terms has instead a frame-bracket term and is not this identity;

**(d) [F splitting]** with $P_i=F_{0i0}$ and
$Q_i=-\tfrac12\epsilon_i{}^{kl}F_{0kl}$ one has
$$F_{jkl}=2U_jP_{[k}U_{l]}+h_{j[k}P_{l]}+Q_i\bigl(U_j\epsilon^i{}_{kl}-\epsilon^i{}_{j[k}U_{l]}\bigr)-2P_{j[k}U_{l]}-Q_{ji}\epsilon^i{}_{kl}-\tfrac12\kappa\,h_{j[k}q_{l]}-\tfrac13\kappa\,q\,h_{j[k}U_{l]},$$
with $q=U(r)+r\chi$ and $q_l$ the spatial part of the zero vector; the four rest-frame components $F_{0a0},F_{0ab},F_{a0b},F_{abc}$ are recovered by $P,Q$, the symmetric tracefree evolution equations, the traces $q,q_a$ and the curvature cyclic/trace relations, so every Bianchi residual is represented;

**(e) [divergence identity]** the double divergence of the reconstructed Weyl part satisfies
$$\nabla^jF_{jkl}=-\Delta^p{}_{[i}{}^{i}{}_{j}C^{j]}{}_{pkl}+C^{ij}{}_{p[l}\Delta^p{}_{k]ij}+\tfrac12\Theta_i{}^p{}_j\nabla_pC^{ij}{}_{kl}+\Delta^p{}_{[l}{}^j{}_{k]}S_{pj}-\Delta^p{}_j{}^j{}_{[k}S_{l]p}+\nabla_pS^j{}_{[l}\Theta_{k]}{}^p{}_j,$$
every term of which contains an undifferentiated residual $\Theta$ or $\Delta$ times a smooth coefficient built from the reduced solution or its derivatives (in particular no untracked derivatives of residuals);

**(f) [closed subsidiary system]** the components (b), (d), (e) together with the identity $D_\omega\Delta=-D_\omega R^{\mathrm{pre}}$ expressed through $F$ and the conservation of the prescribed Schouten tensor form a closed linear homogeneous first-order system in $(\Theta,\Delta,P,Q)$ with smooth locally bounded coefficients: the spatial torsion and the spatial curvature residual satisfy transport equations along $U$, the pair $(P,Q)$ satisfies the symmetric-hyperbolic curl pair
$$0=\mathcal L_UP_k+\tfrac12\epsilon_k{}^{ij}D_iQ_j+N(z),\qquad 0=\mathcal L_UQ_k-\tfrac12\epsilon_k{}^{ij}D_iP_j+N(z),$$
with curl speed at most $\tfrac12$ and transport speed zero, and its time matrix is positive definite on the spacelike initial surface; hence by the energy uniqueness of the local well-posedness theorem the residuals vanish from zero initial data: if $z=0$ on a spacelike surface and the constraints hold there, then $z=0$ on the domain of determination;

**(g) [conclusion]** zero residuals imply that the tentative connection is torsion-free and metric-compatible, hence Levi--Civita; that the reconstructed curvature is the actual curvature, with Ricci trace the prescribed Einstein Ricci and all remaining Bianchi constraints satisfied; hence the metric solves the full Einstein-dust field equation.

derivations.claim: ((a): curvature data.) In the normal-adapted tetrad, the Gauss equation of [L1] expresses the spatial curvature $R_{ijkl}$ through $R^h_{ijkl},K$; the Codazzi equation gives the mixed components $R_{0ijk}$; the Ricci equation and the Ricci trace give $R_{0i0j}$'s symmetric part; and the Hamiltonian and momentum constraints are the remaining Ricci equations. Inserting these components into the Weyl tensor and expanding in the $U$-frame by the Lorentz transformation [L2] yields $E_{ij}$ and $B_{ij}$ uniquely, because the map from Weyl tensors to $(E,B)$ is injective ([[lem-gr-dust-weyl-reconstruction-from-electric-magnetic]]).

((b): connection data.) In the $U$-frame, the spatial components of the connection are the metric connection of the induced spatial geometry plus terms involving $K$ and the spatial derivatives of $U$; the frame components along $U$ of the connection are the components $\chi_{ij}$ of $\nabla U$, determined by $K$ and $U$'s spatial derivatives; and the parallel gauge sets $\Gamma_0{}^i{}_j=0$. Since $U$ is transverse to $\Sigma$, these data determine every initial connection component.

((c): zero initial residuals.) The zero time components are the reduction identities [L3]; the purely spatial torsion vanishes because the tentative connection agrees with the Levi--Civita connection of the induced spatial metric on tangential vectors; the curvature residual vanishes because the constructed curvature equals the prescribed one by (a).

((d): tilted initialization.) Restrict the dual Bianchi identity to tangent triples and use $\Delta|_\Sigma=0$ to get $\zeta^jF_{jkl}=0$ for the future-positive timelike conormal $\zeta$; substituting the $F$-splitting of [[thm-gr-dust-subsidiary-and-residual-vanishing]] clause (d) into the $(k,0)$ and spatial dual components gives the displayed system up to orientation signs. The block is symmetric; by [L4] its quadratic form on $(P,Q)$ is at least $(z-\tfrac12|v|)(|P|^2+|Q|^2)>0$ unless $P=Q=0$, because $z>|v|$ and $|v|\ge\tfrac12|v|$. Hence $P=Q=0$ on $\Sigma$. citations.quote:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a
spacelike embedded hypersurface in the sense of
[[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (a), so that
$\Sigma$ is an embedded three-dimensional submanifold
([[def-embedded-submanifold-and-slice-chart]]) and the restriction of $g_p$
to $T_p\Sigma$ is positive definite for every $p\in\Sigma$
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). In the notation of
[[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]] clause (a), whose claims
this lemma establishes:

**(a) The future unit normal.** For every $p\in\Sigma$ the orthogonal
complement $T_p\Sigma^{\perp}$ is one-dimensional, nondegenerate for $g_p$,
and negative definite: every nonzero $u\in T_p\Sigma^{\perp}$ is timelike,
$g_p(u,u)<0$. Hence there is exactly one $n_p\in T_p\Sigma^{\perp}$ with
$g_p(n_p,n_p)=-1$ and $g_p(n_p,N_p)<0$.

**(b) Smoothness along the hypersurface.** The assignment $p\mapsto n_p$ is
smooth along $\Sigma$: for every $p\in\Sigma$ there are an open neighborhood
$O$ of $p$ in $M$ and a smooth vector field $\tilde n$ on $O$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]) with
$\tilde n|_{\Sigma\cap O}=n|_{\Sigma\cap O}$, and for any two such local
extensions the covariant derivative at a point of $\Sigma$ in a direction
tangent to $\Sigma$ agrees. Thus for $V\in T_p\Sigma$ the vector
$\nabla_Vn\in T_pM$ is well defined as $\nabla_{\tilde X}\tilde n|_p$ for any
smooth extensions $\tilde n$ of $n$ and $\tilde X$ of a tangent field with
$\tilde X_p=V$ ([[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]).

**(c) The induced metric and second fundamental form.** The **induced
metric** $h_p(V,W):=g_p(V,W)$ is a smooth Riemannian metric on $\Sigma$, and
$$K_p(V,W):=g_p(\nabla_Vn,W)\qquad(V,W\in T_p\Sigma)$$
(the **second fundamental form**) defines a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field $K$ on $\Sigma$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) with
$$K_p(V,W)=-g_p(\nabla_VW,n_p),$$
where $\nabla_VW$ is the ambient covariant derivative at $p$ of any smooth
extension of a tangent field with value $W$ at $p$, in the direction of any
extension with value $V$ at $p$.

**(d) The shape operator.** The endomorphism $S_p:T_p\Sigma\to T_p\Sigma$
defined by $h_p(S_pV,W)=K_p(V,W)$ for all $W\in T_p\Sigma$ is well defined,
linear and self-adjoint for the positive definite form $h_p$, and the
Weingarten relation $\nabla_Vn=S_pV$ holds for every $V\in T_p\Sigma$.

For an affine connection as in [[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]] and coordinates $(x^1,\ldots,x^n)$, its **Christoffel symbols** in this chart are the unique smooth functions $\Gamma^k{}_{ij}$ such that
$$\nabla_{\partial_i}\partial_j=\sum_k\Gamma^k{}_{ij}\partial_k.$$
The first lower index $i$ is the differentiating direction and the second lower index $j$ labels the differentiated vector field. In the coordinate frame, the one-forms from [[def-connection-one-form-in-a-local-frame]] are $\omega^k{}_j=\sum_i\Gamma^k{}_{ij}\,dx^i$. A different chart generally has different symbols. This definition asserts neither symmetry in $i,j$ nor tensorial transformation.

For dimension one there is one smooth coefficient $\Gamma^1{}_{11}$; in dimension zero there are no coefficients. All statements are local, and at a boundary chart the derivatives are the smooth up-to-boundary coordinate derivatives.

For an affine connection as in [[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]] and coordinates $(x^1,\ldots,x^n)$, its **Christoffel symbols** in this chart are the unique smooth functions $\Gamma^k{}_{ij}$ such that
$$\nabla_{\partial_i}\partial_j=\sum_k\Gamma^k{}_{ij}\partial_k.$$
The first lower index $i$ is the differentiating direction and the second lower index $j$ labels the differentiated vector field. In the coordinate frame, the one-forms from [[def-connection-one-form-in-a-local-frame]] are $\omega^k{}_j=\sum_i\Gamma^k{}_{ij}\,dx^i$. A different chart generally has different symbols. This definition asserts neither symmetry in $i,j$ nor tensorial transformation.

For dimension one there is one smooth coefficient $\Gamma^1{}_{11}$; in dimension zero there are no coefficients. All statements are local, and at a boundary chart the derivatives are the smooth up-to-boundary coordinate derivatives.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\nabla$ be an affine connection
on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]). Smooth vector fields
are smooth sections of the tangent bundle
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]); as there, their use
rests on the canonical smooth structure of $TM$, which assumes the axiom
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]]. This is the only use of that
axiom in this definition.

**(a) Metric compatibility.** The connection $\nabla$ is **$g$-compatible**, or
**compatible with the metric** $g$, when for all smooth vector fields $X,Y,Z$ on
$M$ the identity of smooth functions

$$X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$$

holds on $M$. Here $g(Y,Z)$ is the smooth function $p\mapsto g_p(Y_p,Z_p)$ and
$X$ acts on functions as a derivation; the identity uses only the action of
$\nabla$ on vector fields and requires no extension of $\nabla$ to tensor
fields. When such an extension is available, this identity is the statement
$\nabla_Xg=0$, and the compatibility of $\nabla$ with the inverse metric
$g^{-1}$ follows; neither statement is part of this definition.

**(b) Torsion freedom.** The **torsion** of $\nabla$ is the tangent-valued
$2$-tensor $T(X,Y)=\nabla_XY-\nabla_YX-[X,Y]$ of
[[def-torsion-tensor-of-an-affine-connection]], with bracket as in
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]]. The connection is **torsion-free**
when $T(X,Y)=0$ for all smooth $X,Y$, that is, when
$\nabla_XY-\nabla_YX=[X,Y]$ identically.

**(c) Metric-selected connections.** A **metric-selected connection** for
$(M,g)$ is an affine connection on $M$ that is both torsion-free and
$g$-compatible. Equivalently, it is an element of the class

$$\operatorname{LC}(M,g):=\{\nabla:\nabla\text{ is an affine connection on }M,\ \nabla\text{ is torsion-free and }g\text{-compatible}\}.$$

The name records that the pair of conditions selects the connection out of all
affine connections; it is the pair of conditions imposed on the connection that
conventional general relativity uses, and the connection so selected is called
the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

For an affine connection as in [[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]] and coordinates $(x^1,\ldots,x^n)$, its **Christoffel symbols** in this chart are the unique smooth functions $\Gamma^k{}_{ij}$ such that
$$\nabla_{\partial_i}\partial_j=\sum_k\Gamma^k{}_{ij}\partial_k.$$
The first lower index $i$ is the differentiating direction and the second lower index $j$ labels the differentiated vector field. In the coordinate frame, the one-forms from [[def-connection-one-form-in-a-local-frame]] are $\omega^k{}_j=\sum_i\Gamma^k{}_{ij}\,dx^i$. A different chart generally has different symbols. Let $M$ and $N$ be smooth manifolds, let $F:M\to N$ be a map, let $p\in M$ and
let $r\in\mathbb N_0\cup\{\infty\}$, where $\mathbb N_0=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$.
For $m,q\in\mathbb N_0$ and an open set $E\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, a map
$g:E\to\mathbb R^q$ is **of class $C^r$** as follows. When $m=0$, every such
map is declared $C^r$. When $m\ge1$, each component $g_l$ with $l<q$ must be
$C^r$ in the sense of
[[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]]; when $q=0$ this
component condition is vacuous.
Suppose $F$ is continuous at $p$. Then $F$ is **of class $C^r$ at $p$** when
there are smooth charts $(U,\varphi)$ of $M$ at $p$ and $(V,\psi)$ of $N$ at
$F(p)$ with $F(U)\subseteq V$ such that the coordinate representative

$$\psi\circ F\circ\varphi^{-1}:\varphi(U)\longrightarrow\psi(V)$$

([[def-coordinate-representation-of-a-map]]) is of class $C^r$ on a
neighbourhood of $\varphi(p)$ in this componentwise Euclidean sense. By
[[lem-chart-independence-of-c-r-smoothness]], this condition is independent of
the chosen charts: if one such representative is $C^r$, then every one is, so
"some charts" may be read as "any charts". A map is **$C^r$ on an open set**
$W\subseteq M$ when it is continuous on $W$ and $C^r$ at every point of $W$. A
map that is $C^r$ for every finite $r$ — equivalently $C^\infty$ — is called
**smooth**; the term **$C^r$ map between smooth manifolds** is reserved for the
case where $F$ is continuous and the representative condition holds at every
point of $M$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and let
$U\subseteq M$ be an open set carrying a fixed smooth **background metric**
$\bar g$ with Levi-Civita connection $\bar\nabla$
([[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), whose Christoffel
symbols in any chart are $\bar\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]); the same symbol
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ denotes those of $g$. Let $\kappa>0$ and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$
be constants and let $T$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $U$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]), the **matter stress-energy
tensor**, with $T=g^{ab}T_{ab}$ its metric trace
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]).

**(a) Gauge vector.** The **harmonic-gauge vector field** of the pair
$(g,\bar g)$ is the smooth vector field
$$H^a:=g^{bc}\bigl(\Gamma^a{}_{bc}-\bar\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\bigr) .$$
The difference of the connection coefficients is a $(1,2)$-tensor, so $H$ is a
well-defined smooth vector field independent of the chart used to express the
symbols ([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]).

**(b) Reduced Einstein equation.** The **reduced Einstein equation** for the
pair $(g,T)$ with respect to $\bar g$ is the second-order quasilinear system
$$\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\nabla_{(a}H_{b)}=\kappa\bigl(T_{ab}-\tfrac12Tg_{ab}\bigr)+\Lambda g_{ab},$$
where $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ is the Ricci tensor of $g$
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]),
$H_b=g_{bc}H^c$ and $\nabla_{(a}H_{b)}=\tfrac12(\nabla_aH_b+\nabla_bH_a)$.

**(c) Reduced solutions.** A **reduced solution** on $U$ is a pair $(g,T)$ of a
smooth Lorentzian metric and a smooth symmetric $2$-tensor on $U$ satisfying
(b) for the fixed background $\bar g$.

**(d) Einstein residual.** The **Einstein residual** of a pair $(g,T)$ is the
smooth symmetric $2$-tensor
$$E_{ab}:=G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}-\kappa T_{ab},\qquad G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12Sg_{ab},$$
with $S=g^{ab}\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ the scalar curvature
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). The pair solves the Einstein
equation exactly when $E=0$.

**(e) Constraint equations.** If $g$ is defined on a neighborhood of a spacelike
hypersurface $\Sigma$ with future unit normal field $\mathfrak n$ and tangential
frame $(e_i)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]]), the
**constraint residuals** are the functions $E(\mathfrak n,\mathfrak n)$ and
$E(\mathfrak n,e_i)$ on $\Sigma$; that these are the normal and
normal-tangential projections of the field equation, and that they agree with
the Hamiltonian and momentum constraint equations of the initial data, is
recorded in [[lem-gr-constraint-projections]] and
[[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]].

The definition introduces the objects only. The principal part of (b), its
first-order symmetric hyperbolic reduction, the identity expressing $E$ through
$H$, the wave equation satisfied by $H$ and the propagation of the constraint
residuals are proved in [[lem-gr-reduced-einstein-principal-part]],
[[thm-gr-reduced-einstein-local-existence]],
[[lem-gr-einstein-residual-and-subsidiary-identity]] and
[[thm-gr-harmonic-constraint-propagation]].

derivations.claim: (Existence of the metric germ and its slice geometry (a).) Prescribe a smooth metric on a product neighborhood whose value and $s$-derivative on $\Sigma$ are the displayed jet and whose higher jets are chosen arbitrarily smooth; such a metric germ exists because a smooth function and its first normal derivative can be prescribed on a hypersurface and extended smoothly. On $\Sigma$, $g_{00}=-1$, $g_{0i}=0$, $g_{ij}=h_{ij}$, so $g$ restricted to $T\Sigma$ is $h$ and $\partial_s$ is a unit timelike vector orthogonal to $\Sigma$; by [L1] it is the future unit normal (with the orientation of the statement) and the second fundamental form is $\tfrac12\partial_sg_{ij}=K_{ij}$. This is (a).

(Computation of $H^0$.) Insert the Christoffel components [L2], [L3] into [L4]: $H^0=g^{00}(\Gamma^0{}_{00}-\bar\Gamma^0{}_{00})+g^{ij}(\Gamma^0{}_{ij}-\bar\Gamma^0{}_{ij})+2g^{0i}(\Gamma^0{}_{0i}-\bar\Gamma^0{}_{0i})=-(\operatorname{tr}_hK-0)+h^{ij}(K_{ij}-0)+0=-\operatorname{tr}_hK+\operatorname{tr}_hK=0$ on $\Sigma$.

(Computation of $H^i$.) Similarly $H^i=g^{00}(\Gamma^i{}_{00}-\bar\Gamma^i{}_{00})+g^{jk}(\Gamma^i{}_{jk}-\bar\Gamma^i{}_{jk})+2g^{0j}(\Gamma^i{}_{0j}-\bar\Gamma^i{}_{0j})=-(0-0)+h^{jk}(\Gamma^h{}^i{}_{jk}-\Gamma^h{}^i{}_{jk})+2\cdot0=0$ on $\Sigma$, using that the tangential Christoffel symbols of $g$ on $\Sigma$ agree with those of $h$ and hence with those of the background because $h_0|_\Sigma=h$ and tangential derivatives agree. This is (b).

No cardinality-one case is separated: the arguments treat general finite or countable families and the one-element case is included without special treatment.
