$\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a smooth spacelike hypersurface
([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]) with future unit normal
field $\mathfrak n$ and tangential frame $(e_i)$
([[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]), and let
$U$ be an open neighborhood of $\Sigma$ carrying a smooth background metric
$\bar g$ and a smooth symmetric tensor $T$ with $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $U$. Let
$H$ and $E$ be the gauge vector and Einstein residual of
[[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]. Suppose:

1. $(g,T)$ solves the reduced Einstein equation on $U$;
2. $H=0$ on $\Sigma$;
3. the constraint residuals vanish on $\Sigma$: $E(\mathfrak n,\mathfrak n)=0$
   and $E(\mathfrak n,e_i)=0$ for all $i$.

Then there is an open neighborhood $W\subseteq U$ of $\Sigma$ on which $H=0$ and
$E=0$; consequently $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$ on $W$, so $g$ solves
the Einstein equation with the prescribed matter tensor there.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a spacelike embedded hypersurface with future unit normal
$n$, induced metric $h$ and second fundamental form
$K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]],
[[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]), and let
$G$ and $S$ be the Einstein tensor and scalar curvature of $g$
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Then, at every $p\in\Sigma$
and for all tangential vectors $X,Y,Z,W\in T_p\Sigma$:

**(a) Gauss equation.**
$$R^g(X,Y,Z,W)=R^h(X,Y,Z,W)+K(X,Z)K(Y,W)-K(X,W)K(Y,Z);$$

**(b) Codazzi equation.**
$$g\bigl(R^g(X,Y)Z,n\bigr)=(\nabla^h_XK)(Y,Z)-(\nabla^h_YK)(X,Z);$$

**(c) normal projections.**
$$G(n,n)=\tfrac12\bigl(S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|_h^2\bigr),\qquad G(n,Y)=(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-\nabla^h_Y(\operatorname{tr}_hK);$$

**(d) constraint equations.** If in addition the field equation
$G+\Lambda g=\kappa T$ holds at $p$ for a smooth symmetric $2$-tensor $T$ and
constants $\kappa,\Lambda$, then
$$S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|^2_h=2\Lambda+2\kappa\,T(n,n),\qquad \operatorname{div}_hK(Y)-\nabla^h_Y(\operatorname{tr}_hK)=\kappa\,T(n,Y)$$
for every tangential $Y$.

Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold, let $h$ be a smooth Riemannian metric
on $\Sigma$, let $K$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor on $\Sigma$, and
let $\mathcal D$ be fixed smooth initial data for a symmetric $2$-tensor $T$ on
$\Sigma$ (its value and the value of its normal derivative in the models below).
Let $(M,g,N)$ and $(M',g',N')$ be two time-oriented smooth Lorentzian
four-manifolds with spacelike embeddings $j,j'$ of $\Sigma$ inducing the
same $(h,K)$, carrying smooth symmetric tensors $T,T'$ satisfying the field
equations
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab},\qquad G'_{ab}+\Lambda g'_{ab}=\kappa T'_{ab}$$
on neighborhoods of the images of $\Sigma$, with $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$,
$\nabla'^aT'_{ab}=0$ there and with equal initial data $\mathcal D$ for
$T,T'$ (transported by the embeddings).

Then there are open neighborhoods $U$ of $j(\Sigma)$ and $U'$ of
$j'(\Sigma)$ and a smooth diffeomorphism $\varphi:U\to U'$ such that:

1. $\varphi(j(\sigma))=j'(\sigma)$ for every $\sigma\in\Sigma$;
2. $\varphi^*(g')=g$ and $\varphi^*(T')=T$ on $U$;
3. $\varphi$ carries the time orientation of $N$ to that of $N'$.

Thus any two solutions of the field equation arising from the same constrained
geometric data are locally isometric near the initial surface by a
data-fixing time-orientation-preserving isometry. Here an **isometry fixing the
data** means a smooth diffeomorphism satisfying (2) (the definition is given
explicitly by these equations; no separate notion of Lorentzian isometry is
presupposed).

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open
interval with $0\in I$ and let $B\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be an open ball centred
at $0$ of radius $R>0$ with a fixed Euclidean norm $|\cdot|$. Suppose
$(s,\sigma):U\to I\times B$ is a diffeomorphism of an open set $U\subseteq M$
onto $I\times B$ ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]) such
that, writing $v^s:=ds(v)$ and $v^\sigma:=d\sigma(v)$ for $v\in T_qM$,
$q\in U$:

**(C1)** $\partial/\partial s$ is future timelike and every level set
$s^{-1}(c)$ is spacelike;

**(C2)** there is $K\ge1$ such that every future causal $v\in T_qM$, $q\in U$,
satisfies $|v^\sigma|\le K\,v^s$.

On the open submanifold $U$ with the induced metric and time orientation
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]), let
$$D^\pm_U(S):=\bigl\{p\in U:\ \text{every past- (respectively future-) inextendible causal curve in }U\text{ through }p\text{ meets }S\bigr\}$$
be the domains of dependence of the spacelike slice
$S:=s^{-1}(0)=\{0\}\times B$ in the sense of
[[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (d), computed in
$U$. Then:

**(a)** $D^+_U(S)\subseteq\{s\ge0\}$ and $D^-_U(S)\subseteq\{s\le0\}$;

**(b)** the open set $Q:=\{q\in U:|s(q)|+K\,|\sigma(q)|<R\}$ is contained in
$D^+_U(S)\cup D^-_U(S)$; more precisely
$Q\cap\{s>0\}\subseteq D^+_U(S)$ and $Q\cap\{s<0\}\subseteq D^-_U(S)$, and $Q$
is a neighbourhood of $S$ in $U$;

**(c)** the open set $W:=\mathrm{int}_U\bigl(D^+_U(S)\cup D^-_U(S)\bigr)$
satisfies $Q\subseteq W$, and $S$ is a Cauchy set of the open submanifold
$(W,g|_W)$: every causal curve in $W$ that is inextendible in $W$ meets $S$
in exactly one parameter value. Consequently, $(W,g|_W,N|_W)$ is globally
hyperbolic by [[thm-gr-cauchy-surface-implies-globally-hyperbolic]].

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with the
causal curves of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]], and let
$S\subseteq M$.

**(a) Spacelike hypersurfaces.** A subset $\Sigma\subseteq M$ is a **spacelike
embedded hypersurface** when it is an embedded three-dimensional submanifold
of $M$ ([[def-embedded-submanifold-and-slice-chart]]) such that the
restriction of $g_p$ to $T_p\Sigma\times T_p\Sigma$ is positive definite for
every $p\in\Sigma$; equivalently, every nonzero vector tangent to $\Sigma$ is
spacelike ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). A spacelike
embedded hypersurface is automatically a nondegenerate hypersurface, so its
$g$-orthogonal complement in $T_pM$ is one-dimensional and nondegenerate, and
it carries a unique future-directed unit timelike normal; that normal is
constructed where it is used, not here.

**(b) Achronality and acausality.** $S$ is **achronal** when no two distinct
points $p,q\in S$ satisfy $p\ll q$ or $q\ll p$; $S$ is **acausal** when no two
distinct points $p,q\in S$ satisfy $p\le q$ or $q\le p$. Every acausal set is
achronal, since $p\ll q$ implies $p\le q$.

**(c) Cauchy sets.** $S$ is a **Cauchy set** when for every inextendible
causal curve $\gamma:I\to M$ the parameter set
$$\gamma^{-1}[S]:=\{t\in I:\gamma(t)\in S\}$$
has exactly one element. Because a strictly increasing continuous surjection
of intervals induces a bijection of parameter sets, this condition is
invariant under reparametrization
([[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (e)); it is stated in terms of
parameters rather than of the point set $\gamma(I)\cap S$, so that a closed
causal curve counts two visits to the same point as two parameter values. A
**Cauchy hypersurface** is a Cauchy set that is also a spacelike embedded
hypersurface in the sense of clause (a).

**(d) Domains of dependence.** For any $S\subseteq M$ define
$$D^+(S):=\{p\in M:\text{every past-inextendible causal curve through }p \text{ meets }S\},$$
and dually $D^-(S):=\{p\in M:\text{every future-inextendible causal curve
through }p\text{ meets }S\}$, where "meets $S$" means that some parameter
value is mapped into $S$, and $D(S):=D^+(S)\cup D^-(S)$ is the **domain of
dependence** of $S$.

**(e) Cauchy horizon.** For a closed set $S\subseteq M$ the **future Cauchy
horizon** is
$$H^+(S):=D^+(S)\setminus I^-(D^+(S)),$$
the set of points of $D^+(S)$ that are not chronologically preceded by any
point of $D^+(S)$; dually $H^-(S):=D^-(S)\setminus I^+(D^-(S))$, and the
**Cauchy horizon** is $H(S):=H^+(S)\cup H^-(S)$.

**(f) Scope.** These are mathematical definitions. Neither existence of
Cauchy sets nor any relation between the objects defined here is asserted.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and suppose there exists a Cauchy set
$S\subseteq M$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause
(c)): every inextendible causal curve meets $S$ in exactly one parameter
value. Then:

**(a)** there is no nonconstant future causal curve with equal endpoints
(so $(M,g,N)$ is causal and chronological in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (a));

**(b)** $(M,g,N)$ is strongly causal (clause (b) of that definition);

**(c)** for all $p,q\in M$ the causal diamond
$J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ is compact; consequently $(M,g,N)$ is globally
hyperbolic in the sense of clause (c) of that definition.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold that is globally hyperbolic in
the sense of [[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause
(c): strongly causal and with compact causal diamonds
$J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ for all $p,q\in M$. Let $h$ be the auxiliary metric of
[[thm-gr-auxiliary-complete-riemannian-metric]] and let $\le$, $J^\pm$ be the
relations of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. Then:

**(a)** the causal relation is closed: if $p_k\le q_k$ for all $k$ and
$p_k\to p$, $q_k\to q$, then $p\le q$; consequently $J^+(x)$ and $J^-(x)$
are closed for every $x$, and so are $J^+(K)$ and $J^-(K)$ for every compact
$K\subseteq M$;

**(b)** for all compact $K_1,K_2\subseteq M$ the set
$J^+(K_1)\cap J^-(K_2)$ is compact.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with the
causal curves and the relations $\le$, $\ll$, $I^{\pm}$, $J^{\pm}$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. All curves below are curves in
that sense.

**(a) Chronology and causality.** $(M,g,N)$ is **chronological** when there is
no $p\in M$ with $p\ll p$, equivalently when there is no nonconstant future
timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)$. It is **causal**
when there is no nonconstant future causal curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with
$\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)$; a nonconstant future causal curve with equal endpoints
is called a **closed causal curve**, and a closed future timelike curve is
called a **closed timelike curve**.

**(b) Strong causality.** $(M,g,N)$ is **strongly causal** when for every
$p\in M$ and every open set $U\subseteq M$ with $p\in U$ there is an open set
$V$ with $p\in V\subseteq U$ such that for every future causal curve
$\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ and all $a\le s<t\le b$ with $\gamma(s)\in V$ and
$\gamma(t)\in V$ one has $\gamma([s,t])\subseteq V$. Thus no causal curve can
leave $V$ and later re-enter it; a set $V$ with this property for all causal
curves is called **causally convex for causal curves that meet it twice**.

**(c) Global hyperbolicity.** $(M,g,N)$ is **globally hyperbolic** when it is
strongly causal and for all $p,q\in M$ the **causal diamond**
$J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ is compact in the subspace topology
([[def-compact-space]]).

**(d) Time functions.** A **time function** on $(M,g,N)$ is a function
$u:M\to\mathbb R$ which is continuous ([[def-continuity-real]]) and satisfies
$u(\gamma(a))<u(\gamma(b))$ for every future causal curve
$\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $a<b$ that is not constant on $[a,b]$.

**(e) Temporal functions.** A **temporal function** on $(M,g,N)$ is a smooth
function $u:M\to\mathbb R$ ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]])
whose gradient is past-directed timelike: writing $du$ for its differential
([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]) and $\nabla u$ for the vector field
with $g(\nabla u,X)=du(X)$ for every smooth vector field $X$, constructed from
the inverse metric of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]], one
has
$$g(\nabla u,\nabla u)<0\qquad\text{and}\qquad du(N)=g(\nabla u,N)>0 .$$
The first inequality says that the gradient is nowhere zero and timelike; the
second fixes it as past-directed for the chosen time orientation. No level set
of a temporal function is asserted here to be a hypersurface or to be
spacelike, and no relation between temporal functions and compactness is
asserted; those claims are proved separately where they are used.

**(f) Scope and conventions.** These are mathematical conditions on the
Lorentzian model. Different sources define global hyperbolicity by equivalent
but differently phrased conditions; this page fixes the formulation of (c)
and proves the implications it uses. In particular no equivalence between
global hyperbolicity and the existence of a Cauchy hypersurface is asserted
by this definition, and the physical reading of strong causality or global
hyperbolicity as predictability of a classical model is adopted only in the
framework postulates.

Let $M^m$ be a smooth manifold, let $k\in\mathbb N$ satisfy $0\le k\le m$,
and let $S\subseteq M$. One says that $S$ is an **embedded $k$-dimensional
submanifold** of $M$ when for every $p\in S$ there
is a smooth chart $\varphi:U\to\varphi(U)\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ with $p\in U$
such that

$$\varphi(S\cap U)=\varphi(U)\cap(\mathbb R^k\times\{0\}).$$

Such a chart is a **slice chart** for $S$ at $p$. The topology on $S$ is the
subspace topology inherited from $M$ ([[def-subspace-topology-top]]).

The next lemma proves that the restricted slice charts define a smooth
$k$-manifold structure on $S$.

**(a) Spacelike hypersurfaces.** A subset $\Sigma\subseteq M$ is a **spacelike

**(d) Domains of dependence.** For any $S\subseteq M$ define

and dually $D^-(S):=\{p\in M:\text{every future-inextendible causal curve

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a
spacelike embedded hypersurface in the sense of
[[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (a), so that
$\Sigma$ is an embedded three-dimensional submanifold
([[def-embedded-submanifold-and-slice-chart]]) and the restriction of $g_p$
to $T_p\Sigma$ is positive definite for every $p\in\Sigma$
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). In the notation of
[[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]] clause (a), whose claims
this lemma establishes:

**(a) The future unit normal.** For every $p\in\Sigma$ the orthogonal
complement $T_p\Sigma^{\perp}$ is one-dimensional, nondegenerate for $g_p$,
and negative definite: every nonzero $u\in T_p\Sigma^{\perp}$ is timelike,
$g_p(u,u)<0$. Hence there is exactly one $n_p\in T_p\Sigma^{\perp}$ with
$g_p(n_p,n_p)=-1$ and $g_p(n_p,N_p)<0$.

**(b) Smoothness along the hypersurface.** The assignment $p\mapsto n_p$ is
smooth along $\Sigma$: for every $p\in\Sigma$ there are an open neighborhood
$O$ of $p$ in $M$ and a smooth vector field $\tilde n$ on $O$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]) with
$\tilde n|_{\Sigma\cap O}=n|_{\Sigma\cap O}$, and for any two such local
extensions the covariant derivative at a point of $\Sigma$ in a direction
tangent to $\Sigma$ agrees. Thus for $V\in T_p\Sigma$ the vector
$\nabla_Vn\in T_pM$ is well defined as $\nabla_{\tilde X}\tilde n|_p$ for any
smooth extensions $\tilde n$ of $n$ and $\tilde X$ of a tangent field with
$\tilde X_p=V$ ([[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]).

**(c) The induced metric and second fundamental form.** The **induced
metric** $h_p(V,W):=g_p(V,W)$ is a smooth Riemannian metric on $\Sigma$, and
$$K_p(V,W):=g_p(\nabla_Vn,W)\qquad(V,W\in T_p\Sigma)$$
(the **second fundamental form**) defines a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field $K$ on $\Sigma$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) with
$$K_p(V,W)=-g_p(\nabla_VW,n_p),$$
where $\nabla_VW$ is the ambient covariant derivative at $p$ of any smooth
extension of a tangent field with value $W$ at $p$, in the direction of any
extension with value $V$ at $p$.

**(d) The shape operator.** The endomorphism $S_p:T_p\Sigma\to T_p\Sigma$
defined by $h_p(S_pV,W)=K_p(V,W)$ for all $W\in T_p\Sigma$ is well defined,
linear and self-adjoint for the positive definite form $h_p$, and the
Weingarten relation $\nabla_Vn=S_pV$ holds for every $V\in T_p\Sigma$.

derivations.claim: (Local existence (a).) Fix $p\in\Sigma$ and a coordinate ball $O_p$ around $p$ small enough that a normal-coordinate product neighborhood of $O_p$ exists. By [L1] build the harmonic initial data for the metric variables on $O_p$, and extend the matter data $\psi_0$ to a smooth germ with the prescribed normal derivative; by [L2] the reduced system coupled to the matter reduction has a smooth solution on a product neighborhood of $O_p$; the gauge vector and the constraint residuals vanish on $O_p$, so by [L2] the solution satisfies the field equation and the matter equations there, and by construction the induced metric and second fundamental form of $O_p$ are $(h,K)$. This gives (a).

(Gluing (b), first part). For two coordinate balls $O_1,O_2$ with nonempty overlap, restrict both solutions to the overlap; both have induced data $(h,K)$ and satisfy the field and matter equations, so by [L3] there is a data-fixing isometry between neighborhoods of the overlap; in particular the metric and matter fields agree after applying the isometry, and since the isometry fixes the surface pointwise on the overlap it is the identity there; hence the two local solutions coincide on the overlap. Therefore the local solutions glue to a smooth solution $(g,\psi)$ on a neighborhood $W$ of $\Sigma$ with the stated properties.

(The surface is Cauchy on its domain of dependence (b), second part). Shrink $W$ to a product neighborhood $(-\epsilon,\epsilon)\times\Sigma$ of the normal coordinate $s$ in which the level sets of $s$ are spacelike. At $s=0$, $\Sigma$ is acausal (a causal curve from a point of $\Sigma$ to a different point of $\Sigma$ would have a nonpositive tangent at an interior minimum of $s$, contradicting its causal character). In a conically bounded product chart, [L4] gives local Cauchy neighborhoods around each point of $\Sigma$; since every inextendible causal curve through a nearby point enters the local cone region and meets the base patch, the domain of dependence of $\Sigma$ contains the open sets $\{|s|<\epsilon_p,\ d(x,\Sigma\text{-point})<\lambda(\epsilon_p-|s|)\}$ over finitely many charts covering a compact piece; hence every point of $\Sigma$ is interior to $D(\Sigma)\cap W$, and $D(\Sigma)\cap W$ is open. Every inextendible causal curve in $D(\Sigma)\cap W$ meets $\Sigma$ exactly once by the definition of the domain of dependence and acausality, so $\Sigma$ is a Cauchy hypersurface for that open neighborhood; by [L4] $D(\Sigma)\cap W$ is then globally hyperbolic with compact causal diamonds.
(Uniqueness (c).) This is exactly [L3].

boundaries.reason: No empty set, empty family or empty index range is formed: the quantified objects (points, fields, mode families, data sets) are nonempty by the hypotheses, and the proofs never split off an empty case.
The value zero is not a distinguished boundary of this claim: no step divides by a quantity that can vanish and no separate zero case is required.
No cardinality-one case is separated: the arguments treat general finite or countable families and the one-element case is included without special treatment.

The hypotheses exclude degenerate configurations: the metric is Lorentzian/nondegenerate, the time matrix or coefficient is positive definite, velocity fields are unit and nonzero where required, and no degenerate limit is claimed.
The assertions are local in open domains around the initial surface or open time intervals, and no endpoint behaviour (completeness, boundary extension or endpoint regularity) is claimed.
No nonconstructive selection from a family is made: the argument uses the objects named in the Given clause and the supplied maps, with at most finite choices.
The item states one-directional implications or constructions, not an equivalence, so no forward direction of an if-and-only-if is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice for the integral below
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let a perfect-fluid model on a Lorentzian manifold
be given with smooth equation of state $p=p(\epsilon)$ defined on an open
interval $J\subseteq\mathbb R$, with $\epsilon+p(\epsilon)>0$ and
$p'(\epsilon)>0$ for all $\epsilon\in J$
([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]). Fix a base point
$\epsilon_*\in J$ and define the **barotropic enthalpy variable**
$$r:J\to\mathbb R,\qquad r(\epsilon):=\int_{\epsilon_*}^{\epsilon}\frac{\sqrt{p'(z)}}{z+p(z)}\,dz .$$
The integrand is continuous on $J$ ([[thm-continuous-implies-integrable]]), so
$r$ is well defined and $C^1$ with $r'(\epsilon)=\sqrt{p'(\epsilon)}/(\epsilon+p(\epsilon))>0$
([[cor-ftc-integral-function-differentiable-almost-everywhere]]); hence $r$
maps $J$ diffeomorphically onto the open interval $r(J)$, and we write
$\epsilon(r)$ for its inverse and $c_s:=\sqrt{p'}$ for the **sound-speed
function**, so that $r'(\epsilon)=c_s(\epsilon)/(\epsilon+p(\epsilon))$ and
$c_s\in(0,1)$ when $0<p'<1$ is assumed.

The definition and the two displayed equivalences are the form in which the
fluid system is fed into [[lem-gr-barotropic-fluid-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]];
no existence theorem is asserted here.

Let a perfect-fluid model with smooth equation of state $p=p(\epsilon)$ satisfy
$\epsilon+p>0$ and $0<p'(\epsilon)<1$ on an open interval $J$, let
$r:J\to r(J)$ and $c_s=\sqrt{p'}$ be the enthalpy variable and sound speed of
[[def-gr-barotropic-enthalpy-variable]], and let $D,\vartheta,a^b,h^{ab}$
denote the comoving derivative, expansion, acceleration and rest-space
projection of [[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]. Then:

**(a)** the perfect-fluid equations
$D\epsilon+(\epsilon+p)\vartheta=0$, $(\epsilon+p)a^b+h^{ba}\partial_ap=0$ are
equivalent to
$$D r+c_s\,\vartheta=0,\qquad D n^b+c_s\,h^{ba}\partial_a r=0 ,$$
and the stress-energy tensor
$T^{ab}=(\epsilon+p)n^an^b+pg^{ab}$ is divergence-free exactly when these
equations hold;

**(b)** in every orthonormal frame $(n,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ at a point, the principal
symbol of the system (a) in the variables $(r,n^1,n^2,n^3)$ at a covector
$\zeta=\zeta_0n^\flat+\zeta_\perp$ is the symmetric matrix
$$A(\zeta)=\begin{pmatrix}\zeta_0&c_s\zeta_\perp^{\mathsf T}\\ c_s\zeta_\perp&\zeta_0 I_3\end{pmatrix};$$
its eigenvalues are $\zeta_0$ (multiplicity two) and
$\zeta_0\pm c_s|\zeta_\perp|$ (multiplicity one each); consequently $A(\zeta)$
is positive definite for every future-directed timelike covector $\zeta$
(because $\zeta_0>|\zeta_\perp|$ and $c_s<1$);

**(c)** consequently the combined Einstein-fluid system, with the reduced
Einstein equation in the harmonic gauge, is a first-order quasilinear symmetric
hyperbolic system with positive definite time matrix, coupled only through
zeroth-order terms in the first derivatives of the metric.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$ and let $U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open
matter domain ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[prop-an-open-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold-has-a-canonical-restricted-smooth-structure]]).

**(a) Dust.** Let $(\rho,u,T)$ be a dust model on $U$
([[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]). Then

$$\nabla^aT_{ab}=0\ \text{on }U\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad \nabla_a(\rho u^a)=0\ \text{and}\ u^a\nabla_au^b=0\ \text{on }U .$$

**(b) Perfect fluid.** Let $(\varepsilon,p,n,T)$ be a perfect-fluid model on
$U$ with comoving derivative $D$, expansion $\vartheta$, acceleration $a$ and
projection $h$ ([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]). Then

$$\nabla^aT_{ab}=0\ \text{on }U\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad D\varepsilon+(\varepsilon+p)\vartheta=0\quad\text{and}\quad (\varepsilon+p)a^b+h^{ba}\partial_ap=0\ \text{on }U .$$

Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold, let $h$ be a smooth Riemannian metric
and $K$ a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor on $\Sigma$
([[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]]). Let a **matter sector** be
specified as follows: a finite list of tensor fields $\psi$ on a spacetime
carrying $\Sigma$, a smooth stress-energy construction $T(g,\psi)$ and a system
of equations $E(g,\psi)=0$ such that, in every chart, the combined system for
$(\psi,g)$ with the metric variables of
[[lem-gr-reduced-einstein-principal-part]] clause (b) attached is a first-order
quasilinear symmetric hyperbolic system coupled only through zeroth-order terms
in the first derivatives of the metric, and such that $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ is a
consequence of $E(g,\psi)=0$ on-shell. Suppose smooth initial data $\psi_0$ on
$\Sigma$ are given so that the constraint equations
$$S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa\,T(n,n),\qquad \operatorname{div}_hK(Y)-\nabla^h_Y\operatorname{tr}_hK=\kappa\,T(n,Y)$$
hold on $\Sigma$ for the normal vector $n$ and the stress tensor determined by
$(h,K,\psi_0)$ ([[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]]). Then:

**(a)** every $p\in\Sigma$ has an open neighborhood $O_p$ in $\Sigma$ such that
there are an open neighborhood $W_p$ of $O_p$ in a smooth four-manifold, a smooth
Lorentzian metric $g$ and matter fields $\psi$ on $W_p$ solving the field
equations $G+\Lambda g=\kappa T(g,\psi)$ and the matter equations, with
$O_p$ a spacelike embedded hypersurface of induced metric $h$ and second
fundamental form $K$;

**(b)** the local solutions of (a) glue: over a neighborhood $W$ of $\Sigma$
there are $g,\psi$ solving the equations, with $\Sigma$ spacelike of data
$(h,K)$, and $\Sigma$ lies in the interior of its domain of dependence in $W$,
so that $D(\Sigma)\cap W$ is an open globally hyperbolic neighborhood of
$\Sigma$ with $\Sigma$ as a Cauchy hypersurface and $(g,\psi)$ restricts to a
globally hyperbolic development of the data;

**(c)** any two developments as in (a)--(b) of the same data are related near
$\Sigma$ by a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving isometry
([[thm-gr-local-geometric-uniqueness]]).

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a spacelike embedded hypersurface with induced metric
$h$, future unit normal field $n$ and second fundamental form
$K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]],
[[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]). Let
$s$ be a smooth function defined near $\Sigma$ with $s=0$ exactly on $\Sigma$
and $ds(n)=1$ (a normal time coordinate), and let $h_0$ be a smooth metric on a
product neighborhood of $\Sigma$ with $h_0|_{\Sigma}=h$ and
$\partial_sh_0=0$. Put $\bar g:=-ds^2+h_0$ as background metric. Define a smooth
metric germ $g_0$ on $\Sigma$ by the initial jet
$$g_{ij}=h_{ij},\qquad g_{00}=-1,\qquad g_{0i}=0,\qquad \partial_sg_{ij}=2K_{ij},\qquad \partial_sg_{0i}=0,\qquad \partial_sg_{00}=-2\operatorname{tr}_hK .$$
Then:

**(a)** $g_0$ is the germ of a smooth Lorentzian metric for which $\Sigma$ is
spacelike with induced metric $h$, future unit normal $n=\partial_s$ and second
fundamental form $K$;

**(b)** the harmonic-gauge vector of $(g_0,\bar g)$ vanishes on $\Sigma$:
$H^a|_\Sigma=0$.

derivations.claim: (Hypotheses.) By [L1] the fluid sector has a first-order quasilinear symmetric hyperbolic reduction with zeroth-order metric coupling; by [L2] its stress tensor is on-shell divergence-free.

(Application.) Applying [L3] to the matter sector described by [L1]--[L2] and to the data $(\Sigma,h,K_2)$ with matter data $(\epsilon_0,n_0)$, whose jet is fixed by [L4], gives the asserted local development, the causal statements and the uniqueness up to a data-fixing isometry.

citations.quote:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
signature $(-+++)$ and metric-selected connection $\nabla$, and let $(\rho,u)$
be a dust model on an open matter domain $U_0\subseteq M$
([[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]), so $\rho>0$ is the rest density,
$u$ is the future-directed unit timelike four-velocity and
$T^{ab}=\rho u^au^b$. Fix a constant $c>0$ (the speed of light of the
framework, [[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]) and make the following
**reduction conventions**, all local to an open set $U\subseteq U_0$:

**(a) Signature flip.** Put $\gamma:=-g$, a smooth metric of signature
$(+---)$ on $U$, with inverse $\gamma^{-1}=-g^{-1}$; all indices in the
reduction are raised and lowered with $\gamma$
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]). Put
$$U:=u,\qquad r:=\rho c^2 .$$
Then $\gamma(U,U)=1$, and the Einstein equation of the framework reads
$G(\gamma)-\Lambda\gamma=\kappa\,r\,U^\flat_\gamma\otimes U^\flat_\gamma$ with
the same constant $\kappa$ and the Einstein tensor of $\gamma$
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). The original metric and
frame connection are recovered by the constant signs $g=-\gamma$; no physical
equation is changed.

**(b) Orthonormal frame.** Choose a smooth orthonormal frame
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ on $U$ with $e_0=U$ and
$\gamma(e_i,e_j)=\eta_{ij}:=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1)_{ij}$
([[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]], [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]).
Its connection coefficients are defined by
$$\nabla_ie_j=\Gamma_i{}^k{}_j\,e_k,\qquad \Gamma_{ijk}:=\gamma_{kl}\Gamma_i{}^l{}_j=-\Gamma_{ikj},$$
and the frame components of $U$ are $U^i=\delta^i_0$.
The **spatial projection** onto the $\gamma$-orthogonal complement of $U$ and the tensor
$$h_{ij}:=\gamma_{ij}-U_iU_j,\qquad l_{ij}:=h_{ij}-U_iU_j$$
coincide with $\gamma$-orthogonal projection onto $\operatorname{span}(e_1,e_2,e_3)$
when restricted to spatial pairs.

**(c) Kinematics.** With $\nabla$ the metric connection of $\gamma$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) put
$$\chi_{ij}:=h_i{}^k\nabla_kU_j,\qquad \chi:=h^{ij}\chi_{ij},\qquad \chi^{ij}:=h^{ik}h^{jl}\chi_{kl},$$
and let $D$ denote fully projected covariant differentiation: for a spatial
tensor field $T$, $(DT)_{i\ldots}:=(h_i{}^j\cdots)\nabla_j(T_\ldots)$, so
$D_ih_{jk}=0$ and $D_i\epsilon_{jkl}=0$. Let $\epsilon_{ijkl}$ be the
$\gamma$-volume tensor with $\epsilon_{0123}=1$ and set
$\epsilon_{ijk}:=\epsilon_{0ijk}$ (so $\epsilon_{123}=1$).

**(d) Comoving-parallel gauge.** Assume the coordinates
$(x^0=s,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ on $U$ are **comoving** ($e_0=\partial_s$ and $x^\alpha$
constant along the flow lines of $e_0$, $s$ a parameter on them) and
**parallel** ($\Gamma_0{}^i{}_j=0$, i.e. the spatial frame is parallelly
transported along $U$). This gauge is admissible for tilted configurations: the
initial surface $s=0$ is the given spacelike surface and need not be orthogonal
to $U$.

**(e) Unknowns.** The unknowns of the reduction are the coefficients
$$u_{\mathrm{red}}:=\bigl(e_a{}^\mu,\ \Gamma_a{}^i{}_j,\ E_{ij},\ B_{ij},\ r\bigr),\qquad a=1,2,3,$$
where $E$ and $B$ are the electric and magnetic parts of the Weyl curvature
defined in [[def-gr-dust-electric-magnetic-weyl-variables-and-schouten]]; the transport,
evolution and subsidiary equations they satisfy are stated and derived in
[[def-gr-dust-electric-magnetic-weyl-variables-and-schouten]],
[[lem-gr-dust-reduced-evolution-equations]],
[[lem-gr-dust-symmetric-hyperbolic-reduction]] and
[[thm-gr-dust-subsidiary-and-residual-vanishing]].

Work in the reduction conventions of
[[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]] with $q:=U(r)+r\chi=0$ (the
dust continuity equation in the comoving gauge) and let $E,B$ be the
electric-magnetic variables of
[[def-gr-dust-electric-magnetic-weyl-variables-and-schouten]]. Then:

**(a) [Weyl evolution]** the reduced Weyl equations are
$$0=P_{ij}=\mathcal L_UE_{ij}+D_kB_{l(i}\epsilon_{j)}{}^{kl}-3\chi_{(i}{}^lE_{j)l}-2\chi^l{}_{(i}E_{j)l}+h_{ij}\chi^{kl}E_{kl}+2\chi E_{ij}+\tfrac12\kappa r\bigl(\chi_{(ij)}-\tfrac13\chi h_{ij}\bigr),$$
$$0=Q_{ij}=\mathcal L_UB_{ij}-D_kE_{l(i}\epsilon_{j)}{}^{kl}-\chi^l{}_{(i}B_{j)l}-2\chi_{(i}{}^lB_{j)l}+\chi B_{ij}-\chi^{kl}B^{pq}\epsilon_{pk(i}\epsilon_{qlj)},$$
where $\mathcal L_U$ is the Lie derivative along $U$ and the bracket on the
indices $i,j$ has weight $\tfrac12$; they are obtained by projecting the
Bianchi identity of the prescribed curvature onto the symmetric tracefree
spatial parts, the density-derivative terms cancelling by $q=0$;

**(b) [trace preservation]** contracting (a) with $h^{ij}$ shows that
$h^{ij}E_{ij}$ and $h^{ij}B_{ij}$ satisfy homogeneous transport equations along
$U$; consequently zero initial traces remain zero, and the evolution may be
restricted to the five-dimensional tracefree space;

**(c) [transport equations]** with the parallel-comoving gauge one has
$$\partial_se_a{}^\mu=-\Gamma_a{}^j{}_0e_j{}^\mu,\qquad \partial_s\Gamma_a{}^i{}_j=R^{\mathrm{pre}\,i}{}_{j0a}-\Gamma_k{}^i{}_j\Gamma_a{}^k{}_0,\qquad \partial_sr=-r\chi,$$
the first two expressing zero time torsion and zero time-curvature residual, the
third the continuity equation; for tentative data the frame bracket is used in
the curvature definition so that these hold identically;

**(d) [symmetric hyperbolicity]** the system of (a) and (c), together with the
definition of the extrinsic curvature variables, is a first-order quasilinear
system for $(e_a{}^\mu,\Gamma_a{}^i{}_j,E_{ij},B_{ij},r)$ which is symmetric
hyperbolic on a spacelike initial surface: with the positive spatial Frobenius
product, the principal symmetric-tensor curl
$$(C(\xi)B)_{ij}=\epsilon_{kl(i}\xi^kB_{j)}{}^l$$
is skew-adjoint with operator norm at most $|\xi|$ ([[lem-gr-dust-symmetric-hyperbolic-reduction]]), so the coupled block
$\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&C(\xi)\\-C(\xi)&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ is
symmetric with the same bound, every other block is transport along $U$, and a
future-positive timelike conormal $\zeta$ (satisfying
$\zeta(U)>|\zeta_\perp|$) makes the total time matrix positive definite; in
particular the local well-posedness theorem for symmetric hyperbolic systems
applies to the reduced dust system.

Let $V$ be the real vector space of symmetric $3\times3$ matrices with the
positive Frobenius product $\langle B,B'\rangle=B^{ij}B'_{ij}$, and for
$\xi\in\mathbb R^3$ define
$$C(\xi):V\to V,\qquad (C(\xi)B)_{ij}=\epsilon_{kl(i}\xi^kB_{j)}{}^l ,$$
with indices raised and lowered by the Euclidean metric and $\epsilon$ the
Levi-Civita symbol on the spatial frame of
[[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]]. Then:

**(a)** $C(\xi)$ is skew-adjoint: $\langle C(\xi)B,B'\rangle=-\langle B,C(\xi)B'\rangle$;

**(b)** $\|C(\xi)\|\le|\xi|$ for the operator norm induced by the Frobenius
product;

**(c)** the block operator $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&C(\xi)\\-C(\xi)&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$
on $V\oplus V$ is symmetric (self-adjoint) with operator norm at most $|\xi|$;

**(d)** if $\zeta$ is a covector with $\zeta(U)=z$ and spatial part
$\zeta_\perp$, the symbol matrix
$\left(\begin{smallmatrix}zI&C(\zeta_\perp)\\-C(\zeta_\perp)&zI\end{smallmatrix}\right)$
is positive definite whenever $z>|\zeta_\perp|$, in particular for every
future-positive timelike conormal $\zeta$; hence the reduced dust system is
symmetric hyperbolic with positive time matrix on a spacelike initial surface.

Work in the reduction conventions of [[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]]
with an initial spacelike surface $\Sigma$ given by $s=0$, on which the dust
data consist of the induced metric $h$, the second fundamental form $K$ with
respect to the future unit normal $N$, and the prescribed future unit dust
velocity $U$ (tilted relative to $\Sigma$ in general). Then:

**(a) [curvature data]** in a normal-adapted tetrad $(N,e_i)$ the Gauss equation
fixes the six purely spatial components of the curvature from $(h,K)$, the
Codazzi equation fixes the eight mixed components (with their cyclic relation),
and the six spatial Ricci equations fix the symmetric part of $R_{0i0j}$; the
remaining four Ricci equations are the Hamiltonian and momentum constraints of
[[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]]. Transforming this full
algebraic curvature by the Lorentz basis change from the $N$-frame to the
$U$-frame determines the initial electric and magnetic parts $E_{ij}=C_{0i0j}$,
$B_{ij}=C^*{}_{0i0j}$ of the Weyl tensor uniquely;

**(b) [connection data]** the initial connection in the $U$-frame is
determined by the spatial Levi--Civita connection of $h$, the second fundamental
form $K$ and the spatial derivatives and frame components of $U$; its
$U$-component is fixed by the parallel gauge $\Gamma_0{}^i{}_j=0$. Since $U$ is
transverse to $\Sigma$, the tangential directions together with $U$ span the
tangent space, so these data determine all initial connection coefficients;

**(c) [vanishing initial residuals]** with the data of (a),(b) one has
$T^i{}_{jk}=0$ and $\Delta^i{}_{jkl}=0$ on $\Sigma$: the zero tangential torsion
and curvature residuals are the Gauss--Codazzi--Ricci data, the zero
$U$-components are the reduction identities, and the spatial Ricci equations
plus the constraints give the remaining components;

**(d) [tilted Bianchi initialization]** restricting
$D_\omega\Delta=-D_\omega R^{\mathrm{pre}}$ to three tangent slots of $\Sigma$
and using $\Delta|_\Sigma=0$, the dual Bianchi identity and
$q=q_a=0$, one obtains for the residual components of
[[thm-gr-dust-subsidiary-and-residual-vanishing]] clause (d), with a
future-positive timelike initial conormal $\zeta$, writing $z=\zeta(U)>0$ and
$v=\zeta_\perp$ in the $U$ rest frame,
$$zP+\tfrac12\,v\times Q=0,\qquad zQ-\tfrac12\,v\times P=0 ,$$
up to the fixed orientation signs; the combined $6\times6$ block is symmetric
with quadratic form at least $(z-\tfrac12|v|)(|P|^2+|Q|^2)$; since
$z>|v|$ for timelike $\zeta$, this forces $P=Q=0$ on $\Sigma$. No normal
derivatives of the constraints are assumed to vanish; the tilt of $\Sigma$
relative to $U$ is exactly what makes the conormal argument work.

Work in the reduction conventions of [[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]]
and with the zero quantities $z=(T,\Delta,F,q)$ of
[[def-gr-dust-torsion-and-curvature-residuals]]; assume the gauge conditions
$e_0=U$, $\Gamma_0{}^i{}_j=0$ and $q_k=0$ of that item and the reduced system of
[[lem-gr-dust-reduced-evolution-equations]], so that $P_{ij}=Q_{ij}=0$,
$T^0{}_{ab}=0=\Delta^i{}_{j0a}$ and the transport equations hold. Then:

**(a) [Cartan identities]** exterior differentiation of the structure equations
gives exactly $D_\omega\Theta^i=\Omega^i{}_j\wedge\theta^j$ and
$D_\omega\Omega^i{}_j=0$; and the algebraic Bianchi identity of the prescribed
curvature gives $R^{\mathrm{pre}}\wedge\theta=0$;

**(b) [reduction identities]** $\iota_U\Theta=0$ and $\iota_U\Delta=0$
identically; consequently the first Cartan identity gives a transport equation
for the spatial torsion, $e_0(\Theta^a{}_{ib})=N(z)$, and the spatial
derivatives of the vanishing time components may be dropped;

**(c) [commutator identity]** for a tensor field $A$,
$$(\nabla_i\nabla_j-\nabla_j\nabla_i)A=\Omega_{ij}\cdot A-\Theta_{ij}{}^p\nabla_pA,$$
where the second covariant derivative differentiates its lower derivative index
covariantly as well as every index of $A$; a literal commutator omitting the
derivative-slot terms has instead a frame-bracket term and is not this identity;

**(d) [F splitting]** with $P_i=F_{0i0}$ and
$Q_i=-\tfrac12\epsilon_i{}^{kl}F_{0kl}$ one has
$$F_{jkl}=2U_jP_{[k}U_{l]}+h_{j[k}P_{l]}+Q_i\bigl(U_j\epsilon^i{}_{kl}-\epsilon^i{}_{j[k}U_{l]}\bigr)-2P_{j[k}U_{l]}-Q_{ji}\epsilon^i{}_{kl}-\tfrac12\kappa\,h_{j[k}q_{l]}-\tfrac13\kappa\,q\,h_{j[k}U_{l]},$$
with $q=U(r)+r\chi$ and $q_l$ the spatial part of the zero vector; the four rest-frame components $F_{0a0},F_{0ab},F_{a0b},F_{abc}$ are recovered by $P,Q$, the symmetric tracefree evolution equations, the traces $q,q_a$ and the curvature cyclic/trace relations, so every Bianchi residual is represented;

**(e) [divergence identity]** the double divergence of the reconstructed Weyl part satisfies
$$\nabla^jF_{jkl}=-\Delta^p{}_{[i}{}^{i}{}_{j}C^{j]}{}_{pkl}+C^{ij}{}_{p[l}\Delta^p{}_{k]ij}+\tfrac12\Theta_i{}^p{}_j\nabla_pC^{ij}{}_{kl}+\Delta^p{}_{[l}{}^j{}_{k]}S_{pj}-\Delta^p{}_j{}^j{}_{[k}S_{l]p}+\nabla_pS^j{}_{[l}\Theta_{k]}{}^p{}_j,$$
every term of which contains an undifferentiated residual $\Theta$ or $\Delta$ times a smooth coefficient built from the reduced solution or its derivatives (in particular no untracked derivatives of residuals);

**(f) [closed subsidiary system]** the components (b), (d), (e) together with the identity $D_\omega\Delta=-D_\omega R^{\mathrm{pre}}$ expressed through $F$ and the conservation of the prescribed Schouten tensor form a closed linear homogeneous first-order system in $(\Theta,\Delta,P,Q)$ with smooth locally bounded coefficients: the spatial torsion and the spatial curvature residual satisfy transport equations along $U$, the pair $(P,Q)$ satisfies the symmetric-hyperbolic curl pair
$$0=\mathcal L_UP_k+\tfrac12\epsilon_k{}^{ij}D_iQ_j+N(z),\qquad 0=\mathcal L_UQ_k-\tfrac12\epsilon_k{}^{ij}D_iP_j+N(z),$$
with curl speed at most $\tfrac12$ and transport speed zero, and its time matrix is positive definite on the spacelike initial surface; hence by the energy uniqueness of the local well-posedness theorem the residuals vanish from zero initial data: if $z=0$ on a spacelike surface and the constraints hold there, then $z=0$ on the domain of determination;

**(g) [conclusion]** zero residuals imply that the tentative connection is torsion-free and metric-compatible, hence Levi--Civita; that the reconstructed curvature is the actual curvature, with Ricci trace the prescribed Einstein Ricci and all remaining Bianchi constraints satisfied; hence the metric solves the full Einstein-dust field equation.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, let
$K\subseteq\operatorname{int}K'\subseteq O$ be compact, let $R\ge0$, and let
$T>0$ and $C$ be as in [[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-existence]] for
the class $\mathcal S(K,R)$; for every datum $u_0\in\mathcal S(K,R)$ let $u$ be
the solution produced there on $(-T,T)$ with values in $K'$. Then:

**(a) [local existence]** For every $u_0\in\mathcal S(K,R)$ and every
$x_0\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ the solution $u$ is $C^1$ on a neighborhood of
$(0,x_0)$ in $(-T,T)\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ and solves $(\star)$ pointwise
there.

**(b) [finite speed / independence of the extension]** Let $\lambda_0>0$ be
determined by the coefficient bounds on a compact set containing the values of
the solutions in the following sense: for a truncated cone
$$D:=\{(t,x):0\le t\le t_0,\ d(x,x_0)\le\lambda(t_0-t)\}$$
with $t_0<T$, $\lambda\ge\lambda_0$, lying in a single chart of $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$
in which the coordinate representation of $A^\mu$ satisfies
$\lambda\,A^0+\xi_iA^i\ge0$ for all unit $\xi$ (which holds for $\lambda$ large
enough by clause (a) of [[lem-gr-finite-speed-independence-of-extension]]),
let $u,v$ be solutions of two periodic symmetric hyperbolic systems whose
coefficient families agree on an open neighbourhood of $D$, with
$u(0,\cdot)=v(0,\cdot)$ on the ball $\{d(x,x_0)\le\lambda t_0\}$. Then
$u=v$ on $D$.

**(c) [local uniqueness and stability]** If two classical solutions of the same
system on a common interval have values in $K$, $H^s$ norms at most $R$ and the
same initial value, they coincide; and the continuous-dependence estimate of
[[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-uniqueness-stability]] clause (b) holds
for the solutions of clause (a).

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$
([[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]]) and let $K\subseteq O$ be
compact, and let $K'\subseteq O$ be compact with $K$ contained in the
interior of $K'$. Then for every $R\ge0$ there are a time $T>0$ and a constant
$C$ (depending on $A^\mu,B,K,K',s$ and on $R$) such that:

for every $u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ taking values in $K$ with
$\|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R$ there is a Sobolev solution
$u:(-T,T)\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ of $(\star)$ with
$u(0)=u_0$ which is classical and satisfies
$$u\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^s)\cap C^0((-T,T);H^{s-1}),\quad \partial_tu\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^{s-1}),$$
$$\sup_{|t|<T}\|u(t)\|_{H^s}\le C(1+R),\qquad \sup_{|t|<T}\|\partial_tu(t)\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C(1+R),$$
and whose values lie in $K'$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, let
$K\subseteq\operatorname{int}K'\subseteq O$ be compact, let $R\ge0$, and let
$T>0$ and $C$ be as in [[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-existence]] for
the data class $\mathcal S(K,R)$. Let $u_0\in C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$
take values in $K$. Then the solution $u\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^s)\cap C^0H^{s-1}$
of that theorem with $u(0)=u_0$ satisfies $u\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^m)$ and
$\partial_tu\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^{m-1})$ for every $m\ge s$, with bounds
depending only on $m$, $T$, the coefficient family, $K'$ and the $H^j$ bounds
of $u_0$ for $j\le m$; consequently $u\in C^\infty((-T,T)\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi})$
and solves $(\star)$ classically.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, let
$K\subseteq O$ be compact and $R\ge0$.

**(a) Uniqueness.** Let $J\ni0$ be an open interval and let
$u,v:J\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ be classical solutions of
$(\star)$ in the sense of clause (d) of
[[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]], both taking values in $K$ and
satisfying $\sup_{t\in J}\|u(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$, $\sup_{t\in J}\|v(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$.
If $u(0)=v(0)$, then $u=v$ on $J$.

**(b) Continuous dependence.** Let $K'\subseteq O$ be compact with
$K\subseteq\operatorname{int}K'$ and let $T>0$ be a time for which the existence
theorem [[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-existence]] produces solutions
from every datum with values in $K$ and norm at most $R$, with values in $K'$
and the bounds $C(1+R)$ of that theorem. Then for all such data $u_0,v_0$ with
solutions $u,v$
$$\|u(t)-v(t)\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C'\,e^{C'|t|}\,\|u_0-v_0\|_{H^{s-1}}\qquad(|t|<T),$$
with $C'=C'(A^\mu,B,K',R,s)$.

Work in the reduction conventions of
[[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]] with $q:=U(r)+r\chi=0$ (the
dust continuity equation in the comoving gauge) and let $E,B$ be the
electric-magnetic variables of
[[def-gr-dust-electric-magnetic-weyl-variables-and-schouten]]. Then:

**(a) [Weyl evolution]** the reduced Weyl equations are
$$0=P_{ij}=\mathcal L_UE_{ij}+D_kB_{l(i}\epsilon_{j)}{}^{kl}-3\chi_{(i}{}^lE_{j)l}-2\chi^l{}_{(i}E_{j)l}+h_{ij}\chi^{kl}E_{kl}+2\chi E_{ij}+\tfrac12\kappa r\bigl(\chi_{(ij)}-\tfrac13\chi h_{ij}\bigr),$$
$$0=Q_{ij}=\mathcal L_UB_{ij}-D_kE_{l(i}\epsilon_{j)}{}^{kl}-\chi^l{}_{(i}B_{j)l}-2\chi_{(i}{}^lB_{j)l}+\chi B_{ij}-\chi^{kl}B^{pq}\epsilon_{pk(i}\epsilon_{qlj)},$$
where $\mathcal L_U$ is the Lie derivative along $U$ and the bracket on the
indices $i,j$ has weight $\tfrac12$; they are obtained by projecting the
Bianchi identity of the prescribed curvature onto the symmetric tracefree
spatial parts, the density-derivative terms cancelling by $q=0$;

**(b) [trace preservation]** contracting (a) with $h^{ij}$ shows that
$h^{ij}E_{ij}$ and $h^{ij}B_{ij}$ satisfy homogeneous transport equations along
$U$; consequently zero initial traces remain zero, and the evolution may be
restricted to the five-dimensional tracefree space;

**(c) [transport equations]** with the parallel-comoving gauge one has
$$\partial_se_a{}^\mu=-\Gamma_a{}^j{}_0e_j{}^\mu,\qquad \partial_s\Gamma_a{}^i{}_j=R^{\mathrm{pre}\,i}{}_{j0a}-\Gamma_k{}^i{}_j\Gamma_a{}^k{}_0,\qquad \partial_sr=-r\chi,$$
the first two expressing zero time torsion and zero time-curvature residual, the
third the continuity equation; for tentative data the frame bracket is used in
the curvature definition so that these hold identically;

**(d) [symmetric hyperbolicity]** the system of (a) and (c), together with the
definition of the extrinsic curvature variables, is a first-order quasilinear
system for $(e_a{}^\mu,\Gamma_a{}^i{}_j,E_{ij},B_{ij},r)$ which is symmetric
hyperbolic on a spacelike initial surface: with the positive spatial Frobenius
product, the principal symmetric-tensor curl
$$(C(\xi)B)_{ij}=\epsilon_{kl(i}\xi^kB_{j)}{}^l$$
is skew-adjoint with operator norm at most $|\xi|$ ([[lem-gr-dust-symmetric-hyperbolic-reduction]]), so the coupled block
$\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&C(\xi)\\-C(\xi)&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ is
symmetric with the same bound, every other block is transport along $U$, and a
future-positive timelike conormal $\zeta$ (satisfying
$\zeta(U)>|\zeta_\perp|$) makes the total time matrix positive definite; in
particular the local well-posedness theorem for symmetric hyperbolic systems
applies to the reduced dust system.

Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold, let $h$ be a smooth Riemannian metric
and $K$ a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor on $\Sigma$
([[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]]). Let a **matter sector** be

**(a)** every $p\in\Sigma$ has an open neighborhood $O_p$ in $\Sigma$ such that

Lorentzian metric $g$ and matter fields $\psi$ on $W_p$ solving the field

$(h,K)$, and $\Sigma$ lies in the interior of its domain of dependence in $W$,

**(c)** any two developments as in (a)--(b) of the same data are related near

([[thm-gr-local-geometric-uniqueness]]).

Work in the reduction conventions of [[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]]
and with the zero quantities $z=(T,\Delta,F,q)$ of
[[def-gr-dust-torsion-and-curvature-residuals]]; assume the gauge conditions
$e_0=U$, $\Gamma_0{}^i{}_j=0$ and $q_k=0$ of that item and the reduced system of
[[lem-gr-dust-reduced-evolution-equations]], so that $P_{ij}=Q_{ij}=0$,
$T^0{}_{ab}=0=\Delta^i{}_{j0a}$ and the transport equations hold. Then:

**(a) [Cartan identities]** exterior differentiation of the structure equations
gives exactly $D_\omega\Theta^i=\Omega^i{}_j\wedge\theta^j$ and
$D_\omega\Omega^i{}_j=0$; and the algebraic Bianchi identity of the prescribed
curvature gives $R^{\mathrm{pre}}\wedge\theta=0$;

**(b) [reduction identities]** $\iota_U\Theta=0$ and $\iota_U\Delta=0$
identically; consequently the first Cartan identity gives a transport equation
for the spatial torsion, $e_0(\Theta^a{}_{ib})=N(z)$, and the spatial
derivatives of the vanishing time components may be dropped;

**(c) [commutator identity]** for a tensor field $A$,
$$(\nabla_i\nabla_j-\nabla_j\nabla_i)A=\Omega_{ij}\cdot A-\Theta_{ij}{}^p\nabla_pA,$$
where the second covariant derivative differentiates its lower derivative index
covariantly as well as every index of $A$; a literal commutator omitting the
derivative-slot terms has instead a frame-bracket term and is not this identity;

**(d) [F splitting]** with $P_i=F_{0i0}$ and
$Q_i=-\tfrac12\epsilon_i{}^{kl}F_{0kl}$ one has
$$F_{jkl}=2U_jP_{[k}U_{l]}+h_{j[k}P_{l]}+Q_i\bigl(U_j\epsilon^i{}_{kl}-\epsilon^i{}_{j[k}U_{l]}\bigr)-2P_{j[k}U_{l]}-Q_{ji}\epsilon^i{}_{kl}-\tfrac12\kappa\,h_{j[k}q_{l]}-\tfrac13\kappa\,q\,h_{j[k}U_{l]},$$
with $q=U(r)+r\chi$ and $q_l$ the spatial part of the zero vector; the four rest-frame components $F_{0a0},F_{0ab},F_{a0b},F_{abc}$ are recovered by $P,Q$, the symmetric tracefree evolution equations, the traces $q,q_a$ and the curvature cyclic/trace relations, so every Bianchi residual is represented;

**(e) [divergence identity]** the double divergence of the reconstructed Weyl part satisfies
$$\nabla^jF_{jkl}=-\Delta^p{}_{[i}{}^{i}{}_{j}C^{j]}{}_{pkl}+C^{ij}{}_{p[l}\Delta^p{}_{k]ij}+\tfrac12\Theta_i{}^p{}_j\nabla_pC^{ij}{}_{kl}+\Delta^p{}_{[l}{}^j{}_{k]}S_{pj}-\Delta^p{}_j{}^j{}_{[k}S_{l]p}+\nabla_pS^j{}_{[l}\Theta_{k]}{}^p{}_j,$$
every term of which contains an undifferentiated residual $\Theta$ or $\Delta$ times a smooth coefficient built from the reduced solution or its derivatives (in particular no untracked derivatives of residuals);

**(f) [closed subsidiary system]** the components (b), (d), (e) together with the identity $D_\omega\Delta=-D_\omega R^{\mathrm{pre}}$ expressed through $F$ and the conservation of the prescribed Schouten tensor form a closed linear homogeneous first-order system in $(\Theta,\Delta,P,Q)$ with smooth locally bounded coefficients: the spatial torsion and the spatial curvature residual satisfy transport equations along $U$, the pair $(P,Q)$ satisfies the symmetric-hyperbolic curl pair
$$0=\mathcal L_UP_k+\tfrac12\epsilon_k{}^{ij}D_iQ_j+N(z),\qquad 0=\mathcal L_UQ_k-\tfrac12\epsilon_k{}^{ij}D_iP_j+N(z),$$
with curl speed at most $\tfrac12$ and transport speed zero, and its time matrix is positive definite on the spacelike initial surface; hence by the energy uniqueness of the local well-posedness theorem the residuals vanish from zero initial data: if $z=0$ on a spacelike surface and the constraints hold there, then $z=0$ on the domain of determination;

**(g) [conclusion]** zero residuals imply that the tentative connection is torsion-free and metric-compatible, hence Levi--Civita; that the reconstructed curvature is the actual curvature, with Ricci trace the prescribed Einstein Ricci and all remaining Bianchi constraints satisfied; hence the metric solves the full Einstein-dust field equation.

derivations.claim: (Setup and initial data.) Choose coordinates, the initial surface $s=0$ and the reduction gauge as in [[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]]; the tilt of $U_0$ relative to $\Sigma$ is allowed because the gauge is comoving, not normal. By [[lem-gr-dust-initial-data-and-tilted-initialization]] the initial curvature and connection data are determined by $(h,K,U_0)$, all initial residuals vanish, and the spatial Bianchi residuals also vanish by the tilted conormal argument. The density enters only through $r_0=\rho_0c^2$, including the value zero.

(Well-posedness of the reduced system.) By [L1]--[L2] the reduced system is a first-order quasilinear symmetric hyperbolic system in the variables of the reduction, with coefficients smooth in the variables and the initial data determined by the constrained data; [L3] gives a smooth solution on a neighborhood of $\Sigma$ with the stated regularity, and the density component satisfies the transport equation with the explicit positive solution of [L4].

(Recovering the full system and uniqueness.) By the residual-vanishing theorem [L2] the zero quantities vanish on the domain of determination, so the solution of the reduced system satisfies the full Einstein-dust system with the prescribed velocity and density; the causal statements follow as in [[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]], and the uniqueness up to a data-fixing isometry is [L5].

Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and
let $(\varphi,V,K)$ be the scalar-field matter model with scalar equation
$\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0$ and candidate stress-energy tensor
$T_{ab}=K[\partial_a\varphi\,\partial_b\varphi-g_{ab}(\tfrac12\partial^c\varphi\,\partial_c\varphi+V(\varphi))]$
([[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]]). Fix a chart and the background
$\bar g,\bar\nabla$ of [[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]. Then
the system consisting of the reduced Einstein equation with this $T$ and the
scalar equation, together with the definition of the auxiliary variables
$$u:=\bigl(g_{ab},\bar\nabla_0g_{ab},\bar\nabla_ig_{ab},\ \varphi,\ \varphi_0:=\bar\nabla_0\varphi,\ \varphi_i:=\bar\nabla_i\varphi\bigr)$$
is, on every region where the metric is Lorentzian and the chart is initially
orthogonal, a first-order quasilinear symmetric hyperbolic system whose time
matrix is block diagonal with positive definite blocks: the metric block
$\operatorname{diag}(I,-g^{00}I,g^{ij}I)$ of
[[lem-gr-reduced-einstein-principal-part]] clause (b) and, for the scalar
variables, a positive definite block built from $1$ and $-g^{00}$; the coupling
between the metric and scalar blocks is only through zeroth-order terms in the
first derivatives of $g$. Moreover the stress-energy tensor is on-shell
divergence-free: $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ whenever $\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0$
([[prop-gr-scalar-field-stress-energy-conservation]]).

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a spacelike embedded hypersurface with induced metric
$h$, future unit normal field $n$ and second fundamental form
$K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]],
[[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]). Let
$s$ be a smooth function defined near $\Sigma$ with $s=0$ exactly on $\Sigma$
and $ds(n)=1$ (a normal time coordinate), and let $h_0$ be a smooth metric on a
product neighborhood of $\Sigma$ with $h_0|_{\Sigma}=h$ and
$\partial_sh_0=0$. Put $\bar g:=-ds^2+h_0$ as background metric. Define a smooth
metric germ $g_0$ on $\Sigma$ by the initial jet
$$g_{ij}=h_{ij},\qquad g_{00}=-1,\qquad g_{0i}=0,\qquad \partial_sg_{ij}=2K_{ij},\qquad \partial_sg_{0i}=0,\qquad \partial_sg_{00}=-2\operatorname{tr}_hK .$$

**(a)** $g_0$ is the germ of a smooth Lorentzian metric for which $\Sigma$ is
spacelike with induced metric $h$, future unit normal $n=\partial_s$ and second
fundamental form $K$;

**(b)** the harmonic-gauge vector of $(g_0,\bar g)$ vanishes on $\Sigma$:
$H^a|_\Sigma=0$.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold carrying a chart $(x^0=t,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ whose
domain $U$ contains the slice $\Sigma:=\{t=0\}$, let $\bar g$ be a smooth
background metric on $U$ with its Levi--Civita connection $\bar\nabla$, and let
$T$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor on $U$ together with the
background-covariant derivatives needed below (the matter field data). Suppose
smooth functions $g^0_{ab},g^1_{ab}$ on $\Sigma\cap U$ are given such that:

1. $g^0_{ab}$ are the components of a smooth Lorentzian metric on
   $\Sigma\cap U$ with $g^{00}_0<0$ and positive definite spatial block
   $(g_0^{ij})$;
2. $g^1_{ab}$ is symmetric and agrees on $\Sigma$ with the components of
   $\bar\nabla_0g_{ab}$ for some smooth extension $g$ of $g^0$ to $U$;
3. the harmonic-gauge condition $H^a=0$ holds on $\Sigma\cap U$ for the pair
   $(g,\bar g)$ ([[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]).

Then there is an open neighborhood $V\subseteq U$ of $\Sigma\cap U$ and a smooth
metric $g$ on $V$ with $g|_{\Sigma\cap U}=g^0$ and
$\bar\nabla_0g_{ab}|_{\Sigma\cap U}=g^1_{ab}$, solving the **reduced Einstein
equation** with the given background $\bar g$ and matter tensor $T$
([[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]) on $V$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a smooth spacelike hypersurface
([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]) with future unit normal
field $\mathfrak n$ and tangential frame $(e_i)$
([[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]), and let
$U$ be an open neighborhood of $\Sigma$ carrying a smooth background metric
$\bar g$ and a smooth symmetric tensor $T$ with $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $U$. Let
$H$ and $E$ be the gauge vector and Einstein residual of
[[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]. Suppose:

1. $(g,T)$ solves the reduced Einstein equation on $U$;
2. $H=0$ on $\Sigma$;
3. the constraint residuals vanish on $\Sigma$: $E(\mathfrak n,\mathfrak n)=0$
   and $E(\mathfrak n,e_i)=0$ for all $i$.

Then there is an open neighborhood $W\subseteq U$ of $\Sigma$ on which $H=0$ and
$E=0$; consequently $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$ on $W$, so $g$ solves
the Einstein equation with the prescribed matter tensor there.

carrying $\Sigma$, a smooth stress-energy construction $T(g,\psi)$ and a system
of equations $E(g,\psi)=0$ such that, in every chart, the combined system for

hold on $\Sigma$ for the normal vector $n$ and the stress tensor determined by

Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold, let $h$ be a smooth Riemannian metric
on $\Sigma$, let $K$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor on $\Sigma$, and
let $\mathcal D$ be fixed smooth initial data for a symmetric $2$-tensor $T$ on
$\Sigma$ (its value and the value of its normal derivative in the models below).
Let $(M,g,N)$ and $(M',g',N')$ be two time-oriented smooth Lorentzian
four-manifolds with spacelike embeddings $j,j'$ of $\Sigma$ inducing the
same $(h,K)$, carrying smooth symmetric tensors $T,T'$ satisfying the field
equations
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab},\qquad G'_{ab}+\Lambda g'_{ab}=\kappa T'_{ab}$$
on neighborhoods of the images of $\Sigma$, with $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$,
$\nabla'^aT'_{ab}=0$ there and with equal initial data $\mathcal D$ for
$T,T'$ (transported by the embeddings).

Then there are open neighborhoods $U$ of $j(\Sigma)$ and $U'$ of
$j'(\Sigma)$ and a smooth diffeomorphism $\varphi:U\to U'$ such that:

1. $\varphi(j(\sigma))=j'(\sigma)$ for every $\sigma\in\Sigma$;
2. $\varphi^*(g')=g$ and $\varphi^*(T')=T$ on $U$;
3. $\varphi$ carries the time orientation of $N$ to that of $N'$.

Thus any two solutions of the field equation arising from the same constrained
geometric data are locally isometric near the initial surface by a
data-fixing time-orientation-preserving isometry. Here an **isometry fixing the
data** means a smooth diffeomorphism satisfying (2) (the definition is given
explicitly by these equations; no separate notion of Lorentzian isometry is
presupposed).

Let $(\varphi,V,K)$ be the scalar-field matter model of
[[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]] with smooth potential $V$, and let
$(\Sigma,h,K_2,\varphi_0,\pi_0)$ be smooth initial data: a smooth three-manifold
$\Sigma$ with Riemannian metric $h$, symmetric $2$-tensor $K_2$, and smooth
functions $\varphi_0,\pi_0$ on $\Sigma$ (the scalar value and its prescribed
normal derivative). Suppose the constraint equations of
[[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] hold on $\Sigma$, computed with
the scalar stress-energy tensor determined by $(h,K_2,\varphi_0,\pi_0)$ and the
chosen unit normal. Then the data admit a local development in the sense of
[[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]]: a smooth Lorentzian metric $g$ and
scalar field $\varphi$ near $\Sigma$ satisfying
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\,T_{ab},\qquad \Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0$$
with $T$ the scalar stress tensor, $\Sigma$ spacelike of induced metric $h$ and
second fundamental form $K_2$, and $\varphi|_\Sigma=\varphi_0$,
$\partial_n\varphi|_\Sigma=\pi_0$; and any two such developments of the same
data agree near $\Sigma$ up to a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving
isometry.

Let a perfect-fluid model have smooth equation of state $p=p(\epsilon)$ on an
open interval $J$ with $\epsilon+p>0$ and $0<p'(\epsilon)<1$
([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]). Let
$(\Sigma,h,K_2,\epsilon_0,n_0)$ be smooth initial data: a three-manifold
$\Sigma$ with Riemannian metric $h$, symmetric $2$-tensor $K_2$, a smooth
function $\epsilon_0:\Sigma\to J$ and a smooth future-directed unit timelike
vector field $n_0$ on $\Sigma$ (not required to be normal). Suppose the
constraint equations of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] hold on
$\Sigma$ with the stress-energy tensor computed from $(\epsilon_0,n_0)$. Then
the data admit a local development in the sense of
[[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]]: a smooth Lorentzian metric $g$, a
smooth function $\epsilon$ and a smooth future-directed unit timelike field $n$
near $\Sigma$ satisfying
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\bigl((\epsilon+p)n_an_b+p\,g_{ab}\bigr),\qquad D\epsilon+(\epsilon+p)\vartheta=0,\qquad (\epsilon+p)a^b+h^{ba}\partial_ap=0$$
with $p=p(\epsilon)$ and $D,\vartheta,a,h$ as in
[[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]], with $\Sigma$ spacelike of induced data
$(h,K_2)$ and matter data $(\epsilon_0,n_0)$; and any two developments of the
same data agree near $\Sigma$ up to a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving
isometry.

Let $(\Sigma,h,K,\rho_0,U_0)$ be smooth initial data for the dust model
([[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]): a smooth three-manifold $\Sigma$ with
Riemannian metric $h$, symmetric $2$-tensor $K$, a smooth rest density
$\rho_0\ge0$ on $\Sigma$ (zero on empty regions allowed) and a smooth
future-directed unit timelike vector field $U_0$ on $\Sigma$ (prescribed
independently, tilted relative to $\Sigma$ in general). Suppose the constraint
equations of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] hold on $\Sigma$
with the dust stress tensor determined by $(\rho_0,U_0)$ and the chosen normal.
Then there is a smooth local development: a smooth Lorentzian metric $g$, a
smooth function $\rho\ge0$ and a smooth future-directed unit timelike field $u$
solving
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\rho c^2\,u_au_b,\qquad \nabla_uu=0,\qquad u(\rho)+\rho\,\nabla\!\cdot u=0$$
near $\Sigma$, with $\Sigma$ spacelike of induced data $(h,K)$ and matter data
$(\rho_0,U_0)$; $\Sigma$ lies in the interior of the domain of dependence of the
solution region; the construction never divides by $\rho$, and every two such
developments of the same data agree near $\Sigma$ up to a data-fixing
time-orientation-preserving isometry. In particular the conclusions hold for
smooth data with $\rho_0\equiv0$ on open subsets (the velocity is then
separately prescribed there).

derivations.claim: (Vacuum branch.) The vacuum equations are the reduced equations with $T=0$; [[thm-gr-reduced-einstein-local-existence]] gives a smooth reduced solution from the initial jet, and [[thm-gr-harmonic-constraint-propagation]] turns it into a solution of the field equation because the constraints hold; the causal and uniqueness conclusions are those of [[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]].

(Matter branches.) Each branch theorem verifies the two hypotheses of the abstract development theorem (symmetric hyperbolicity with zeroth-order coupling, on-shell conservation) and applies it to the constrained data; the conclusions listed in the statement are exactly those of [L3]. [L2, L3] ∎
